Adani Power.summary:
The active houseViews on **Adani Power** have narrowed to a single note — **Asit C Mehta** (Accumulate, TP ₹680, May-2025) — now 14 months old. There is effectively no live cross-house debate in scope. The broader PDF library (outside the active houseViews) provides useful context: **Jefferies** carried Buy/TP ₹355 as of June 2026 (raised from ₹335, premised on 23% EBITDA CAGR through FY30E and 56% PPA lock-in on the 23.7 GW expansion pipeline), and **Morgan Stanley** issued OW/TP ₹275 in June 2026, describing APL as a "cash compounding machine" with a lower-risk-than-assumed growth profile. The divergence between Asit's ₹680 and institutional targets in the ₹255–₹355 range is stark and reflects either a more aggressive PPA tariff assumption or a model that has simply not been updated against current capacity-cost data.

My own read: **Adani Power** is a hard-to-ignore baseload story given India's structural power deficit and the group's credible track record of executing large thermal projects at scale — but it is equally hard to hold with conviction at stretched valuations. The equity is a long-duration growth option: FCF remains deeply negative until FY29-30E, meaning the entire thesis rests on the pace and tariff quality of PPA contracting on the ~44% of new capacity that is still uncontracted. Governance and regulatory risk are the perennial blind spot for sell-side coverage — APL has a history of tariff disputes, fuel cost disallowance battles, and related-party complexity that rarely surfaces in target-price arithmetic. I'd watch two things most closely: (1) whether the uncontracted new capacity gets tied into PPAs at tariffs consistent with management's EBITDA CAGR guidance, and (2) any signal from the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission on cost pass-through interpretations. The Jefferies and Morgan Stanley notes in the PDF library remain more credible guides to current institutional valuation than Asit's dated ₹680.

Asit|250521.change: No prior Asit C Mehta report in the library to compare. TP ₹680, Accumulate.
Asit|250521.view:
Asit C Mehta's May-2025 Accumulate at TP ₹680 is the only active houseView on Adani Power and is now 14 months old. The ₹680 target sits well above institutional coverage in the ₹255–₹355 range as of June 2026 — a gap more likely explained by a different base year, a higher terminal multiple, or model staleness than by superior insight.

The Accumulate rating (not a strong Buy) at what was probably a smaller premium to CMP in May 2025 is not a useful current signal. Treat this note as a thematic marker — the bull case on India's power deficit and APL's scale as the largest private thermal operator is directionally correct — but do not rely on the ₹680 level for sizing decisions without a fresh institutional cross-check.

AIA Engineering.summary:
Two houses appear in the active House Views panel. **ICICI Direct** (Buy, PT ₹5,285) upgraded AIA Engineering on 27-May-2026 results day — a sharp pivot from Hold at ₹4,035 just four months earlier (01-Feb-2026), lifting the target 31%. **Asit C Mehta** (Buy, PT ₹5,106, Sep-2024) is directionally aligned but ~21 months stale and carries limited current weight. For context, **Nomura** (not in the active panel) maintains a Reduce at PT ₹3,568 in the local library as of the same date (27-May-2026) — acknowledging a 21% EBITDA beat and 2% volume growth in 4QFY26 but holding the call unchanged. The target spread is ₹3,568–₹5,285, reflecting genuine disagreement on whether AIA's premium valuation is warranted when mining volumes still declined 4% y-y in the latest quarter despite the overall beat.

**My own read:** AIA occupies a genuinely defensible niche — high-chrome grinding media that demonstrably outperforms forged steel in wear rates for mining and cement customers. The conversion story is real and long-cycle; it is not a fad thesis. But the multiple tends to run ahead of earnings, and quarterly delivery is lumpy. Nomura's unchanged Reduce despite a large EBITDA beat is the more analytically honest position: it signals the bear case is about normalized earnings power and valuation, not one quarter. ICICI's rapid U-turn (Hold→Buy in four months, with no change in the structural narrative) reads more as momentum than fresh conviction. Two things I would watch most: (1) whether global copper and gold mining capex holds through H2 CY2026 — AIA's conversion pipeline depends on new-mine development not deferring grinding media decisions; (2) whether the 15% y-y cement volume growth in 4QFY26 proves durable as a structural offset to lumpy mining cycles, or whether it was a seasonally strong blip.

ICICI|260527.change: Upgraded to Buy from Hold; PT raised ₹4,035→₹5,285 (prior Trendlyne entry: Hold/₹4,035, 01-Feb-2026). No pdfdata match in local library — change derived from Trendlyne history.
ICICI|260527.view:
ICICI's upgrade is a sharp momentum pivot triggered by the 4QFY26 results beat. Less than four months after downgrading to Hold at ₹4,035, they moved to Buy/₹5,285 — a 31% PT hike. The speed of the reversal is the flag: the structural thesis (high-chrome conversion, long-cycle mining exposure) has not changed materially, so the upgrade is pricing the earnings beat and improved near-term momentum, not a revised fundamental view.

That is not necessarily wrong — a strong quarterly result can genuinely shift the risk-reward — but it makes the call highly dependent on the next two or three quarters sustaining the beat. If mining volumes slide back in FY27H1, a revisit seems likely. Without the full report in the local library, the assumptions behind the ₹5,285 PT cannot be independently checked. Treat as a useful sentiment signal rather than a deeply anchored conviction.

Asit|240905.change: Dated Sep-2024; no prior Asit entry in the library to compare. Only Asit note on record — TP ₹5,106, Buy rating.
Asit|240905.view:
This is a ~21-month-old note and should be weighted accordingly. The structural framing — high-chrome media conversion opportunity driven by mining and cement — remains the right long-term thesis and is the same narrative all current bulls are citing. But a great deal has evolved since Sep-2024: multiple quarterly cycles, ICICI's roundtrip from bullish → Hold → bullish again, and shifting global mining sentiment.

Asit's ₹5,106 PT coincidentally lands close to ICICI's current ₹5,285, but the convergence is coincidental — Asit has not updated. Treat this as historical context for the thesis framing; it has no current actionable weight.

Apollo Hospitals.summary:
**PL** (260522, Buy, TP ₹9,350) is the freshest voice, posting a strong Q4FY26 result note. **MO** (260211, Buy, TP ₹9,015) is five months older and pre-Q4 but directionally aligned. **Geojit** (251219, upgraded to Buy, TP ₹7,763) made an early call that proved correct but whose target is now well below the current stock level. The two ICICI-branded houses split in Nov-2025: **ICICI Securities** (251109) issued a cautious Hold ("soft quarter; bed addition critical") while **ICICI Direct** (251107) upgraded to Buy with TP ₹8,840 — a sibling-house disagreement resolved in favour of the bulls by Q4FY26's beat. There is no live bear in the current library; the debate is about degree and entry point, not direction. The PT cluster across the active bulls is ₹9,015–₹9,350; the dated Geojit and ICICI targets (₹7,763–₹8,840) have been outrun by the stock.

My own read: Apollo is the highest-quality way to own India's hospital structural story — an under-bedded market, rising insurance penetration, and a brand strong enough to push ARPOB through price and case-mix. Operating metrics (~68% occupancy, mature-hospital EBITDA margins above 25%, ROCE on a multi-year improvement path) are genuinely compelling. But I would surface what the sell-side underweights. **Valuation** is the primary risk: at ~27–33x EV/EBITDA the stock prices near-flawless execution, and incremental upside increasingly leans on the HealthCo demerger/listing crystallising value rather than just on hospital operations. **Regulatory price caps** (NPPA/CGHS) are the under-weighted tail — already trimmed oncology margins and could broaden, directly exposing the pricing-led margin expansion story. And the **~1,400-bed ramp** carries real execution risk in clinician hiring and payer onboarding that could keep new-unit losses elevated past guidance. Net: constructive on the franchise, cautious on the entry multiple. I would watch HealthCo listing progress and any widening of price-cap scope most closely.

PL|260522.change: Q4FY26 result update (260522), Buy, TP ₹9,350. Prior PL trendlyne entry 250814: Buy, TP ₹9,300 — PT nudged up ₹9,300→₹9,350; Buy maintained.
PL|260522.view: PL's "strong growth across segments" framing aligns with the broader post-Q4 consensus. The ₹50 PT lift is marginal — PL is confirming the thesis rather than making a new call. Adds weight to the bull book; does not reveal a distinct analytical angle.

MO|260211.change: Feb-2026 note (260211), Buy, TP ₹9,015. Prior MO trendlyne entry 260121 (Buy, TP ₹9,015) — PT and rating unchanged; note focuses on hospital optimisation and HealthCo traction driving a Q3 beat.
MO|260211.view: MO's Feb-2026 note is now five-plus months old and pre-dates Q4FY26. The hospital-optimisation and HealthCo-traction call was directionally right — Q4 validated both — but the TP of ₹9,015 sits below PL's post-result ₹9,350 and was almost certainly revised upward in subsequent notes not in this library. Treat as directionally valid; stale on the price target number.

Geojit|251219.change: Dec-2025: upgraded Accumulate→Buy (prior trendlyne entry: Geojit 250616, Accumulate, TP ₹7,757); PT essentially flat at ₹7,757→₹7,763. Target of ₹7,763 is now well below current stock levels.
Geojit|251219.view: Geojit made the right early-upgrade call, but the level is overtaken by events. At TP ₹7,763 (Dec-2025), the target has no live relevance to current positioning. Useful only as confirmation of the broad upgrade cycle Apollo went through in late-2025.

ICICI|251109.change: Nov-2025 note (251109), Hold, TP ₹8,080. No prior ICICI Securities entry in the trendlyne data — this is the only captured entry for this entity; cannot quantify the change vs prior.
ICICI|251109.view: The lone cautious voice in the current library — "soft quarter; bed addition critical to revive growth" was a reasonable read in Nov-2025 but has been challenged by Q4FY26's broad-based beat. The core concern, however, remains the right structural question: bed-addition execution is what drives the next growth leg, and that risk has not disappeared because one quarter was strong. The TP of ₹8,080 is stale. The analytical instinct is worth preserving even if the timing was off.

ICICI|251107.change: Nov-2025: upgraded to Buy (per trendlyne headline), TP ₹8,840. No prior ICICI Direct entry in the trendlyne data — prior rating before upgrade not available from this source.
ICICI|251107.view: Upgraded in the same week its sibling house ICICI Securities issued a Hold — an interesting internal split where ICICI Direct leaned constructive and proved the better near-term call. The TP of ₹8,840 is now stale relative to post-Q4 consensus. Useful as a historical marker of when broad-market sentiment turned positive; not an active price guide.

ASK Automotive.summary:
**BP Wealth** (Buy, PT ₹593, Dec-2025) is the only house in the active panel. The most substantive current note is **CLSA** (Outperform, PT ₹630, 20-May-2026 — in local library but not yet in houseViews), which provides the freshest and most analytically grounded read. Both are directionally bullish with a tight PT cluster of ₹593–₹630. CLSA's FY26 results note documents a ~2x revenue multiplier vs 2W production volume growth (23% revenue growth adjusted for the wheel-assembly divestiture, vs 12% 2W industry volume growth), implying real content-per-vehicle gains at key OEMs. The main unresolved debate: whether the 4QFY26 EBITDA margin dip to 11.6% (−138bps QoQ) is a transient new-product-ramp cost or the beginning of structural pricing pressure from OEMs.

**My own read:** ASK Automotive's consistent outperformance of 2W volumes is the core differentiator — if the ~2x revenue multiplier holds over a full cycle, the re-rating case is credible. The EV lightweighting angle (flagged by JM Financial in 2024) adds a plausible structural kicker, though 2W EV penetration remains modest and the timing of that uplift is uncertain. Two things I would probe that the current bullish coverage underweights: first, the wheel-assembly divestiture complicates the revenue comp, and I would want to verify how clean the adjusted 23% figure is before anchoring on it; second, the EBITDA margin trend needs watching — if OEM pricing discipline is compressing margins as ASK adds new product lines, the premium embedded in the current targets gets harder to sustain. With only one active house in the panel the stock is under-covered, which means negative surprises can reprice it sharply. I would watch FY27 EBITDA margin guidance at the next results, and any OEM programme wins or losses in the new product pipeline.

BPW|251201.change: Dated Dec-2025; no prior BP Wealth entry in the library to compare. TP ₹593, Buy rating.
BPW|251201.view:
BP Wealth's Dec 2025 note is now ~7 months old and predates CLSA's more current FY26 results update (May 2026). The headline format — "Shining Star Series BUY" — suggests a screener or thematic initiation rather than a deep-dive fundamental report, so the analytical depth behind the ₹593 PT is uncertain without the full text. Directionally it is aligned with CLSA (both bullish, PT cluster ₹593–₹630), and the underlying thesis is presumably the same content-per-vehicle and revenue-multiplier narrative.

Treat this as corroborating backdrop rather than an independently weight-bearing view. Its staleness and probable lighter format mean it adds limited incremental information relative to CLSA's more recent and evidenced note.

AWL Agri Business.summary:
Coverage here is thin: just two houses, both dated November 2025 and now ~8 months stale. **ICICI Securities** (Buy, PT ₹350) is the bull, citing foods-mix improvement and industry-level stability. **Deven Choksey** (Hold, PT ₹274) is more cautious, content to wait for a sustained H2 recovery before upgrading. Notably, ICICI quietly trimmed its PT from ₹360 to ₹350 on its prior update — the directional trend of their revisions (₹395→₹375→₹360→₹350) is a gradual de-rating even from the most bullish house. Choksey also nudged its PT up from ₹265 to ₹274 but held conviction flat. The TP spread (₹274–₹350) is wide relative to the number of brokers — 28% gap — and reflects a genuine disagreement about how fast the Foods segment can move the consolidated earnings needle.

My own read: AWL has the right strategic logic — Fortune is a genuine consumer brand with distribution reach most rivals cannot replicate, and moving into atta, ghee, and rice is a credible adjacency play. The problem is structural: roughly three-quarters of revenues will remain tied to palm oil commodity prices for years, which caps re-rating potential regardless of Foods segment progress. ICICI's ₹350 is hard to justify without Foods gross margins demonstrably expanding — revenue-mix shift alone does not create earnings quality. Choksey's Hold at ₹274 is the more grounded call at this stage. Both notes predate any 2026 operational data, so both targets should be held lightly. The one or two things I would watch: quarterly Foods revenue share and EBITDA margin progression, and the palm oil price cycle (which drives the bulk of revenues and therefore most of the near-term earnings volatility).

DC|251110.change: PT raised ₹265→₹274 (Trendlyne: prior entry 250717 Hold ₹265, current entry 251110 Hold ₹274); Hold maintained. No pdfdata match — trendlyne-sourced only.
DC|251110.view:
Deven Choksey's Hold with a small PT bump to ₹274 reads as cautious acknowledgment of sequential recovery without upgrade conviction. The headline — "festive demand to drive H2 rebound" — is standard seasonal commentary for a consumer-staples name. This note is now ~8 months old and predates any 2026 operational or strategy data.

The ₹274 PT sits well below ICICI's ₹350, making clear that DC assigns little premium to the Foods transformation story. The Hold is defensible: the edible-oil drag is structural, Foods margins are not yet visible in quarterly disclosures, and a festive-season bounce is an insufficient catalyst for a re-rating. Worth revisiting once Q2 or Q3 FY27 numbers are available.

ICICI|251106.change: PT trimmed ₹360→₹350 (Trendlyne: prior entry 250716 Buy ₹360, current entry 251106 Buy ₹350); Buy maintained. No pdfdata match — trendlyne-sourced only.
ICICI|251106.view:
ICICI Securities carries the most bullish PT at ₹350 — a 28% premium over Deven Choksey's Hold target. Their November 2025 note cites foods-mix improvement and industry strength as stabilising forces after prior quarters of volume and margin headwinds. The framing is constructive, but even as they held the Buy, the PT was quietly trimmed from ₹360.

The cumulative trajectory of ICICI's own revisions (₹395→₹375→₹360→₹350) tells a more cautious story than the maintained Buy rating. This note is now ~8 months stale and does not reflect any 2026 data. ₹350 is hard to justify without Foods gross margins moving visibly and sustainably higher; treat this as a directional upper-bound rather than a precise target, and discount it meaningfully until Foods margin data confirms the thesis.

Adani Enterprises.summary:
Only Jefferies covers Adani Enterprises in this library, and their current houseView (3 Jun 2026) is a conference day-1 takeaways note — not a standalone rated call. Their live Buy at ₹2,800 comes from the 2 Jun 2026 note, where both the TP and rating were held flat vs the prior report. There is no cross-house debate to map: no other broker is present in the library, and the 3 Jun note is descriptive rather than analytical, relaying panel themes around energy infrastructure and AI-driven power demand. The gap the library cannot fill is what the broader sell-side thinks — Jefferies' tone here is constructive but deliberately non-committal given the conference format.

My own read: AEL is best understood as a portfolio of early-to-mid-stage infrastructure incubations — airports, green hydrogen, roads, defense manufacturing, data centers — rather than a company with a clean, near-term earnings trajectory. The FY26 capex of ₹1.55tn is real and reflects genuine on-the-ground execution, but it also means the balance sheet is stretched and EBITDA visibility is limited across many sub-businesses. The post-Hindenburg stabilisation is real, but the group's USD debt load and reliance on ongoing capital market access remain structural vulnerabilities that the sell-side tends to underweight. The AI/power narrative sits more naturally with Adani Power and Adani Green than with AEL directly — AEL's edge is the incubation platform, not operating assets. Airports are the clearest near-term earnings driver; I'd watch concession EBITDA margins as greenfield capex ramps at newer airports. Fair value is genuinely hard to anchor: you are pricing optionality on India's infrastructure deficit with governance risk and conglomerate discount as the key unknowns. The stock rewards patience more than precision.

Jeff|260603.change: Conference takeaways note (3 Jun 2026); no TP or rating stated in this note. The latest rated Jefferies report (2 Jun 2026) maintained Buy at ₹2,800 — both TP and call unchanged vs their prior report (prevTP ₹2,800, prevCall Buy).
Jeff|260603.view:
The 3 Jun Jefferies note is a clean management-messaging recap from the Adani Group conference — useful for tracking what the group is emphasising (energy infra build-out, AI-led power demand, disciplined capex) but not a standalone investment thesis. The constructive framing is partly structural to the conference format, which naturally skews toward positives.

I'd treat the ₹2,800 Buy with measured scepticism: it is probably the right directional call if execution holds, but AEL's conglomerate structure makes that target harder to validate than a single-business stock — sum-of-the-parts analysis requires assumptions about listing timelines, holdco discounts, and capital recycling that can move the output substantially. The most useful thing to watch from Jefferies going forward: whether they update their airport EBITDA build (the clearest near-term earnings driver) and whether any report flags deterioration in holdco leverage metrics.

Adani Ports and SEZ.summary:
Three of four houses are bullish on ADSEZ: **Kotak** (ADD, FV ₹1,900, Jun-2026), **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, ₹1,900, Apr-2026), and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Buy, ₹1,777 — stale, Aug 2025). The lone dissenter is **BOB Capital Markets**, which downgraded from Buy to Hold in May 2026 and cut its PT from ₹1,960 to ₹1,820, citing a margin dip it called "transient" but backing the concern with a rating change. Bull targets cluster at ₹1,900 for the two freshest notes; PL's ₹1,777 is ~10 months stale and no longer informative on price. The TP spread among current notes is tight (₹1,820–₹1,900), reflecting broad consensus on fair value around ₹1,900. The real debate is whether BOB's margin concern — logistics-arm dilution of consolidated EBITDA — is genuinely transient or structural. Kotak's AR2026 balance-sheet analysis (the most granular piece in this batch) confirms the investment step-up is internally funded but does not directly address the margin trajectory.

My own read: ADSEZ's cargo franchise remains exceptional — 13 ports, Mundra as a deep-water hub, a live VLCC terminal, and consecutive months of double-digit volume growth. Kotak's finding that the capex acceleration is running at 3× the FY20-25 pace yet funded from operating cash flow rather than incremental debt is genuinely reassuring on balance-sheet quality. But two risks the consensus is glossing over: first, the **conglomerate discount** — any recurrence of Adani group-level stress (governance, credit, regulatory) sends the stock down irrespective of port fundamentals, and this tail risk is effectively unmodellable and consistently ignored by all houses. Second, **logistics margin dilution** is a real structural dynamic as non-port revenue mix grows; BOB is the only house in current coverage explicitly flagging it, and it deserves more credit than the herd gives it. I'd be comfortable at ₹1,900 but would not chase above that without evidence of EBITDA margin recovery. Key monitors: monthly cargo volumes for deceleration signals as comps get harder in 2H FY27, Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin, and any Adani group corporate news.

Kotak|260603.change: No prior Kotak report in the library to compare; ADD at Fair Value ₹1,900.
Kotak|260603.view:
Kotak's AR2026 analysis is the most substantive piece in this coverage batch. Digging into standalone balance-sheet data to confirm that the investment step-up (3× the FY20-25 annual pace) is funded from operating cash flow rather than incremental debt is a more rigorous check than the generic "capex ramp" narrative most other houses repeat without sourcing. The ADD at ₹1,900 is appropriately calibrated — the engine is accelerating but RoCE uplift is still ahead.

The framing "starting to show its colors" is honest rather than promotional. Most useful for the balance-sheet decomposition; it provides the best available evidence that the capex step-up is self-financing and therefore more sustainable than a debt-funded build.

BOB|260504.change: Downgraded Buy→Hold (per Trendlyne); PT cut ₹1,960→₹1,820 vs prior BOB note dated 260204.
BOB|260504.view:
BOB is the lone dissenter and provides the most useful counterweight in this coverage. A downgrade from Buy to Hold combined with a ₹140 PT cut signals the margin concern is not as transient as their own headline implies — if it were truly transient, the rating would more likely have stayed.

The margin pressure is most plausibly coming from the logistics arm: as non-port revenue scales, it dilutes consolidated EBITDA margin even as absolute EBITDA grows. BOB is the only house explicitly flagging this dynamic. Treat this note as the best available articulation of the bear case; if Q1 FY27 margins do not recover toward pre-dip levels, BOB's Hold will look more prescient than the consensus Buy.

MO|260430.change: PT raised ₹1,820→₹1,900 (Trendlyne: prior entry 260330 Buy ₹1,820, current entry 260430 Buy ₹1,900); Buy maintained.
MO|260430.view: Post Q4 FY26 result update after a beat — PT walked up ₹80 and Buy maintained. Motilal Oswal has been a consistent bull throughout this coverage run, steadily raising targets as results deliver. The note confirms earnings momentum but adds little incremental analytical depth beyond the headline beat. Useful as a consensus-confirming data point; not a thesis-setter.

PL|250805.change: Dated Aug 2025; no prior PL entry in the library to compare. This note is ~11 months old.
PL|250805.view: Stale Q1 FY26 result update at PT ₹1,777 — a level the stock has since traded well above. This note no longer carries any actionable signal. The more recent Kotak, BOB, and MO notes are far more informative on current valuation and thesis.

Sun Pharmaceuticals.summary:
The one genuinely split book here. **Bernstein** is the bull (Outperform, ₹2,235) on an under-appreciated US innovation franchise; **Kotak** is constructive (Add, raised to ₹1,960). Against them, **CLSA** (Hold, ₹2,020) and **Jefferies** are neutral, and **JPMorgan** is the bear, flagging a 4QFY26 EBITDA/PAT miss ~11-13% below consensus. The fault line is clean: optimism on the specialty re-rating versus caution on near-term earnings quality and US compliance/pricing. Tellingly, even the bulls disagree on magnitude — Kotak's ₹1,960 sits well below Bernstein's ₹2,235.

My own read: Sun's specialty pivot (Ilumya, Winlevi, Leqselvi, the SPARC NCEs) is the most credible branded-innovation transition in Indian pharma, and it genuinely lowers dependence on commoditised US generics — I buy the direction. The India branded franchise underneath is excellent: consistently growing ~2-3x the IPM, defensive and high-margin. Where I land closer to the bears: the swing factor for this stock has, for a decade, been **US FDA compliance at Halol** — and Halol/Baska are again pending reinspection. That single risk can gate the entire US franchise and is concrete in a way 'specialty is underappreciated' is not. I'd also discount the **GLP-1 / metabolic** ambition heavily — a crowded global field where Sun is a late, unproven entrant. So I weight JPMorgan/CLSA's caution slightly above Bernstein's optimism: own Sun for the India base plus specialty optionality, but size for the binary Halol risk and don't pay up for pipeline catalysts that haven't cleared the FDA. The Halol reinspection outcome is the thing to watch above all else.

Bern|260525.change: Maintained Outperform; PT held ₹2,235. Doubles down on the innovation arm as 'most underappreciated'.
Bern|260525.view: The most bullish and most thesis-driven take — and a useful articulation of the long-term case. But by construction it is talking up a re-rating that hasn't happened; 'most underappreciated' is a narrative, and the ₹2,235 print is the highest precisely because it front-loads pipeline success. Compelling if specialty delivers and Halol stays clean — two things not yet in hand.

CLSA|260524.change: Hold; PT ₹2,020. India/other regions offsetting tepid US generics.
CLSA|260524.view: A sensible fence-sitter — its 'strong India offsetting soft US generics' framing captures the real tension better than either extreme. Hold is an honest call here.

JP|260524.change: Bearish; flags 4QFY26 EBITDA/PAT ~11-13% below consensus on higher costs.
JP|260524.view: The most useful counterweight in the book. A double-digit EBITDA/PAT miss is concrete, not narrative — exactly the near-term earnings-quality signal the bull case tends to wave away. When the bears are pointing at reported numbers and the bulls at pipeline, the bears usually have the stronger near-term ground; I'd take this seriously.

Kotak|260524.change: Maintained Add; PT raised ₹1,850→₹1,960 despite muted Global Innovative Medicines sales.
Kotak|260524.view: Constructive but measured — and tellingly its raised PT (₹1,960) sits far below Bernstein's ₹2,235, which tells you even the optimists can't agree on how much the specialty arm is worth. That gap is itself evidence the re-rating is genuinely contested.

Jeff|260522.change: Neutral; broadly in-line quarter (India formulations solid).
Jeff|260522.view: Neutral, in-line quarter — adds to the cautious cluster. The real message of the book is that three of five houses are neutral-to-negative; the bull case is the minority view here, not the consensus.

Aegis Logistics.summary:
Only one house is represented in the local library: **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹1,010, June 2026), writing a First Take on 4QFY26 results. The trendlyne archive shows **Motilal Oswal** last at Neutral with PT ₹670 in May 2024 — two years stale and nearly 33% below JPMorgan's target — but that note predates the stock's significant re-rating and Aegis's capacity expansion cycle, so it cannot be treated as a live bear view. The local library has no active bear or neutral counterweight; JPMorgan is the only current voice, and its tone is unambiguously constructive after a large earnings beat.

My own read: Aegis runs a high-quality, asset-backed toll model — LPG and chemical terminal handling fees are structurally sticky, underpinned by long-term OMC agreements and India's rising LPG penetration in the eastern/rural pipeline. The 4QFY26 beat (adj PAT ₹4.1bn vs JPMorgan's ₹2.9bn estimate and street ₹2.4bn) was exceptionally wide, which is unusual for a terminal business with largely fixed contractual revenue — it signals either a non-recurring item in the gas division or that utilisation/throughput surprised sharply on the upside; the note does not clarify which, and that distinction matters for the sustainability of earnings. The two things I would watch most: (1) whether the gas-division beat was throughput-driven (durable) or a one-time revaluation/catch-up, and (2) the pace of Pipavav Phase III and Mumbai terminal capacity adds, which are the next leg of the growth story. At JPMorgan's ₹1,010 target the stock likely prices in a healthy expansion pipeline; any slip in commissioning timelines or OMC volume commitments would be the key de-rating risk.

JP|260601.change: PT maintained at ₹1,010; OW maintained (prevTP ₹1,010 → currTP ₹1,010; prevCall OW → currCall OW). This is a First Take note — no formal model revision, just results commentary.
JP|260601.view:
JPMorgan's comfort with OW and an unchanged ₹1,010 target despite a large earnings beat is telling: they were already well above street on their estimate (₹2.9bn vs ₹2.4bn), so the beat confirms rather than surprises their thesis. That suggests they have a differentiated, higher-conviction model on the gas terminal economics — worth weighting their view accordingly.

The caveat is that First Take notes are deliberately thin — no updated EPS, no revised terminal-value assumptions, no view on what drove the beat (throughput, tariff, or one-off). Until the full note lands with a model update, the ₹1,010 target should be read as a floor rather than a refined intrinsic-value estimate. I'd watch for their post-results detailed update to see if the target moves up materially, which would be the cleaner signal on where fair value sits post this earnings inflection.

Afcons Infrastructure.summary:
Only one broker is in the current library — **ICICI Securities** (Hold, PT ₹420, Nov-2025) — and that note is now over eight months stale, predating the worst of the West Asia Crisis (WAC) disruption that hammered 4QFY26 (revenue down ~19% y-y). ICICI was already sounding cautious at the time, flagging order inflow intensity as the key monitorable after a 'subpar quarter'; in retrospect that was an early warning that the WAC headwinds would compound. No updated call exists in the current library. At ₹420, ICICI's target is almost certainly stale relative to revised earnings and order assumptions after 4QFY26 results.

My own read: Afcons has a genuinely differentiated franchise — complex marine, underground and O&G EPC that most domestic peers cannot execute — and **Shapoorji Pallonji**'s backing provides project access and balance-sheet headroom that a standalone read understates. The WAC disruption is the critical near-term variable: vendor advance demands and material-availability constraints create working-capital pressure that may take two to three quarters to unwind fully, even if the geopolitical situation stabilises. Whether FY27 delivers a revenue recovery depends heavily on international order replenishment (particularly Middle East and African corridors) and on whether WAC-related WC normalises on schedule. At current levels the market is giving Afcons credit for a recovery that has not yet shown up in the backlog or cash flows. I'd want to see 1QFY27 order inflows and WC data before committing — if international wins remain below trend, the FY27 recovery thesis loses its foundation.

ICICI|251114.change: Dated Nov-2025 (now over 8 months old); PT ₹420, Hold (per Trendlyne). This is the only ICICI entry in the library; no prior ICICI report exists in the data to establish a delta.
ICICI|251114.view:
ICICI's Hold at ₹420 proved directionally right — flagging 'order inflow intensity' as the key monitorable was prescient, and 4QFY26 confirmed the concern. The 'subpar quarter' label in Nov-2025 was an understatement of what was to follow. The constructive elements of their thesis (Afcons' differentiated capabilities, healthy order book at the time) remain structurally valid, but the earnings model and TP embedded in this note are stale — they predate both the 4QFY26 miss and any management guidance revision post-WAC.

The Hold stance is still probably appropriate given the uncertainty around FY27 execution, but the ₹420 number should not be used as a current valuation anchor. Worth watching for an ICICI follow-up after FY26 annual results — whether they maintain Hold or downgrade on sustained order-inflow weakness will signal whether the bull case for a franchise recovery is holding.

Alkem Laboratories.summary:
Coverage has thinned to three houses — **BOB Capital** (Sell, ₹4,638), **ICICI Securities** (Buy, ₹6,500), and **Motilal Oswal** (Neutral, ₹5,525). The freshest is BOB’s May 2026 post-4QFY26 note; ICICI and MO are both from February 2026 and pre-date the results print. The ~40% TP spread reflects genuine disagreement on FY27 margin trajectory. BOB downgraded from Hold to Sell, arguing EBITDA margins are likely flat in FY27 and valuations stretched — the gross margin beat was real but offset by elevated R&D and one-time charges (Labor Code, real estate impairment). ICICI’s Buy is anchored to recovery from the “temporary India pause” (India grew 9% YoY in 4Q, partly validating that narrative) and medium-term CDMO/med-tech scale-up. MO’s Neutral at ₹5,525 — the lowest non-bear target — reflects a show-me stance on Occlutech integration costs and the CDMO opex trajectory. Both ICICI and MO are now ~5 months stale and would benefit from a post-4Q refresh.

My own read: Alkem’s domestic branded-generic franchise in antibiotics and GI remains one of the most defensible in mid-tier pharma — brand equity and distribution depth that are genuinely hard to replicate, and a gross margin trajectory that has improved materially (65.4% in 4QFY26, +606bp YoY). That said, BOB’s core critique deserves credit: the gross margin beat does not automatically translate into EBITDA margin expansion when R&D for CDMO ambitions is structural rather than one-off and Occlutech adds opex before it contributes to earnings. At ICICI’s ₹6,500 target, Alkem is pricing in a more benign scenario than the evidence currently supports. I would sit closer to MO’s cautious neutral and watch two things: (1) whether India branded generics sustain double-digit growth through H1FY27 — the “temporary pause is over” thesis needs ongoing validation; (2) whether Occlutech/CDMO integration costs remain within guided ranges or creep into a structural drag on margins.

BOB|260529.change: Downgraded Hold→Sell; PT slashed ₹5,962→₹4,638 (vs prior Hold at ₹5,962 on 15-Feb-2026 per trendlyne).
BOB|260529.view:
BOB’s downgrade is the most aggressive move in this results round — a ~22% TP cut and a rating flip to Sell. Their core thesis (EBITDA margins flat in FY27 on elevated opex; valuations expensive at current levels) is worth taking seriously even if ₹4,638 seems deeply pessimistic versus the rest of the pack.

BOB has historically been volatile on Alkem: Buy at ₹7,225 in Nov 2024, then Hold, then briefly Sell (Feb 2025 at ₹4,527), back to Hold, now Sell again. That oscillation suggests mark-to-market reactivity rather than structural conviction — but the valuation point stands independently. At ~30x+ FY27E, Alkem is not cheap for a business with uncertain FY27 margin direction. Treat BOB as the useful contrarian signal on valuation and margin risk, not a high-conviction structural short — but their argument that rising gross margins don’t automatically flow to EBITDA when CDMO opex is ramping is the most important critique of the bull case.

ICICI|260215.view:
ICICI’s February note framed the 3Q India slowdown as a temporary pause with CDMO/new-venture scale-up as the medium-term catalyst. That narrative has partly played out — 4QFY26 India growth recovered to 9% YoY, partially validating the characterisation.

This note is now ~5 months old and pre-dates the 4Q results. ICICI’s ₹6,500 Buy is directionally reasonable but stale; the ₹100 TP trim was a minor adjustment, not a conviction move. The CDMO/Occlutech thesis is the longer-dated call — ICICI appears to be an early mover on that narrative. Worth revisiting when they update post-4Q: if they maintain Buy and nudge the TP up, it carries more weight. If they stay flat or trim again, it signals the new-venture ramp is taking longer than guided.

MO|260214.view:
Motilal’s February note on the Occlutech acquisition is the most thematic of the three views — framing it as a med-tech diversification opportunity rather than a near-term earnings catalyst. That is an honest characterisation: Occlutech (occlusion devices for structural heart disease) is a niche business that will take years to scale meaningfully in India.

MO’s persistent Neutral and the most conservative non-bear TP (₹5,525) reflects a “show me” stance on execution. The ₹35 TP trim in February signals they see near-term headwinds from opex rather than a clear catalyst. Post-4Q, their TP looks conservative given the gross margin beat — but their overall caution may be warranted. If H1FY27 India growth comes in above 10% and CDMO costs are contained, MO looks most likely to upgrade. Watch their next quarterly note for any shift in tone.

Amara Raja Energy and Mobility.summary:
Coverage in this portal has thinned to just two houses — **Anand Rathi** (Hold, ₹1,490, Nov 2024) and **Geojit** (Buy, ₹1,682, Sep 2024) — both 19–21 months stale. Neither was written in the context of the Gotion partnership collapse or the subsequent sell-side re-rating; both reflect peak new-energy optimism. For reference, the most recent external sell-side consensus (May 2026) clustered in a ₹800–942 range — roughly 45–53% below the 2024 stale targets. AR’s Nov 2024 Hold was itself a downgrade from a higher prior target; Geojit’s Sep 2024 Buy was an aggressive upgrade on new-energy momentum. The real bull/bear debate no longer lives in this coverage set — these two views are historical context only.

My own read: Amara Raja’s lead-acid business — automotive OEM and industrial — is consistently under-appreciated. It continues to grow and generates real cash; that franchise is durable regardless of what happens on the new-energy side. The harder question is the Giga corridor pivot. The Gotion breakup removed the LFP chemistry pillar that anchored the original thesis, and the pivot to NMC cells introduces more competition (established global players with scale advantages) and execution risk (cell line commissioning targeted for mid-2027). The 2024 bull targets at ₹1,490–1,682 are simply not credible in the current context. Before turning constructive on a new-energy premium, I would want to verify: (1) whether the NMC cell line commissioning schedule holds, (2) whether the BESS order pipeline is backed by firm customer contracts, and (3) whether the RM cost dynamics that pressured margins in 4QFY26 are transient or structural. Until those are clearer, the lead-acid franchise is worth owning but the new-energy re-rating remains speculative.

AR|241107.change: Downgraded to Hold, TP ₹1,490 (Nov 2024). Trendlyne confirms this was a downgrade event; no prior AR entry in the data to establish exact prior TP. Note is now ~20 months old.
AR|241107.view:
This view predates the Gotion breakup by roughly 18 months and the most recent quarterly results by considerably longer. A Hold at ₹1,490 reflected the new-energy optimism of late 2024 — at the time, the Giga corridor was on track and the LFP partnership intact. None of those assumptions remain current.

Treat this as historical context: AR was cautious enough to downgrade when the rest of the sell-side was still upgrading, which is a signal of relative discipline. But the ₹1,490 target is effectively a stale constructive view that has not been refreshed through any of the material developments since. Discount the number entirely; the downgrade direction (Hold vs Buy) is the only signal worth retaining.

Geojit|240913.change: Upgraded to Buy, TP ₹1,682 (Sep 2024), up from Accumulate at ₹990 (Feb 2024) — a ~70% TP increase in 7 months. Note is now ~22 months old.
Geojit|240913.view:
Geojit’s Sep 2024 upgrade was a momentum call on the new-energy re-rating wave — ₹1,682 was aggressive even at the time and is now entirely disconnected from where sell-side consensus sits post-Gotion. The prior Accumulate at ₹990 in Feb 2024 shows how fast sentiment swung in that period; the reverse has since occurred, and by a comparable magnitude.

Both Geojit entries are historical context only. Neither is actionable, and neither reflects the current strategic picture around the Giga corridor, Gotion collapse, or NMC pivot. The arc from ₹990 Accumulate → ₹1,682 Buy → effectively unstated-but-stale is a useful reminder that high-optionality re-rating calls in Indian industrials can move violently in both directions when the underlying partnership or technology thesis changes.

Amber Enterprises.summary:
Three of four houses are bullish — **BOB Capital Markets** (Buy, PT ₹8,700, Feb-2026), **ICICI Direct** (Buy, PT ₹9,500, Sep-2025), and **Anand Rathi** (Buy, PT ₹10,050, Jul-2025) — with only **ICICI Securities** (Hold, PT ₹7,000, Nov-2025) staying cautious on RAC weakness. Target spread is wide at ₹7,000–₹10,050, reflecting real disagreement on the pace of earnings mix-shift. Notably, three brokers not in the current houseViews set — **CLSA** (OP, PT ₹8,100), **JPMorgan** (Neutral, PT ₹7,650), and **Kotak** (Buy, PT ₹8,710) — all published fresh notes in June 2026 on Amber's entry into smartphone manufacturing via an Oppo collaboration, making the houseViews here (dated Jul–Nov 2025) largely stale on the key debate: whether the smartphone pivot is a TAM-expanding inflection or a margin headwind.

My own read: Amber is a genuine transformation story — from a seasonal, weather-sensitive RAC-OEM into a multi-vector electronics platform spanning consumer appliances, industrial EMS, and now smartphones. The Oppo deal is strategically logical (OPPO/OnePlus/Realme sell ~39mn phones domestically and Amber gets production volume with minimal upfront capex via a sublease), but the economics are thin at the start — management guided 1.5–2% EBITDA initially, rising only as backward integration matures. The more durable value is in the industrial EMS build-out (auto, telecom, defence PCBs), which is less cyclical and stickier than consumer electronics. I'd sit closer to CLSA/JPMorgan's ₹7,650–₹8,100 range than Anand Rathi's ₹10,050 until the smartphone ramp proves out. Key watches: commercial production timeline (Q1FY28 vs management's 8–9mn unit target for FY28); EBITDA margin trajectory through the mix shift; and whether the Electronics segment drives non-seasonal consistency that reduces dependence on the summer RAC cycle.

BOB|260210.change: Prior note (Jul-2025): Hold, PT ₹7,740. Upgraded to Buy; PT raised ₹7,740→₹8,700 in the Feb-2026 Q3FY26 results note (sourced from Trendlyne; no pdfdata entry for BOB in this library).
BOB|260210.view:
BOB's upgrade is credible — Q3FY26 showed a broad rebound and the Electronics segment (PCBA, motors, components) was gaining momentum. The PT of ₹8,700 sits in the middle of the bull herd and is a reasonable central estimate for the pre-smartphone era.

This note predates the Oppo announcement by four months, so the smartphone angle is entirely absent from BOB's current thesis. Worth watching whether BOB refreshes post the Jun-2026 deal to factor in both the incremental revenue opportunity and the near-term EBITDA drag.

ICICI|251109.change: Prior note (Oct-2024): Sell, PT ₹5,625. Upgraded to Hold; PT raised ₹5,625→₹7,000 in the Nov-2025 note (sourced from Trendlyne; no pdfdata entry for ICICI Securities in this library).
ICICI|251109.view:
ICICI Securities made a meaningful journey from Sell to Hold, driven by RAC industry strength and an improving leverage trajectory. But a ₹7,000 PT is the most cautious in the set, and this note is now over eight months old — it predates the Oppo partnership, the EMS acquisitions, and Q3FY26 results.

The core caution (RAC weakness and balance-sheet overhang) has largely resolved, which makes this the most stale and arguably most mis-priced view in the group. I'd discount it heavily until ICICI Securities publishes a fresh note that engages with the smartphone pivot and the current EMS scale-up.

ICICI|250908.change: Upgraded to Buy; PT ₹9,500 (Sep-2025 note). No prior ICICI Direct entry in the library to establish the previous PT or rating.
ICICI|250908.view:
ICICI Direct's Sep-2025 upgrade at ₹9,500 is the most aggressive PT in the houseViews set, timed to the EMS acquisition narrative gaining traction. The timing was reasonable — Amber was visibly diversifying away from its RAC dependency.

At ₹9,500, the PT prices in a lot: successful EMS scale-up, sustained RAC market share, and now the smartphone segment (which ICICI Direct did not have in scope when writing). I'd treat this as a bull-case ceiling rather than a base case, particularly given EBITDA pressure likely in FY28 from the Oppo ramp before margins improve.

AR|250731.change: Dated Jul-2025; Buy, PT ₹10,050 — Buy retained per headline. No prior Anand Rathi note in the library to establish the PT delta.
AR|250731.view:
Anand Rathi carries the highest PT in the set at ₹10,050, underpinned by conviction in the industrial EMS scale-up story (acquisitions in PCB/components). The Jul-2025 timing pre-dates both the Oppo deal and the Q3FY26 results.

At ₹10,050, AR is well above where CLSA and JPMorgan sit after engaging directly with the smartphone pivot. Either AR sees more value in EMS optionality than the global brokers, or this PT has not been stress-tested against the smartphone margin dilution. Given it is now a full year old and the competitive landscape for EMS/smartphones has evolved considerably, treat this as the most stale bull call in the group.

Anthem Biosciences.summary:
Coverage is thin — only **BOB Capital Markets** (Buy, PT ₹900, May-2026) appears in the current houseViews set. **Nomura** (Buy, PT ₹900) has two recent notes in the local library (Jun and Jul 2026) but is not in the houseViews display; Nomura's Jul-2026 Q1FY27 preview flagged 'likely a subdued quarter' due to inherent B2B CDMO revenue lumpiness and small-scale product concentration — a material cautionary note that the BOB headline glosses over. No bears are in coverage. The narrow PT range (₹835 at BOB's Feb-2026 initiation → ₹900 now) signals limited valuation disagreement among the bulls.

My own read: Anthem is a niche but credible CRDMO story — the combination of fermentation-based CDMO capabilities, specialty ingredients (biotic/probiotic supplements), and an emerging peptides platform gives it broader differentiation than a pure CRO or CMO. The biotech funding recovery thesis (post-2023 drought, improving traction with big pharma) is the macro tailwind all bulls cite. However, being sub-scale with high product concentration is a genuine execution risk: quarterly revenues can swing sharply, as Nomura's Q1FY27 warning underscores. The ₹900 PT is a punchy multiple that prices in delivery on the commercial molecule pipeline and margin sustainability — neither of which is assured in FY27. I'd want two to three quarters of consistent revenue execution before fully endorsing. Key watches: client and molecule diversification (single-customer concentration risk); EBITDA margin trajectory as the business scales into larger batch sizes; and whether the peptides segment earns meaningful revenue or remains aspirational.

BOB|260521.change: Prior note (Feb-2026, initiation): Buy, PT ₹835. PT raised ₹835→₹900; Buy maintained in the May-2026 post-results note (sourced from Trendlyne; no pdfdata entry for BOB in this library).
BOB|260521.view:
BOB initiated in Feb-2026 with a full-spectrum CRDMO capability framing and has since nudged its PT to ₹900 after the May-2026 results on the back of intact growth drivers — commercial molecule pipeline, specialty ingredients momentum, and broader CRDMO sector re-rating.

The bull case hinges on two claims that need watching: 'growth drivers intact' and 'industry-leading margins to sustain'. BOB appears more sanguine than Nomura, which sees Q1FY27 as subdued. If margins compress even modestly — from mix shift, scale-up costs, or competitive pricing pressure — the ₹900 PT loses its cushion quickly. BOB's directional bull stance is probably right for the medium term, but the execution bar is higher than the headline implies and the near-term quarter is set up to disappoint.

Apar Industries.summary:
Only **PL** (Prabhudas Lilladhar) covers Apar in the current library, following a downgrade to Hold in its Q4FY26 result update (260529). The headline reads "Strong T&D tailwinds anchor long term outlook" while the rating is Hold — a textbook valuation call, not a thesis reversal. PL raised its PT ~38% in the very same note (from ₹9,629 to ₹13,309), signalling continued confidence in the business but insufficient upside at current levels. Without another active house in the library for comparison, there is no live cross-house debate; a prior multi-house view (which included Nomura at Buy, TP ₹14,240) is no longer represented in houseViews.

My own read: Apar is a genuine structural compounder inside India's multi-year T&D build-out — conductors, cables, and transformer oil all benefit from PGCIL capex, state-distribution upgrades, and fast-growing export demand. The Q4FY26 beat and PL's sharp PT jump confirm execution is real, not narrative. What I would surface that the sell-side underweights: (1) **export-cable concentration** — a large share of the recent upside is export-driven, and US/EU tariff or trade dynamics could introduce margin volatility that the domestic grid story does not; (2) **raw-material cycles** — aluminium and copper tailwinds flattered FY26 margins and could reverse on a commodity turn; (3) **the ~₹15bn FY27E capex plan** — at this scale, any demand softening converts growth capex into a leverage risk. PL's track record on Apar has been persistently too cautious (Buy in Nov-2022 at ₹1,834, then a string of Accumulate/Hold cuts while the stock compounded past ₹13,000), so their TP of ₹13,309 may again prove conservative if the order pipeline stays robust. For a long-term holder the thesis remains intact; for a new entry today, the margin of safety is thin.

PL|260529.change: PT raised ₹9,629→₹13,309 (prior trendlyne entry: PL 260316, Accumulate, TP ₹9,629); rating downgraded Accumulate→Hold. No pdfdata entry for this note — change derived from trendlyne sequence.
PL|260529.view:
PL raised its PT ~38% in the same note it downgraded the rating — that pairing says "great company, full price" rather than "business deteriorating". The T&D tailwinds narrative is intact; the Hold is pure valuation discipline.

PL's history on Apar is worth keeping in mind: they have consistently underestimated the stock across multiple cycles (Buy in late-2022, then cuts to Accumulate/Hold at progressively higher prices, while the PT kept climbing). The TP of ₹13,309 could again prove conservative if domestic T&D ordering stays robust and export execution continues to beat. That said, flagging margin-of-safety risk at elevated multiples is fair, and for a new position today the upside to target is thin.

Ashok Leyland.summary:
Three houses remain active on **Ashok Leyland** and all lean cautious — though the degree varies. **BOB Capital** (Hold, TP ₹186, May-2026) has progressively cut from Buy earlier in the cycle; its Q4 note ("steady show, muted growth, cost inflation") is the freshest read and directionally reliable. **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, TP ₹185, Apr-2026) nominally holds the most constructive rating but slashed its PT from ₹238 to ₹185 — a 22% cut in under two months — and the note predates Q4 results. The targets have converged: MO Buy at ₹185 vs BOB Hold at ₹186 is effectively the same price with a different label. **Deven Choksey** (Accumulate, TP ₹156, Nov-2025) is the most cautious on level and the most stale — its quiet Buy→Accumulate downgrade in November already signalled eroding conviction before the post-Q4 consensus moved more negative. The missing voices are significant: **Kotak** (Reduce, TP ₹170) and **JPMorgan** (Neutral, TP ₹175), which appeared in the prior houseViews panel, no longer feature — their absence likely reflects library staleness, so the institutional bear and neutral views are under-represented in the current active set.

**My own read:** I sit cautiously neutral. Ashok Leyland runs a well-managed MHCV business with meaningful pricing discipline, but the CV cycle is in its mature phase — the easy volume recovery from the FY22-23 trough is behind us, diesel costs have risen mid-cycle, and fleet operator profitability is under pressure. MO's 22% PT compression in two months is the most honest signal yet that FY27 consensus earnings may need further cuts. DC's TP at ₹156 — below current market levels — is the arithmetic implication of a flat-cycle earnings scenario. Defence and LCV adjacencies are structurally interesting but remain too small to offset a meaningful MHCV slowdown in the next two to three quarters. The two things I would watch most: (1) monthly MHCV wholesale dispatch trends through Q1FY27, particularly whether the festive pre-build tracks ahead of or behind prior year; and (2) freight operator profitability — if spot freight rates stay compressed while diesel costs remain elevated, fleet replacement demand will defer. A more decisive entry looks closer to the ₹150-155 range than current levels.

BOB|260529.change: TP cut ₹199→₹186 (prior BOB entry: Feb-2026, Hold at TP ₹199); Hold maintained. BOB had already downgraded from Buy to Hold in the Feb-2026 note, so this May-2026 update marks a second consecutive deterioration in view.
BOB|260529.view:
BOB has been on a steady downgrade path — Buy early cycle, then downgraded to Hold in February 2026 at TP ₹199, and the Q4FY26 note cuts the target further to ₹186 while maintaining Hold. The headline framing ("steady Q4; muted growth, cost inflation to impact show") is bearish in everything except the rating label. Three consecutive negative TP moves from a house that was constructive earlier in the cycle is a meaningful signal.

The Hold at ₹186 implies theoretical upside from the mid-₹160s, but BOB's own note undermines confidence in that target: "muted growth" and "cost inflation" are not conditions under which a price target tends to get realised. I read this as a ceiling call more than a return call. Not a sell trigger, but no reason to add at current levels.

MO|260401.change: TP cut sharply ₹238→₹185 (prior MO entry: Feb-2026, Buy at TP ₹238); Buy maintained. A 22% target reduction in under two months without a rating change.
MO|260401.view:
Motilal Oswal's April 2026 note — flagging global headwinds and CV cycle risk — is now three-plus months old and predates the Q4FY26 result. The 22% TP cut from ₹238 to ₹185 while retaining a Buy is a classic institutional posture: not wanting to downgrade yet clearly needing to reset the earnings model. The gap between the February and April numbers implies significant earnings cuts were already made.

At TP ₹185, MO's Buy and BOB's Hold converge on essentially the same price — the rating difference is semantic. A post-Q4 update from MO may have revised the target further; the April note's identification of global headwinds as the key risk variable creates a macro-dependent thesis that is difficult to trade around. I would want to see their post-Q4 stance before weighting this Buy meaningfully.

DC|251119.change: Rating downgraded Buy→Accumulate (prior DC entry: Aug-2025, Buy at TP ₹155); TP marginally raised ₹155→₹156. Effectively a downgrade at a flat price.
DC|251119.view:
Deven Choksey's Nov-2025 note is 8+ months old and covers Q2FY26 — well before the diesel cost pressures and macro headwinds that BOB and MO flagged in their more recent coverage. The quiet Buy→Accumulate downgrade at a barely changed TP is a classic soft signal: the house no longer believes the stock warrants aggressive accumulation but is not ready to downgrade formally.

At TP ₹156, DC's target is the lowest in the panel and below current market price — arithmetically implying the stock is fully or mildly overvalued at current levels. The note carries no current actionable weight, but it is a useful reminder that even a operationally positive quarter ("robust performance") was not enough to sustain Buy conviction. A fresh DC update post Q4FY26 would almost certainly be more cautious.

Asian Paints.summary:
The active house views on **Asian Paints** are split between a bull camp and a persistent bear minority. **Axis Direct** (Buy, TP ₹3,130, Jun-2026) is the freshest and most conservative of the bulls — upgraded post FY26 results. **Geojit** (Buy, TP ₹3,244, Nov-2025) and **ICICI Direct** (Buy, TP ₹3,330, Nov-2025) both upgraded in November 2025 following what appeared to be a stabilisation quarter, with Geojit completing a full Sell→Hold→Buy arc through CY25. Against them: **Deven Choksey** (Sell, TP ₹2,753, Nov-2025) held Sell even as Geojit and ICICI Direct upgraded from the same quarterly result in the same week. **PL** (Sell, TP ₹2,142, May-2025) and **ICICI Securities** (Sell, TP ₹2,200, Feb-2025) are stale bears — their PTs have been overtaken by the stock recovery, but the structural concern they identified (competition-led margin compression, muted volumes) was directionally correct. The live bull cluster is ₹3,130–₹3,330; DC's live bear target is ₹2,753. Several major institutional voices (CLSA, Nomura, Jefferies, Kotak, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley) that appeared in the prior houseViews panel no longer feature — their removal likely reflects library staleness, leaving the institutional debate significantly under-represented in the current active set.

**My own read:** Asian Paints owns a genuine franchise — six-decade brand equity, unmatched distribution depth, proprietary colour-matching technology. These moats are real and not easily replicated. But the Birla Opus entry is the most credible competitive test the company has faced in a generation, and I think the November 2025 upgrade wave — triggered by a single stabilising quarter — may have got ahead of the structural adjustment still underway. Birla Group has the balance sheet to sustain aggressive dealer incentives for years; this is not a seasonal challenger that retreats when the going gets tough. The bull camp's ₹3,130–₹3,330 PTs implicitly require both volume growth AND margin recovery to work simultaneously — a high bar when trade-spend competition remains active. DC's lone Sell (₹2,753) is the more intellectually honest live call in this set, even if the absolute level is debatable. I would watch two things: (1) quarterly volume growth — if the November optimism was justified, volumes should be tracking 8–10% YoY; any slip toward 5-6% unwinds the upgrade thesis quickly; and (2) gross margin trajectory — Birla Opus's pricing aggression forces a persistent choice between defending margin and defending share that has not fully resolved.

Axis|260601.change: Upgraded to Buy, TP ₹3,130 (trendlyne confirms upgrade; no prior Axis Direct entry on Asian Paints in the data to compare with).
Axis|260601.view:
Axis Direct's June 2026 upgrade to Buy at TP ₹3,130 is the most current note in the active panel. The target is the most conservative among the bulls — sitting ₹200 below ICICI Direct's ₹3,330 from six months prior — suggesting either a lower earnings multiple or a more restrained volume recovery assumption. The timing (post FY26 full-year results) is its principal strength: this is a considered call on a known data set.

That said, it reads as momentum-driven — constructive on improved near-term visibility rather than a contrarian or differentiated structural thesis. Without the underlying report, the assumptions backing TP ₹3,130 cannot be independently verified. Treat as the most relevant current sentiment marker: when the freshest domestic-brokerage note is a Buy at ₹3,130 post FY26, the street has clearly turned constructive, but the conservative-vs-peers target suggests even the most recent bull is not pounding the table.

Geojit|251114.change: Upgraded to Buy, TP ₹3,244 (prior Geojit entry: Aug-2025, Hold at TP ₹2,777); TP raised ₹2,777→₹3,244. Geojit also moved through Sell (May-2025, TP ₹2,095) → Hold (Aug-2025, TP ₹2,777) → Buy (Nov-2025, TP ₹3,244) across CY25.
Geojit|251114.view:
Geojit's full rating roundtrip in CY25 — Sell to Hold to Buy in six months — is the most vivid illustration of how reactive domestic coverage can be to quarterly beats. The Buy at ₹3,244 was set when the stock was trading lower than the subsequent Axis upgrade, so the implied upside from current levels is probably compressed compared to the original call.

The note is 8+ months old. The rapid-reversal history leaves limited confidence that the conviction is deeply anchored. It confirms the November 2025 upgrade wave happened, but it is not an independent analytical anchor. A refreshed Geojit note post FY26 full-year results would be far more informative.

DC|251114.change: Sell maintained (prior DC entry: Aug-2025, Sell at TP ₹2,470); TP raised ₹2,470→₹2,753 despite the maintained Sell.
DC|251114.view:
DC is the only active Sell in the panel — holding conviction in the same week that Geojit and ICICI Direct upgraded from the same quarterly data. The TP has moved up (from ₹2,470 to ₹2,753), which softens the directional severity, but the Sell rating has not budged. DC's headline framing — "double-digit volume growth despite a weak demand environment on the back of strong execution push" — is actually a creditable operational observation, yet DC still rates Sell, implying the valuation embeds too much optimism given the structural margin headwind.

This dissent from the November upgrade wave is the most useful analytical signal in the current panel. DC is pricing structural competition-led margin impairment that overwhelms near-term volume beats in the valuation — which is the correct framework for thinking about Birla Opus. I would not dismiss this call just because the consensus moved the other way. At TP ₹2,753, DC's Sell is the live bear anchor and deserves more weight than its lone status might suggest.

ICICI|251113.change: Upgraded to Buy, TP ₹3,330 (prior ICICI Direct entry not found in trendlyne — prior rating before upgrade not captured). Highest active bull target in the panel.
ICICI|251113.view:
ICICI Direct's November 2025 upgrade to Buy at TP ₹3,330 was part of the same wave as Geojit, triggered by the Q2FY26 stabilisation. The TP is the highest in the active panel, suggesting ICICI Direct is applying the most generous forward earnings multiple or the most optimistic volume-and-margin recovery combination.

The note is 8+ months old and predates the FY26 full year. The fact that Axis Direct — upgrading six months later with a full additional quarter of data — set a more conservative TP of ₹3,130 may imply ICICI's ₹3,330 has not been validated by FY26 outcomes. Treat as the upper bound of the bull range; a fresh ICICI Direct update post FY26 is needed to confirm this target remains live and unrevised.

PL|250508.change: Dated May-2025 (Q4FY25 result note); no prior PL entry on Asian Paints in the data to compare. Sell, TP ₹2,142.
PL|250508.view:
PL's May-2025 result update (Sell, TP ₹2,142) is 14+ months old. The TP is below every other view in the current panel — bulls and bears alike. The structural concern driving the Sell (Birla Opus disruption, margin compression, difficult volume environment in FY25) was directionally correct, but the absolute level has been overtaken by the November 2025 upgrade wave and subsequent stock recovery.

This note carries no current actionable weight. Its value is historical: it documents the depth of bear sentiment at mid-2025 and confirms that a significant portion of the street saw structural impairment risk at that time. PL would need to update their view materially for any current relevance.

ICICI|250205.change: Dated Feb-2025; no prior ICICI Securities entry in the data to compare. Sell, TP ₹2,200. Headline: "CY25 — likely to be another tough year (despite favourable base)."
ICICI|250205.view:
ICICI Securities' February 2025 note (Sell, TP ₹2,200) is 17+ months old. The "another tough year" framing was accurate — FY25 and early FY26 were genuinely difficult, with Birla Opus ramp-up, gross margin compression, and muted volume growth. The structural diagnosis was right.

However, the TP of ₹2,200 belongs to a different chapter of the Asian Paints story and carries zero current analytical weight. Even DC's active Sell is now at ₹2,753. This note is useful only as a historical baseline for how deep the bear consensus ran at the start of CY25 — it should not inform any current positioning without a fresh ICICI Securities update.

Aditya Birla Capital.summary:
The active houseViews on **Aditya Birla Capital** have narrowed to two houses — **ICICI Securities** (Buy, TP ₹420, May-2026) and **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, TP ₹380, Oct-2025) — both bullish but with very different freshness. The PT spread is ₹380–₹420 (~10%), with ICICI the most current and highest. **MO's Oct-2025 view is now ~9 months stale** and its ₹380 target has been overtaken by the re-rating; treat it as a directional anchor, not a live valuation signal. The broader PDF library (not in houseViews) adds context: **Morgan Stanley** initiated coverage at OW/TP ₹450 in July 2026, premised on a strong 1QFY27 at ABHFL (NII +52% YoY, PAT +95% YoY) — the highest PT across any broker. The shared thesis: NBFC RoA expansion in FY27 driven by NIM recovery as the high-cost wholesale borrowing book reprices and the unsecured mix is calibrated downward. No house carries a Neutral or negative view — notable given ABCL's ~90% PT appreciation since early-2025 and a potential consensus-risk flag.

My own read: ABCL is a reasonable diversified-financial bet on India's private credit cycle, but the investment case has grown demanding at post-re-rating prices. The NBFC RoA expansion story (ICICI's central hook for FY27) depends on credit costs staying range-bound as the unsecured/SME book is rebuilt — precisely the assumption that peers tripped on in FY25-26. ABHFL is the cleaner leg: 1QFY27 momentum is real and the housing finance cycle has a longer runway. The holdco discount is a structural drag; ABCL will likely keep trading below sum-of-parts as long as insurance subsidiaries are majority-held but not mark-to-market consolidated. Two things to watch: (1) NBFC NIM trajectory in Q1-Q2 FY27 — did it trough, or is there another quarter of compression? — and (2) the pace of ABHFL loan-on-book growth vs assignment income, which can move reported PAT significantly in either direction.

ICICI|260505.change: PT raised ₹380→₹420; Buy maintained (vs prior ICICI note Oct-2025).
ICICI|260505.view:
ICICI's May-2026 post-results note is the most substantive and current view on ABCL in the active houseViews. The ₹40 PT lift after FY26 results signals a real positive inflection in the NBFC RoA trajectory and is consistent with the broader sell-side narrative on NIM recovery. The framing — "Strong FY26 finish; FY27 NBFC RoA set to rise on potential margin expansion" — is the key forward-looking bet.

This upgrade is a lagging endorsement of management's FY26 delivery, not yet a forward audit of FY27 credit-cost and NIM assumptions. ICICI's own Feb-2025 TP of ₹220 rising to ₹420 in 15 months is steep; at current prices the margin of safety is thin. I'd want to see Q1 FY27 NBFC results — specifically credit costs and NIM print — before treating ₹420 as conservatively set.

MO|251031.change: PT raised ₹340→₹380; Buy maintained (vs prior MO note Sep-2025).
MO|251031.view:
Motilal Oswal's Oct-2025 note is the stalest active view at ~9 months old. The ₹380 target sits below ICICI's ₹420 and well below the Morgan Stanley PDF-library OW/₹450, reflecting where the market stood before the FY26 results and 1QFY27 cycle. MO's directional call — "Operating performance strengthens in both NBFC and HFC" — was correct, but the view has not been refreshed.

Treat MO's note as corroboration of the bull direction, not as a current price anchor. MO will likely update post Q1 FY27 results; until then the ₹380 PT is simply an estimate that has been lapped by events.

Concord Biotech.summary:
Two houses cover Concord Biotech, both having freshly cut price targets after a weak Mar-Q: **Kotak** is constructive at Add (PT ₹1,275, cut from ₹1,375) and **Jefferies** is cautious at Hold (PT ₹1,020, cut from ₹1,170) — a ~25% spread between the two targets. Neither upgraded; the debate is about whether FY26's headwinds (tariff uncertainty, airspace constraints, customer tender delays, staggered procurement) are truly extrinsic and transient, or whether the persisting oversupply in small-molecule fermentation APIs is a structural drag that will outlast one-quarter noise. Both houses acknowledge management's 18–20%+ revenue growth guidance for FY27 and visibility in the 1HFY27 order book, but diverge on how much credit to give it before seeing execution.

My own read: Concord is a genuine quality franchise — a fermentation-based API specialist with real technical moats and historically strong margins — but FY26 exposed vulnerabilities on multiple fronts simultaneously. The oversupply in immunosuppressant and macrolide APIs is not a temporary glitch; Chinese capacity in these molecules is a persistent overhang and pricing power has eroded. The "delayed customer orders" and "change in procurement pattern" flags from Jefferies are worth taking seriously: if these reflect a structural shift in how large generic customers manage inventory or dual-source, the recovery cadence could be slower than management guides. I'd lean closer to Jefferies' caution than Kotak's constructiveness — the Add call effectively requires trusting both management execution and API pricing stabilisation in FY27, neither of which FY26 gave confidence in. The two things I'd watch most: (1) whether 1HFY27 revenue actually realises at the guided pace by Q2FY27 results, and (2) signs of pricing improvement in key fermentation APIs as a lead indicator of demand-supply rebalancing.

Kotak|260602.view:
Kotak is the more constructive house but is not fully convicted — cutting PT by ₹100 while holding Add signals that even the bull acknowledges FY26 was genuinely poor. The thesis rests on the headwinds being extrinsic (tariffs, airspace, tender timing) and on management's 18%+ FY27 growth guidance being credible given 1HFY27 order visibility. That is a reasonable base case IF the order book converts cleanly.

The part worth stress-testing: Kotak itself calls oversupply in the small-molecule fermentation API space a "headache" — which is a structural admission, not just a cyclical one. An Add with a ₹1,275 PT only works if margin recovery accompanies volume growth; if pricing pressure persists in fermentation APIs, the EBITDA expansion story frays. I'd treat the Add as a cautious long-term hold rather than a near-term catalyst call.

Jeff|260601.view:
Jefferies cut the PT by a steeper ₹150 (13%) and stayed at Hold — the more defensible stance given the Mar-Q miss and unresolved structural questions. The key phrase in their note is "some of the challenges like customer tender delays are not fully behind" — this is Jefferies signalling they won't upgrade until they see cleaner execution, not just management guidance.

The implied ~20% FY27 revenue growth Jefferies uses is similar to Kotak's number, but their willingness to hold rather than add reflects appropriate scepticism about whether the order book actually converts. This is the more useful counterweight in the house-view set: Hold here is not a neutral view, it is a "show me" position. If FY27 1H revenues disappoint again, the ₹1,020 PT likely comes under further pressure.

Container Corporation of India.summary:
The current houseViews for CONCOR are thin and skewed bullish: **MO** (Buy ₹560, May-26) and **ICICI** (Buy ₹682, Nov-25). ICICI's Nov-25 note is 7.5 months old, predates Q4FY26 results (reported May 2026), and carries a ₹682 target that sits ~22% above MO's own post-4Q revised ₹560 — MO cut their target 41% over 12 months (₹980→₹950→₹560) while maintaining Buy. Fresh pdfdata provides a more complete picture: **JPMorgan** (Neutral, PT raised ₹530→₹540 post the Q1FY27 management call, Jul 27) noted management raised FY27 volume guidance from 9.5% to 18%, but JP considers this aspirational — achieving 18% requires 21% volume growth for the remainder of the year against a FY16–26 CAGR of 6.7%, and near-term realizations remain soft with haulage ask rates steep. The previous houseViews also included Jefferies, JPMorgan (May-26 note), and Kotak with post-4Q views; those have been superseded as all three published Q1FY27 updates currently pending houseViews ingestion.

My own read: CONCOR's moat is real — the government-backed ICD network, lower haulage economics than road, and the Dedicated Freight Corridor will benefit it materially over time. But the private Container Train Operator threat deserves more credit than the two-bull houseViews suggests. Private CTOs have proven they can take domestic share on turnaround speed and pricing flexibility, and the FY26 market-share erosion was not a one-off. Management's jump from 9.5% to 18% FY27 volume guidance post Q1FY27 is encouraging but hard to triangulate — JP's scepticism (21% growth for 9 remaining months vs 6.7% historical CAGR) is the right analytical frame. DFC is a genuine long-term catalyst but the JNPT last-mile connection has been the consensus inflection point for years without a clear commissioning date. At ~₹510, the stock has de-rated substantially, which reduces downside risk, but I would want two things before getting constructive: (1) domestic market share stabilisation in consecutive quarters, and (2) a credible DFC-JNPT commissioning schedule. Until then, JPMorgan's Neutral stance is intellectually the most defensible position in the coverage set.

MO|260526.change: Trendlyne: PT slashed ₹950→₹560 (Jan 2026 prior); Buy maintained. Part of a pattern: ₹980 (Jun-25) → ₹950 (Jan-26) → ₹560 (May-26), a 43% reduction from the Jun-25 peak. No pdfdata local match for this note.
MO|260526.view:
MO's headline — "Weak 4Q; realizations and margins remain under pressure" — is accurate, but a maintained Buy after three successive and deep target cuts raises conviction concerns. A house running ₹980 in June 2025 and ₹560 in May 2026 without ever moving off Buy has been consistently wrong on near-term timing. At ₹560, the implied upside from ~₹510 is only ~10% — a thin premium for a Buy rating.

The note is sourced from Trendlyne only (no local PDF), so the analytical detail is unavailable. Weight lightly as a directional indicator that even the most committed CONCOR bull has absorbed a major downgrade to near-term expectations. MO's credibility on the long-term logistics-infra story is intact; their timing track record on CONCOR is poor.

ICICI|251113.change: Trendlyne: PT ₹682 unchanged from the Aug 2025 prior note; Buy maintained. Note dated Nov 2025 — 7.5 months old, predates Q4FY26 results and the FY27 guidance revisions.
ICICI|251113.view:
ICICI's Nov-25 note noted EBITDA beating consensus and management maintaining 13% volume growth guidance for FY26. That guidance was not met — Q4FY26 was weak and management's initial FY27 guidance was just 9.5% (before the aspirational raise to 18% post Q1FY27). ICICI has not refreshed their view through either development.

At ₹682, ICICI's target is the most optimistic view in any current CONCOR note — ~22% above MO's post-4Q ₹560 and ~34% above the current price (~₹510). This target has not been adjusted since Aug-25. Until ICICI publishes a post-Q4FY26 update, treat this as a stale artefact rather than a live call.

Devyani International.summary:
Three active houses are bullish: **DC** (May-26, Buy, PT ₹133), **Emkay** (Jan-26, Buy, PT ₹190), and **MO** (Jan-26, Buy, PT ₹180). **Sharekhan** (Nov-24, Hold, PT ₹180) is 20+ months stale and can be disregarded. DC's ₹133 is the freshest view and the lowest target — almost certainly because the stock devalued between January and May, not because DC is structurally more bearish than Emkay/MO. The Jan-26 views predate Q4FY26 results and the fuller picture on the Sapphire Foods (SF) merger; Q1FY27 results (late July 2026) attracted fresh coverage from external houses not in this houseViews set (JPM OW ₹127, GS Buy ₹142, Kotak Buy ₹155), which broadly aligns with DC's May-26 ₹133 and confirms the Jan-26 Emkay/MO PTs are stale in absolute terms. The central bull thesis: the SF merger consolidating KFC + Pizza Hut under one Yum! Brands franchisee, plus the Q4FY26 KFC SSSG inflection (+4.9% after 11 consecutive negative quarters). The real debate is whether that SSSG recovery is durable or base-effect-driven.

My own read: the SF merger is strategically sound — unified KFC + Pizza Hut removes a structurally loss-making competitor, simplifies Yum! negotiations, and concentrates capex discipline. But a single positive SSSG quarter after 11 negative ones is not yet a trend. India QSR faces persistent structural pressure from food-delivery aggregator discounting and food-price inflation that compress both ticket size and traffic. DC's ₹133 Buy on a derating stock is the most credible timing signal in this set — a house that progressively cut estimates (₹193→₹165→₹133) finally pulling the Buy trigger is a bottom-signal with track-record backing.
