PL’s downgrade is the key contrarian data point here, and it is valuation-led rather than fundamentally bearish — they raised the PT from ₹943 to ₹1,233 in the same note, acknowledging earnings delivery. The message is that the order pipeline is real, but the market has re-rated the stock well past what the numbers justify.

This is the most recent note in the two-house set (May-2026) and the freshest anchor for valuation scepticism. PL has tracked Avalon through at least four reports across FY25–FY26 and has been responsive to earnings rather than stubbornly bearish. I would treat their ₹1,233 Hold as the floor of any defensible near-term fair-value range.

MO|260205.change: PT raised ₹970→₹1,300; Buy maintained (prior MO entry: Apr-2025 at ₹970/Buy).
MO|260205.view:
MO has been the most consistent bull in this name, tracking it from Nov-2024 and delivering three successive PT raises as management executed and raised guidance. The Feb-2026 note anchored on strong growth momentum and a clear management track record.

Staleness is now material: at nearly six months old, this note predates FY27 guidance disclosures and Q1FY27 results. MO’s ₹1,300 target may need revisiting if the stock has continued to appreciate — their Buy was calibrated to a market price likely below current levels. A Q1FY27 result update from MO is the key missing piece; until it arrives, treat ₹1,300 as a valuation data-point, not a live price target.

Avenue Supermarts.summary:
Four houses cover DMart — **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Hold, PT ₹4,410, May-2026 — the freshest note), **ICICI Securities** (Hold, PT ₹4,000, Jan-2026 — lowest target), **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, PT ₹4,600, Jan-2026), and **Axis Direct** (Buy, PT ₹4,770, May-2025 — over 14 months stale). The cautious camp (PL + ICICI) anchors around ₹4,000–4,410; the bulls (MO + Axis) sit at ₹4,600–4,770 — roughly a 15% spread. PL’s May-2026 note is the most current and unambiguous: quick commerce will “continue to dent growth prospects.” The Q1FY27 results, which postdate all four houseViews, have sharpened the debate: 15% revenue growth missed the ∼19–20% consensus, SSSG declined to 5.5% from 10.8% in Q4FY26, and management flagged nil throughput improvement in mature high-traffic metro stores. In the broader broker universe, Kotak cut PT ₹4,250→₹3,850 (Reduce), JPMorgan trimmed ₹4,400→₹4,250 (Neutral), Goldman Sachs maintained ₹4,000 Sell, while Morgan Stanley held OW at ₹5,083 and CLSA cut its PT from ₹6,628 to ₹5,723 but maintained Outperform. A Kotak note (Jul-2026) frames the key structural question: Blinkit is tracking to surpass DMart’s quarterly revenue run-rate by 3QFY27 — a psychological inflection that shifts the framing from cyclical pressure to structural market-share shift. The Annual Investor Meet (Jul-28, new CEO’s first) is the near-term catalyst.

My own read: DMart’s owned-store model, extreme cost discipline, and supply-chain density are real and durable advantages that most grocery retailers globally cannot replicate. But quick-commerce is not a cyclical headwind — it is a structural redefinition of high-frequency urban grocery shopping. The Q1FY27 metro LFL data is the tell: management’s own disclosure that mature high-throughput metro stores saw nil YoY throughput improvement is the leading indicator of q-comm erosion in exactly the highest-value stores. The 50bps gross margin expansion was encouraging but reflects General Merchandise & Apparel mix shift, not grocery momentum. DMart Ready remains nascent; scaling it would require capital allocation and margin sacrifice that conflicts with the very frugality that built the brand. I sit closer to PL’s Hold than MO’s Buy at current valuations. The two signals I’d track most closely: (1) quarterly LFL specifically in urban metro clusters — that is the real q-comm erosion gauge; and (2) the new CEO’s articulation at the Investor Meet of the DMart Ready investment plan and unit-economics path to profitability.

PL|260503.change: PT raised ₹3,994→₹4,410 (prior PL entry: Jul-2025 at ₹3,994/Hold); Hold maintained.
PL|260503.view:
PL’s May-2026 Q4FY26 result update is the freshest note in the set, and its central thesis — that quick commerce will structurally dent DMart’s growth — has been validated by the Q1FY27 earnings print that followed. The PT nudge from ₹3,994 to ₹4,410 reflects earnings revision (Q4 profitability was fine), but the rating conviction is unchanged.

PL has maintained Hold through at least four quarterly cycles without capitulating to the bull case. That consistency is significant. Q1FY27 — metro LFL flat, SSSG 5.5%, revenue well below consensus — further vindicates the cautious read. I would weight this note most heavily among the four: it is the most current, most relevant to the structural debate, and the house has been directionally right.

ICICI|260112.change: Upgraded to Hold; PT ₹4,000 (Jan-2026). Prior ICICI rating not available in the library.
ICICI|260112.view:
ICICI’s Jan-2026 upgrade to Hold at ₹4,000 is now over six months stale. The ₹4,000 PT was the most conservative target in the coverage universe at the time, suggesting ICICI was likely upgrading from a Sell or Reduce rather than becoming constructive.

Post Q1FY27, ICICI’s floor call has converged with the current cautious consensus: Goldman Sachs (Sell, ₹4,000) and Kotak (Reduce, ₹3,850) now sit at or below it. Treat this as the low-end fair-value anchor in the houseViews set, but note it has not been refreshed since January — discount its immediacy accordingly.

MO|260111.change: PT raised ₹4,350→₹4,600 (prior MO entry: May-2025 at ₹4,350/Buy); Buy maintained.
MO|260111.view:
MO’s Jan-2026 note title — “Strong beat on profitability; sustainability remains key” — flagged the right tension: the Q3 profitability surprised, but repeatability was the open question. Their Buy at ₹4,600 positioned them as the moderate bull between the cautious camp and the more aggressive outliers.

The ‘sustainability’ caveat proved prescient: Q1FY27 margins held (+10bp EBITDA YoY, +50bp gross margin) but revenue disappointed at 15% vs. ∼19% consensus. MO’s note is now over six months old. A Q1FY27 refresh would be telling — specifically whether they trim toward the ₹4,250–4,400 range that JPMorgan now occupies, or hold their Buy conviction in the face of the metro LFL stall.

Axis|250505.change: Upgraded to Buy; PT ₹4,770 (May-2025). No prior Axis entry in the library — prior call not confirmed. Note is now over 14 months old.
Axis|250505.view:
Axis’s May-2025 Buy at ₹4,770 is the oldest note in the set by a large margin and should be treated as stale. It predates four quarterly earnings cycles, the full crystallisation of the quick-commerce threat across Blinkit/Zepto/Swiggy Instamart, and the Q1FY27 revenue growth miss.

The ₹4,770 target now sits above MO’s ₹4,600 but was calibrated to a completely different information set. Give this note near-zero weight in forming a current view — it needs a refresh before it can inform any investment decision meaningfully.

Bajaj Finance.summary:
The six-house coverage is now fully in the bull-to-cautious range — **Bernstein** exited, leaving no outright bear. The bull camp — **Deven Choksey** (Buy ₹1,120), **BOB Capital** (Buy ₹1,193), **ICICI Direct** (Buy ₹1,180), and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (upgraded to Buy ₹1,100 on Q4FY26 results) — clusters between ₹1,100–₹1,193. **Motilal Oswal** (Neutral ₹1,000) and **ICICI Securities** (Hold ₹1,050) are the cautious holdouts. The sharpest signal from Q4FY26 result day: PL upgraded (buying the credit-cost improvement) while MO simultaneously cut its PT from ₹1,160 to ₹1,000 (not trusting the re-rating) — both seeing the same numbers, arriving at opposite conclusions. BOB Capital (Feb-2026) and ICICI Direct (Dec-2025) notes are now 4–6 months old. Beyond this houseViews set, broader PDF data shows a widening bull consensus: JPMorgan raised PT ₹1,175→₹1,215 after the 1QFY27 pre-quarter AUM print (24% YoY, 7.2% QoQ — highest since 2QFY24), Jefferies maintained Buy at ₹1,210, and CLSA reiterated Outperform at ₹1,200 after FY26 annual-report analysis — all consistent with the view that Q4FY26 credit-cost improvement is holding.

**My own read:** BAF is one of India's genuinely great consumer-credit compounders, and the 1QFY27 AUM acceleration is a real positive. The swing factor is credit costs — Q4FY26 was one good quarter, not yet a trend; a second clean print in 1QFY27 formal results would meaningfully strengthen the bull case. Deven Choksey's FINAI operating-leverage thesis is the most interesting angle, but it needs to show up in actual cost-to-income compression before it deserves full valuation credit. Motilal's ₹1,000 Neutral is probably the honest near-term fair-value anchor; the ₹1,100–₹1,215 bull range prices the full normalisation. I'd accumulate on weakness rather than chase, with a 2-quarter validation window. The two things to watch: (1) 1QFY27 credit costs and NIM guidance in the formal result; (2) FINAI's measured impact on opex ratios — if cost-to-income is not compressing by end-FY27, the operating-leverage narrative fades.

DC|260504.change: Dated May-2026; Buy, PT ₹1,120 (per Trendlyne). No prior Deven Choksey entry in the library to compare against.
DC|260504.view:
Deven Choksey's "FINAI: Moving from narrative to operating leverage" framing is the most bullish thesis in the coverage — it bets explicitly that BAF's AI platform is crossing the threshold from marketing story to measurable cost and risk efficiency. PT ₹1,120 implies meaningful upside from where the stock has been trading.

If the FINAI thesis plays out in cost-to-income compression over the next 2–3 quarters, this is a defensible call. If the metric does not move, the narrative fades regardless of AUM growth. Worth tracking whether DC updates the view once Q1FY27 formal results are published — that will be the first real test of the operating-leverage claim.

MO|260430.change: PT cut ₹1,160→₹1,000 (vs prior Oct-2025 Motilal note per Trendlyne); Neutral maintained.
MO|260430.view:
Motilal's TP cut on the same Q4FY26 result day that PL upgraded is the most instructive data point in this result round — not a downgrade, but a meaningful reset of earnings/multiple expectations despite the "operationally healthy" characterisation. Staying Neutral at ₹1,000 after a ₹160 cut signals they acknowledge the improvement but see the stock as fair at best.

For a house typically constructive on leading financials, this reflects genuine caution about whether the credit-cost inflection is durable. The Neutral is arguably the most credible middle ground: neither dismissing the franchise nor buying the full re-rating story. I'd weight this view heavily — it is the freshest cautious read and the most quantitatively honest.

PL|260430.change: Upgraded to Buy on Q4FY26 results; PT ₹1,100. No prior Prabhudas Lilladhar entry in the library to compare the previous stance.
PL|260430.view:
PL's Q4FY26 upgrade is a classic catalyst-driven call — "healthy growth outlook with improving credit cost" after what had been a difficult few quarters. Upgrades into improving credit-cost data are often well-timed if the trend holds.

The risk is extrapolation from a single quarter. PT ₹1,100 is reasonable within the bull camp but not aggressive. I'd give this moderate weight — it adds to the Q4FY26 improvement signal chorus, but one quarter does not establish a trend. Q1FY27 formal results are the test.

BOB|260204.change: Dated Feb-2026; Buy, PT ₹1,193 (per Trendlyne). No prior BOB Capital entry in the library to compare. Note is now ~5 months old.
BOB|260204.view:
BOB Capital's Feb-2026 note flagged rising credit costs and accelerated provisioning — the same issues the entire market was grappling with — yet maintained Buy with the highest PT in the current set at ₹1,193. That is a look-through call: trust the franchise, treat the provisioning spike as a one-off.

Subsequent Q4FY26 data has partially validated this view, but the note predates both Q4FY26 results and the 1QFY27 pre-quarter AUM acceleration. At 5 months old it is the stalest directional anchor in the bull camp; treat it as indicative of the optimistic scenario rather than a current valuation anchor.

ICICI|251218.change: Upgraded to Buy, PT ₹1,180 (Dec-2025, per Trendlyne). No prior ICICI Direct entry in the library; this appears to be their initial captured call.
ICICI|251218.view:
ICICI Direct's Dec-2025 upgrade was made into stock weakness when credit-cost concerns were acute — buying into the dip on a high-quality franchise is a defensible strategy. However, this note is ~7 months old and pre-dates Q4FY26 results and the 1QFY27 pre-quarter update; the PT of ₹1,180 has not been refreshed for recent data.

Treat it as a directionally bullish signal from a house that turned constructive early, but not a current valuation anchor. Jefferies and JPMorgan now sit above ₹1,200, suggesting the Dec-2025 PT may be conservative relative to where the fresher bull camp has settled.

ICICI|251207.change: PT unchanged ₹1,050; Hold maintained — consistent with prior Nov-2025 note (Hold, ₹1,050 per Trendlyne). No change.
ICICI|251207.view:
ICICI Securities (distinct from ICICI Direct) is the cautious end of the non-bear camp: Hold at ₹1,050 is the lowest PT among houses that are not outright selling. Their note highlights the retail credit market share and AI-enabled process thesis — similar to Deven Choksey's angle — but arrives at a much more restrained conclusion.

The 7-month vintage makes this less immediately actionable; that said, a ₹1,050 Hold from a house that also recognises the FINAI story is a useful check on the more aggressive bull targets. It implies the operating-leverage thesis does not automatically justify ₹1,100–₹1,200 — the operating leverage has to actually materialise first.

Bajaj Finserv.summary:
Active coverage is thin and heavily weighted toward stale notes. **ICICI Direct** (upgraded Hold→Buy ₹2,150, May-2026) is the sole fresh signal. **Deven Choksey** (Hold ₹2,137, Nov-2025) is now 8 months old; **Emkay** (Buy ₹2,150, Oct-2024) and **Sharekhan** (Buy ₹2,350, Sep-2024) are nearly 20 months stale. The PT range across the four houses is ₹2,137–₹2,350, but most of that range reflects outdated views. Beyond this set, Kotak published a July-2026 note (Buy ₹2,430) explicitly citing an attractive look-through valuation for the Bajaj Finance franchise and a holding-company discount at near-peak 38% — the most constructive recent view available. The real debate is not whether the subsidiaries are strong (they are) but: (1) how much holdco discount is warranted given BAF's current credit-cycle position; (2) how quickly BAGIC recovers from its competitive FY26; and (3) whether BALIC's pivot from volume to profit is sustainable.

**My own read:** Bajaj Finserv is largely a leveraged play on Bajaj Finance — as BAF's credit costs normalise and AUM growth accelerates (1QFY27 pre-quarter showed 24% YoY), Finserv benefits with a holdco structure that can amplify the move. Kotak's near-peak discount observation is the key near-term entry signal: if BAF continues to re-rate, the holdco discount typically compresses, generating extra return. What I would watch more carefully than the sell-side does: (1) BAGIC's combined ratio and whether EOM/commission rule changes deliver actual margin relief; (2) BALIC's profit-focus pivot — if it sustains, insurance contributes positively rather than dragging; (3) the new digital ventures are a structural ROE drag until break-even, and the 1–3 year window is management's optimistic guide. ICICI Direct's ₹2,150 is the most credible near-term anchor; Kotak's ₹2,430 captures the upside if BAF fully re-rates and the holdco discount normalises.

ICICI|260502.change: Upgraded Hold→Buy; PT trimmed ₹2,200→₹2,150 (vs prior ICICI Direct entry dated 12 Nov 2025 per Trendlyne, which was a downgrade to Hold at ₹2,200).
ICICI|260502.view:
The unusual pairing — a rating upgrade alongside a small PT cut — signals that ICICI Direct reset its model (likely higher cost of equity or more conservative BAF growth assumptions) while judging that the stock's selloff since its November 2025 downgrade had gone too far. This is a valuation-recovery call, not a fundamental re-rating.

I find this the most intellectually honest current stance: it acknowledges the business is not flawless (hence the ₹2,200→₹2,150 cut) while recognising price had overcorrected. That said, ₹2,150 leaves limited margin of safety if BAF credit costs or BAGIC's combined ratio disappoint. Credible but not high-conviction — a "back to neutral from too-cautious" rather than a strong endorsement.

DC|251113.change: Downgraded Accumulate→Hold; PT cut ₹2,213→₹2,137 (vs prior Deven Choksey entry dated 05 Sep 2025 per Trendlyne, Accumulate ₹2,213).
DC|251113.view:
DC's Nov-2025 downgrade was triggered by Q2 sequential profitability moderation — a fair near-term read at the time. But this note is now over 8 months old and predates the more constructive May-2026 signals (ICICI Direct re-upgraded; Kotak published Buy ₹2,430 in Jul-2026).

A Hold at ₹2,137 is now the most cautious target in the set and likely stale relative to recent data. DC's coverage via Trendlyne tends to be earnings-reactive rather than thesis-driven, and the absence of an update through two full earnings cycles is itself a signal of limited strong directional conviction. Useful as the bear-case anchor; weight lightly relative to fresher views.

Emkay|241023.change: Dated Oct-2024; Buy, PT ₹2,150 unchanged from prior Emkay entry dated 13 Sep 2024 (per Trendlyne).
Emkay|241023.view: Emkay's Oct-2024 note was a one-event piece covering Allianz's exit from the insurance JVs — not a full thesis update. At nearly 20 months old it carries essentially no current signal. The ₹2,150 PT coincidentally matches ICICI Direct's current target but the alignment is stale — Emkay has not updated through the BAGIC competitive deterioration, the BALIC profit-focus pivot, or the new-ventures ramp discussion. Retain only as historical context; discard for any current view.

Sharekhan|240925.change: Dated Sep-2024; no prior Sharekhan entry in the library to compare.
Sharekhan|240925.view: Sharekhan's Sep-2024 note is the oldest in this coverage set — now nearly 22 months stale. The Buy at ₹2,350 predates every material development of the past 18 months: BAGIC's competitive pressure, BALIC's profit-focus pivot, the new-ventures ramp, and the holdco discount expansion. It carries no actionable signal today; retain only as historical context on where the optimistic end of consensus stood at the start of FY25.

Belrise Industries.summary:
Only **Jefferies** covers Belrise in the library, and they are unambiguously bullish — Buy with a freshly raised PT of ₹250 (from ₹215), implying ~19% upside from the May 2026 CMP. The Q4FY26 quarter was in-line rather than a beat: EBITDA +5% YoY, PAT +17% YoY, with margins slipping 90bp QoQ on one-time start-up costs in the new aero/defence subsidiary and acquisition expenses. New order wins from two 2W OEMs — one believed to be TVS — underpin the bull case. With a single covering house there is no cross-house debate; the real debate is internal to the thesis: whether the 26%/30% EBITDA/EPS CAGR guided for FY26–28E is achievable given ongoing margin volatility and early-stage subsidiary drag.

My own read: Belrise is a post-IPO 2W auto-ancillary riding the structural 2W upcycle, with entrenched positions in metal structural and fuel-delivery parts for Hero, Bajaj, and TVS. The franchise quality is sound, but the aero/defence pivot adds meaningful execution risk at a stage where the market is still price-discovering the stock. The 26% EBITDA CAGR assumption requires both new-order-win volume ramp and margin recovery after one-timers — plausible, but not low-risk. The two things I'd watch most: (1) FY27 EBITDA margin — management guided FY27 ≈ FY26, so any miss would signal the one-time cost was understated; (2) whether the aero/defence subsidiary starts generating visible order intake by H2 FY27 or remains a drag. Jefferies' ₹250 PT looks fair rather than aggressive at this juncture.

Jeff|260525.change: PT raised ₹215→₹250; Buy maintained. (Expanding Footprint note, 25 May 2026 — fine-tuned estimates post Q4FY26 results, new order wins from two 2W OEMs cited as the catalyst.)
Jeff|260525.view:
Jefferies presents a well-grounded, structurally bullish case. The Q4 margin dip (90bp QoQ) is clearly attributed to one-time items — aero/defence subsidiary start-up costs plus acquisition expenses — and management's FY27 margin guidance (≈ FY26) is a tangible commitment to hold them to. The 30% EPS CAGR target is contingent on those one-timers not recurring and new order ramp executing smoothly; achievable, but the bar is high.

The TVS order win, if confirmed, is meaningful — TVS is a quality anchor customer and adds revenue visibility. The PT raise from ₹215 to ₹250 is modest and incremental rather than a big re-rating call, which feels appropriate given the early stage of the aero/defence diversification. The main thing to stress-test in subsequent quarters: whether the 'one-time' subsidiary costs were truly non-recurring or whether they reappear as the subsidiary scales up.

Bharat Petroleum.summary:
The four houses in houseViews — **Geojit** (Hold/₹322, May-2026), **BOB Capital** (Buy/₹368, May-2026), **ICICI** (Buy/₹390, Aug-2025), and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Hold/₹333, Aug-2025) — span constructive to cautious, but ICICI and PL are ~11 months old. The pdfdata offers a fresh July 2026 Q1FY27 read: **Jefferies** (Buy/₹410, trimmed from ₹415) and **Nomura** (Buy/₹395, raised from ₹365) are the most constructive bulls; **JPMorgan** (OW/₹385, trimmed from an earlier ₹465) is positive but cautious; **CLSA** (Hold/₹270 — TP below CMP, effectively bearish) and **Kotak** (Reduce/₹325) are the sceptics. The Q1FY27 result was a significant beat vs feared: net loss ~₹40bn vs consensus/estimates of ₹126–₹156bn loss, driven by record refining GRM of USD 41.4/bbl and inventory gains, partly offset by large marketing losses. The OMC relief was short-lived — crude has since rebounded to ~USD 100/bbl (per Kotak), reigniting FY27 marketing-loss concerns. Geojit's May-2026 downgrade (Buy/₹400 → Hold/₹322) is the most recent action in houseViews and marks the moment even earlier domestic bulls capitulated. CLSA's TP of ₹270 (below CMP) and Nomura's own 'washout FY27, recovery FY28' framing bracket the range of fresh coverage. The critical disagreement: bears (CLSA, Kotak) price in prolonged deep marketing losses; bulls (Jefferies, Nomura, JPM) acknowledge the FY27 pain but anchor to an FY28 refining-upcycle and GRM normalisation.

My own read: BPCL is structurally the weakest OMC. No pricing power on petrol/diesel, more spot-crude exposure than peers (longer physical delivery cycles, higher premiums), a heavy capex cycle, and BPRL upstream impairments flagging exploration as a value drain. The Q1FY27 beat was real but one-off: record GRM at USD 41.4/bbl was materially assisted by inventory gains; sustainable GRM is probably USD 6–8/bbl in normalised conditions. With crude back at ~USD 100/bbl, the 2QFY27 marketing loss trajectory is likely to worsen again. CLSA's FY27 EPS cut (71% in an earlier note) is the honest number on the board. The government would need to announce a meaningful fuel retail price hike to rescue FY27 profitability — politically difficult near-term. The FY28 refining-upcycle thesis is possible but unplannable. The two things I'd watch: (1) any fuel retail price hike announcement — the single catalyst that changes the fundamental picture; (2) net-debt trajectory, where the jump from ₹105bn to ₹174bn in just one quarter (end-March to end-June per JPMorgan) signals the cash drain is accelerating faster than the market may appreciate. On a 6-12 month horizon, the bear case (CLSA/Kotak) is better grounded than the buy-heavy consensus implies.

Geojit|260525.change: Downgraded from Buy to Hold; PT cut ₹400→₹322 (Jan-2026 trendlyne entry was Buy/₹400; May-2026 is Hold/₹322). No pdfdata match for this report.
Geojit|260525.view:
Geojit's post-4QFY26 downgrade is a sensible capitulation to the marketing-loss reality. The walk from Buy/₹400 (January 2026) to Hold/₹322 (May 2026) in five months reflects how quickly the FY27 earnings outlook deteriorated as crude costs rose and marketing margins turned deeply negative. A PT of ₹322 implies limited upside and is effectively a park-and-watch call.

The downgrade is the most recent action in houseViews and the most useful directional signal of the set: even a domestic broker that was constructive heading into FY26 results has stepped aside. Without the full report in the library I can only assess this directionally — but it confirms the cautious shift and is consistent with where CLSA and Kotak sit in the fresher pdfdata.

BOB|260520.view:

Without the full report in the library, the analytical depth is unclear; the headline ('above expectations on better refining margins') suggests a results-reaction note rather than a structural thesis. The TP of ₹368 aligns broadly with JPMorgan (₹385) and Nomura (₹395).

The Q1FY27 pdfdata context is important here: the refining beat that BOB highlights was partly inventory-gain driven, and crude has since rallied back hard. Whether BOB's ₹368 model accounts for mean-reversion in GRM and the ongoing deep marketing losses is unknown. I'd treat this as directional noise consistent with the refining-beat narrative but not a call to weight heavily without the underlying assumptions.

ICICI|250815.change: Dated Aug-2025 (Q1FY26 result note); TP ₹390, Buy. No prior ICICI entry in the library to compare. Note is ~11 months old.
ICICI|250815.view:

The subsequent FY26 full-year results, the Q1FY27 net loss, CLSA's 71% FY27 EPS cut, and crude rebounding to ~USD 100/bbl have all materially worsened the picture vs the Aug-2025 thesis. The 'stronger marketing performance' that drove the Q1FY26 beat is a distant memory — marketing has been deeply negative for quarters since.

At TP ₹390, ICICI now holds the second-highest target among all tracked brokers (only Jefferies at ₹415 is higher), making this look especially aggressive relative to where the freshest coverage sits (CLSA ₹270, Kotak ₹325). Blue Jet Healthcare.summary:
The PDF library currently holds one house-view for Blue Jet Healthcare: **ICICI Securities** (Buy, PT ₹500, dated Feb-2026, Q3FY26 results). Trendlyne shows **Motilal Oswal** also published a near-simultaneous Feb-2026 note (PT ₹500, Buy) — "3Q impacted by pharma destocking; contrast remains stable" — both domestic houses converging on ₹500 after dramatic PT cuts from mid-2025 highs (MO had carried ₹1,100; ICICI ₹750). The broader sell-side derating reflects two consecutive quarterly misses from the PI/API segment: bempedoic acid revenue lumpiness and pharma destocking made Q2–Q3 FY26 look structurally impaired. The central debate is whether the disruption is a temporary inventory-cycle reset or evidence that PI/API contract visibility is inherently lumpy and customer-concentrated. Both houses say temporary; their 50%+ PT cuts from 2025 highs say they are no longer willing to pay for a full recovery until the numbers arrive.

My own read: Blue Jet's contrast media ABA HCl franchise is the quality core — genuinely differentiated chemistry know-how for iohexol/iopamidol intermediates, with real switching costs for global pharma customers. The PI/API segment is the problem: back-to-back guidance misses have eroded conviction that management can forecast contract timing reliably. The ₹500 consensus is not obviously cheap — at current levels it implies the market already prices in a decent Q1FY27 recovery. The stock is a "show me" situation and I would not add ahead of results. Two things to watch: (1) whether Q1FY27 PI/API revenues actually inflect — a third consecutive miss would drive a sharp re-rating lower; (2) whether the bempedoic acid (Esperion) franchise stabilises or faces further lifecycle risks. Until Q1 data arrives, ICICI's note is background context, not an actionable signal.

The ₹750→₹500 cut (−33%) was a substantial reset that aligned ICICI with the broader sell-side rethink after two consecutive PI/API shortfalls; retaining Buy signals the house believes the recovery is still on track.

As of today (Jul-2026) this note is approximately five months stale — it predates Q4FY26 results and any Q1FY27 signals. It is useful for understanding the Q3 diagnosis but carries little weight as a current positioning signal. The key question it raises — is the lumpiness structural? — remains open. I'd treat it as background and wait for the next quarterly update before acting on it.

CEAT.summary:
Among the five covered houses, the divide is sharp. **MO** (Buy, TP ₹4,228) argues that the tyre industry will collectively push through sufficient price hikes to protect margins — pricing discipline is the core bull assumption. **ICICI** (Buy, TP ₹4,700) upgraded from Hold in January 2026, but that note predates the commodity-inflation surge by several months and should be read cautiously. **AR** (Hold, TP ₹3,850) occupies the careful middle: the headline “steep inflationary pressure ahead; price hike crucial” correctly names the risk without a directional verdict. **Emkay** (Reduce, TP ₹3,600) is the most candid bear — having been Buy at ₹4,600 in Sep 2025 on the Camso acquisition story, it reversed entirely to Reduce in April 2026 on all-time-high RM prices, the most meaningful call-change in the set. **PL** (Hold, TP ₹3,240, May 2025) is stale by over a year, predating both Camso and the current RM cycle; discount it entirely. The live target range (stripping PL) is ₹3,600–₹4,700 — unusually wide for a mid-cap tyre name. The real debate: 1QFY27 EBITDA margins compressed to ~8.5% (down ~560 bps QoQ) as the RM basket rose ~16–18% QoQ; CEAT implemented 6–7% replacement and 3–4% OEM price hikes, but whether these suffice through H1FY27 — and whether Camso turns from drag to contributor — is the unresolved question.

My own read: CEAT is executing a genuine strategic pivot toward OHT with Camso and toward international revenues, but the timing of these multi-year investments collides badly with a commodity cost spike. Camso is an EPS drag near-term (adverse currency on forex loans, slower brand-transfer ramp); the India standalone business is growing volumes strongly but cannot shield margins against a ~20% RM basket move. CEAT historically earns thinner returns than Apollo or MRF, giving it less buffer. Emkay’s downgrade carries the most credibility in the current set — the RM headwind is real and ICICI’s bull case is pre-shock. MO’s pricing-discipline thesis is plausible but assumes Apollo and MRF behave cooperatively; any competitive miscue flips the calculus. Two things to watch above all: (1) the September-quarter EBITDA margin, which will reveal whether price-hike pass-through held; (2) Camso’s quarterly revenue and margin contribution, since both were weak in 1Q on currency and brand-transition pressure.

AR|260430.change: No prior Anand Rathi entry in the library — cannot derive a change. Hold TP ₹3,850 per this note.
AR|260430.view:
AR’s Hold at ₹3,850 is the sensible middle-ground stance: the headline “steep inflationary pressure ahead; price hike crucial” correctly names the key risk without making a directional call on whether management will execute. Limited source text is available. The TP of ₹3,850 sits between the bull camp (₹4,228–₹4,700) and the bear (₹3,600), essentially pricing in partial but not full margin recovery.

For AR to upgrade, evidence would need to emerge that replacement-market hikes flowed through to realizations without volume attrition. For a downgrade to Reduce, the Sep-quarter print would need to show continued compression. Until then, Hold is defensible and the ₹3,850 level is a reasonable mid-point anchor.

Emkay|260429.change: Downgraded Buy→Reduce; PT cut ₹4,600→₹3,600 (prior: Emkay Buy ₹4,600, Sep 2025).
Emkay|260429.view:
Emkay’s downgrade from Buy to Reduce is the starkest call-change in the covered set — the PT dropped ₹1,000 and the rating reversed from its post-Camso-acquisition bull stance in Sep 2025. The thesis flip is unambiguous: all-time-high RM prices make H1FY27 a profitability trough, and the prior bull case (Camso as a structural re-rating catalyst) does not survive a simultaneous RM shock during the integration phase.

I find this the most grounded bear call. A house that was bullish on the strategic thesis has repriced for near-term reality. The ₹3,600 Reduce is defensible if margins stay compressed through H1FY27 — which the July-reported 1Q data (EBITDA -6% YoY, margin 8.5%) confirms is the trajectory. The key risk to Emkay’s call: if mid-year price hikes pass through more cleanly than expected, a sharp re-rating is possible. But right now Emkay has the more honest model.

MO|260429.change: Buy TP ₹4,228; first Motilal Oswal entry captured in the library — no prior to compare.
MO|260429.view:
MO’s Buy rests on an industry-level thesis: when the tyre sector faces synchronised RM inflation, established players tend to move on pricing together, absorbing the hit temporarily but restoring margins faster than the market fears. “Pricing discipline” is the operative phrase and it is empirically reasonable for the Indian replacement tyre market, which is moderately oligopolistic.

The risk is that this RM move is larger than usual (basket up ~20% YoY in 1Q) and Camso integration adds complexity that may prevent CEAT from pricing as aggressively as a pure domestic player. MO’s ₹4,228 target is plausible mid-cycle but rests on an industry-behaviour assumption worth monitoring quarter by quarter — any pricing defection by Apollo or MRF changes the calculus for CEAT.

ICICI|260120.change: Upgraded Hold→Buy; PT raised ₹3,500→₹4,700 (prior: ICICI Hold ₹3,500, Sep 2025).
ICICI|260120.view:
ICICI upgraded CEAT sharply in January 2026 — from Hold ₹3,500 to Buy ₹4,700, a 34% PT jump — citing healthy demand momentum and flagging Camso ramp-up as the key monitorable. At the time, with volumes running well and Camso freshly acquired, this was a credible re-rating call.

However, this note is now six months old and predates the commodity-inflation shock that dominated the April–July 2026 earnings season. The ₹4,700 Buy target is the most optimistic in the active set and reflects pre-RM-shock assumptions. ICICI’s “Camso monitorable” has since become a story of adverse currency on forex loans and a weak quarterly contribution. Whether ICICI has privately revised its view is unknown; as published, this is the stalest live bull call after PL.

PL|250502.change: Hold TP ₹3,240 per trendlyne; dated May 2025 — over a year old. No prior PL entry to compare.
PL|250502.view: PL’s May 2025 Hold at ₹3,240 is the oldest note in the group and carries no current signal. The Q4FY25 results context has been superseded by two additional earnings seasons; the Camso acquisition, Vision 2031 targets, and the RM inflation cycle all postdate this note. No weight should be assigned to ₹3,240 as a reference price in the current debate.

CMS Info Systems.summary:
Only **Jefferies** covers CMS Info Systems in the local library, with a June 2026 **Buy** and no disclosed target price. The captured note is Jefferies' India Financial Daily — a daily market digest — rather than a dedicated CMS initiation or update, so the paragraph itself is broad market colour (Nifty/Bank Nifty moves) rather than company-specific analysis. With a single house and no substantive price-target data, there is nothing to cross-house compare; coverage in the library is effectively a placeholder.

**My own read:** CMS Info Systems occupies a comfortable quasi-duopoly in India's outsourced cash-management and ATM services market, alongside Brinks. The franchise is stickier than it looks — PSU bank outsourcing relationships are long-cycle and sticky, and recertification costs create meaningful switching friction. The structural debate is whether UPI-driven cash displacement will eventually cap ATM deployment economics; so far the evidence is nuanced — total ATM count is still growing in Tier 3–5 geographies even as urban cash withdrawals flatten. The more interesting watch is CMS's pivot away from ATM-only revenue toward managed services, digital logistics (secure currency chests), and non-ATM vault management. That mix-shift is the key re-rating lever. I'd watch non-ATM revenue share (the company targets ~30%+ of revenue), net ATM additions per quarter, and FCF conversion — this is a capital-light model and any deterioration in working capital or rise in security incident costs would be a red flag. At current valuations (typically 15–18× forward earnings), the stock prices in steady-state rather than a growth re-rating, which is fair given the secular headwinds but could be conservative if the services pivot accelerates.

Cartrade Tech.summary:
Only one house in the library covers Cartrade Tech with a current note: **Kotak** (2 Jun 2026), which executed a dramatic **Sell→Buy flip**, raising its fair value from ₹1,860 to ₹2,300. There is no cross-house debate to map — the view is a single-broker call. The upgrade rests on two pillars: a materially higher OLX valuation (described as the primary driver, on expectations of steady GMV growth, improving monetisation, and margin expansion) and the belief that Cartrade's deep dealer database and value-added offerings create a moat against AI disruption. The stock had already sold off sharply YTD before the note, so this is partly a re-rating call after a de-rating. No bear or neutral house is represented in the library.

My own read: Cartrade sits at a genuinely interesting intersection — a structurally growing India used-car and 2W market on one side, and real disruption risk from AI-driven discovery and price transparency on the other. Kotak's upgrade timing is understandable after the YTD sell-off, but the OLX re-rating as the primary driver deserves scrutiny: OLX India's classifieds business has historically been a loss-absorbing asset, and 'steady monetisation improvement' is a forward bet, not a demonstrated track record. The AI risk to classified platforms is not theoretical — it has already compressed multiples at analogous Western names, and Cartrade's dealer data moat is a plausible but unproven defence in an environment of rising price transparency. I would land cautiously bullish on the franchise quality but would want to see OLX take-rate expansion in actuals before underwriting the full ₹2,300 FV. Key watches: (1) OLX revenue yield trajectory vs GMV; (2) signs of AI-native used-car discovery platforms gaining dealer or consumer traction; (3) whether Cartrade's value-added services (financing, insurance, inspection) grow as a share of mix — that, more than classifieds listings, is the durable moat.

Kotak|260602.change: PT raised ₹1,860→₹2,300; upgraded to Buy from Sell (per report summary — pdfdata prevCall is null but the note text explicitly states the prior call was Sell).
Kotak|260602.view:
Kotak's Sell→Buy flip after the YTD de-rating is the defining feature of this note. The stated primary rationale is a higher OLX valuation — not a change in the core Cartrade classifieds thesis — which means this is partly a sum-of-the-parts re-rating trade rather than a fundamental conviction shift on Cartrade's own business.

The OLX angle is credible if monetisation inflects, but worth stress-testing: OLX India has spent years burning cash to build GMV, and the market-implied value Kotak is now underwriting is a significant step-up. The secondary pillar — AI disruption risk is manageable given the dealer database — is asserted rather than quantified, and the history of classifieds platforms globally suggests this risk can crystallise faster than incumbents expect. Kotak's call is a reasonable contrarian position at a depressed entry, but the conviction level implied by flipping from Sell to Buy in one note warrants monitoring for follow-through in subsequent updates.

Colgate-Palmolive (India).summary:
All seven current houseViews for Colgate-Palmolive (India) are **stale**: the freshest is **MO** (Jan 2026, Buy ₹2,450); the rest range from Jul to Nov 2025. Five houses are bullish (**MO** Buy ₹2,450, **Geojit** Buy ₹2,550, **DC** Accumulate ₹2,429, **Axis** Buy ₹2,660, **Sharekhan** Buy ₹2,829); **PL** is neutral (Hold ₹2,453); **ICICI** is the lone bear (Sell ₹1,800). The ₹1,029 spread between ICICI and Sharekhan reflects a vintage disagreement — in May 2025, as volumes were soft and the GST disruption was biting, ICICI downgraded while others saw a valuation entry point. A material refresh is imminent: pdfdata already contains Q1FY27 result notes from **Jefferies** (Buy ₹2,650, raised from ₹2,600), **JPMorgan** (Neutral ₹2,250), **Nomura** (Buy ₹2,550), **CLSA** (Hold ₹1,974), **Goldman Sachs** (Sell ₹2,050), and **Kotak** (Reduce ₹2,075) — all dated July 29–30, 2026 — but none have updated the houseViews display yet. Once they do, the bearish camp (CLSA, Goldman, Kotak) will be visible alongside the bulls and the spread will narrow considerably from the current stale picture.

My own read: Colgate India is a genuinely high-quality franchise — ~50%+ oral-care market share, consistent FCF, and no credible competitor threatening the toothpaste moat. Q1FY27 data (12% revenue growth, 8.5% volume growth in toothpaste) confirms the FY26 weakness was real but not structural: GST distribution disruption and urban softness have faded. The tension is between brand investment and margin delivery — management deliberately ran A&P up 34% YoY in Q1FY27, absorbing the gross-margin recovery and keeping EBITDA margins under pressure (~145 bps YoY decline per Nomura pdfdata). The inverted-duty structure (~160 bps drag per Kotak) requires a GST Council fix not in management's control. At ~₹2,135 (per July pdfdata), the stock trades at a meaningful premium to other FMCG names on a two-year revenue CAGR basis (~3.5% per Goldman Sachs and Kotak) — the market is already pricing in the FY27 recovery. I would wait for Q2FY27 volumes before getting constructive: if the 8.5% trend holds, the bull case earns its multiple; if it mean-reverts, Kotak's Reduce at ₹2,075 (fresh July 30) looks right. Sharekhan's ₹2,829 from May 2025 is wishful thinking at current earnings trajectories.

But ₹2,450 as a target is six months stale; fresh pdfdata puts post-Q1FY27 bull targets at ₹2,550–₹2,650 and the bears at ₹1,974–₹2,075. Cummins India.summary:
With **Jefferies**, **JPMorgan**, **Kotak**, and **Nomura** no longer in the active houseViews, the current panel has shrunk to four voices — and two of them are materially stale. **Geojit** (Buy, PT ₹6,160, May-26) is the sole bull, betting on export-growth acceleration and DC genset demand compounding. **IDBI Capital** (Sell, PT ₹5,046, May-26) is the bear, having paradoxically raised its PT from ₹4,401 even while downgrading to Sell — signalling that fundamentals improved but the stock ran past fair value. **PL** (Hold, ₹3,895, Aug-25) and **ICICI** (Hold, ₹2,900, Feb-25) are 10 and 17 months stale respectively and have been overtaken by events. The live debate is therefore thin: Geojit's DC-and-export optimism vs IDBI's overvaluation thesis, with no fresh neutral voice to arbitrate. For richer context, **Kotak**'s Jul-2026 annual-report note (Reduce, PT ₹5,700; in the PDF library but outside the active panel) remains the most current and analytically thorough view — it acknowledges export acceleration as real but flags non-HHP powergen share loss as a structural concern the DC narrative is partially masking.

My own read: Cummins India is a genuinely high-quality franchise — dominant in industrial power generation, with captive access to Cummins Inc technology and pricing power that smaller peers cannot match. The DC genset theme is real and structural. But the multiple has re-rated hard, and the four remaining houseView notes leave a large analytical gap in the middle. Drawing on the broader library (the May-26 broker cluster now absent from the panel, Kotak's Jul-26 annual-report analysis), the pattern is consistent: fundamental upgrades paired with rating caution, meaning the business is getting better but the stock has priced it in aggressively. I'd be in the cautious-neutral camp: hold for franchise quality, resist chasing. The two things I'd watch most are (1) whether DC revenue sustains above 15% of consolidated sales and (2) non-HHP powergen order intake — if core domestic genset share is eroding to Kirloskar and others, the margin of safety at current multiples is thin.

IDBI|260529.change: Downgraded Hold→Sell (May-26); PT raised ₹4,401→₹5,046 (prior Trendlyne entry: Hold/₹4,401, Nov-2025).
IDBI|260529.view:
IDBI's downgrade paired with a PT raise is a clean valuation call: their revised fair value moved up (acknowledging better fundamentals) but the stock moved even further, making the risk-reward unattractive. At ₹5,046 they were likely below the stock price at time of writing — a conviction Sell, not just a trim.

No report in the local library; the specific earnings model is inaccessible. As the sole Sell in the active houseViews, this is the call worth stress-testing. The core question it poses: has the DC and export re-rating been fully priced? Kotak's Jul-2026 note (outside the panel) maintained a Reduce at ₹5,700 even after the annual report confirmed export acceleration — suggesting IDBI's lower ₹5,046 floor sits at the conservative end of a broadly cautious institutional consensus, not as an isolated outlier.

Geojit|260507.change: Upgraded to Buy with PT ₹6,160 (May-2026); no prior Geojit entry in the library to compare.
Geojit|260507.view:
Geojit's Buy was issued in early May 2026, before the late-May cluster of post-Q4 results reports from other brokers. No report is in the local library. At ₹6,160 it is the most bullish PT in the active set and implies the DC-and-export thesis plays out in full.

I would not weight it heavily without the underlying model or a more recent refresh. The directional Buy aligns with a structural view on DC demand, but the specific PT cannot be independently verified. Treat as the bull-case ceiling for the current range rather than a primary conviction anchor.

PL|250808.change: Downgraded Buy→Hold (Aug-25); PT raised ₹3,646→₹3,895 (prior Trendlyne entry: Buy/₹3,646, May-2025).
PL|250808.view: Very stale. PL's Aug-2025 Hold at ₹3,895 pre-dates the DC narrative crystallising and the stock's major re-rating. PL raised the PT while downgrading the rating — the same structural pattern as IDBI a year later — but at levels far below even the current bear case of ₹5,046. This note has no actionable value for current positioning and should be disregarded until PL issues a refreshed view.

ICICI|250210.change: Hold with PT ₹2,900 (Feb-2025); no prior ICICI entry to compare — first captured note.
ICICI|250210.view: Extremely stale and not actionable. ICICI's Feb-2025 Hold at ₹2,900 was written before CPCB IV+ ramp, before DC emerged as a meaningful revenue segment, and before the stock's substantial re-rating. The PT is far below every other house in the current set. Discard entirely for current analysis; it serves only as a historical reference for where institutional caution was anchored 17 months ago.

Cyient.summary:
Coverage is split: **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹1,100, Jun-2026) and **Geojit** (Buy, PT ₹1,159, Mar-2026) are constructive; **Emkay** (Sell, PT ₹1,150, Oct-2025) and **Kotak** (Reduce, PT ₹880, Jun-2026) are negative; **IDBI** (Hold, PT ₹1,015, Apr-2026) and **ICICI** (Hold, PT ₹1,190, Apr-2025 — stale) sit in the middle. Published targets cluster ₹880–₹1,190. The real fault line is the Tao Digital acquisition (US$218 mn, ~11–12× FY2028E EBITDA): JPMorgan frames it as TAM expansion into data engineering and software product engineering, cross-sell potential, and a shift toward larger annuity deals; Kotak is skeptical, calling it a gap-filler whose value depends entirely on execution. IDBI's sharp downgrade — Buy at ₹1,307 in Jan-2026 → Hold at ₹1,015 by Apr-2026 — reflects earnings disappointment before the deal, and their post-acquisition stance is not yet updated. Emkay's Oct-2025 Sell at ₹1,150 predates the acquisition and is stale on that dimension. Geojit's upgrade to Buy in Mar-2026 looks premature given the deal announcement came later.

My own read: Cyient's core ER&D franchise (aerospace/defence, transportation, communications) is solid but cyclically lumpy and structurally under pressure as clients in-source more digital work. The Tao Digital deal is strategically sensible — DET needed a credible digital/data engineering capability to stay relevant — but US$218 mn at 11–12× forward EBITDA is not a bargain for an asset that still needs to prove cross-sell traction. The bears are right to flag execution risk; the bulls are right that standing still was not an option. At ~₹908 (per JPMorgan's 29-May note), the stock prices in modest execution success, which is a reasonable risk/reward only if integration milestones are on track. I'd watch: (1) deal integration milestones and revenue synergies in H1 FY2027, (2) whether the aerospace/defence pipeline converts (lumpy, but the order book matters a lot), and (3) margin trajectory as Tao's cost base is absorbed. IDBI's downgrade trajectory — from ₹1,307 to ₹1,015 in three months — is the most informative data point in the coverage: it reflects a company that missed near-term expectations hard, not just a re-rating. I'd not chase here without evidence of execution.

IDBI|260424.change: Downgraded from Buy (PT ₹1,307, Jan-2026) to Hold (PT ₹1,015) on 24 Apr 2026 — a sharp cut of ₹292 on the target and a full ratings step-down.
IDBI|260424.view:
This is the most telling move in the coverage set. A Buy-to-Hold downgrade with the target slashed 22% in three months signals that Q3/Q4 results missed IDBI's expectations materially, not just marginally. IDBI was the most bullish house at ₹1,307 and is now the most cautious among non-Sell raters. The downgrade predates the Tao Digital announcement (Jun-2026), so it is a pure earnings call — execution on the core ER&D business is what disappointed.

The current Hold at ₹1,015 means IDBI sees limited near-term upside from ~₹908 CMP. Worth watching whether IDBI updates post-acquisition: if they stay at Hold/₹1,015 despite the deal, that's a meaningful signal that the market is likely already pricing in deal optionality. If they re-initiate higher, the logic would need to rest on cross-sell acceleration — which is hard to verify before FY2027 results.

Geojit|260319.change: Upgraded to Buy (PT ₹1,159) on 19 Mar 2026; no prior Geojit entry in the library to compare.
Geojit|260319.view:
Geojit's Mar-2026 upgrade to Buy at ₹1,159 came before the Tao Digital deal announcement in June. The thesis was presumably a recovery in core ER&D growth after the weak patches in H1 FY2026. At ₹908 CMP, ₹1,159 implies ~28% upside — meaningful, but Geojit is a smaller broker and this upgrade is now five months stale, predating the deal's risk/reward shift.

I'd discount this view somewhat: it doesn't incorporate the acquisition's dilution/leverage effects, and the subsequent IDBI downgrade (a more active tracker) suggests the fundamental picture between Mar and Apr worsened. Geojit has not updated since March, which is a gap.

Emkay|251017.change: Sell rating with PT ₹1,150 as of Oct 2025; no prior Emkay entry to compare. Dated Oct-2025 — over seven months old.
Emkay|251017.view:
Emkay's Oct-2025 Sell at ₹1,150 (headline: 'Steady operating performance; ambitious growth ahead') is a contradiction in terms — a Sell at a target above the then-prevailing price, paired with 'steady' operations and 'ambitious' guidance. This typically signals concern about valuation and execution credibility rather than a fundamental collapse thesis.

The note is now materially stale: it predates the Q3/Q4 disappointment that prompted IDBI's downgrade, and it entirely predates the Tao Digital acquisition. Emkay's current view on the deal is unknown. The Sell label should be interpreted in the Oct-2025 context only — it is not an active, informed bear call on the current situation. I would not rely on this for current positioning.

ICICI|250425.change: Downgraded to Hold (PT ₹1,190) on 25 Apr 2025; no prior ICICI entry to compare. Dated Apr-2025 — over 13 months old, substantially stale.
ICICI|250425.view:
ICICI's Apr-2025 Hold at ₹1,190 is the oldest and most stale note in the set. It predates the significant earnings deterioration (IDBI's downgrade implies Q3/Q4 FY2026 missed hard), and it predates the Tao Digital deal entirely. A Hold at ₹1,190 from over a year ago is not a live view.

The only informational value here is that ICICI was already cautious (downgraded to Hold) even in the relatively benign Apr-2025 environment. If ICICI has not put out a fresh note after the Q4 results or the acquisition, that itself is a signal — they may not have enough conviction to update. I would assign near-zero weight to this for current analysis.

Dalmia Bharat.summary:
The broker community is split wide on Dalmia Bharat, with a nearly ₹700 spread in price targets across the full coverage set. The April 2026 Q4FY26 result notes — BOB (freshly upgraded Hold, TP ₹2,110), PL (Buy, TP ₹2,287), MO (Buy, TP ₹2,230) — are the latest in the houseViews, but the local PDF library's 1QFY27 crop from late July 2026 shows an even more bifurcated picture: **Nomura** most bullish (Buy, TP ₹2,500), **CLSA** Outperform (₹2,250), **Goldman Sachs** Buy (₹1,980), while **JPMorgan** and **Morgan Stanley** both sit at Neutral/Underweight ₹1,800 and **Kotak** is Reduce at ₹1,850. BOB notably broke from a persistent Sell stance (held since mid-2025) to upgrade to Hold in April 2026, citing reasonable valuations rather than a thesis change; PL and MO have stayed bullish throughout. The central debate: whether Dalmia's aggressive capacity expansion — JPA acquisition plus a 110–130mt target by FY31 from a ~55mt base — can deliver above-industry volume growth, or whether sector-wide overcapacity, integration risk, and muted cement pricing leave the upside capped.

My own read: Dalmia is a well-run operator with a defensible franchise in East/South India, but the July 2026 CMP (~₹1,808 per Goldman Sachs) is sitting right at the bear-camp TPs (Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Kotak all at ₹1,800–₹1,850), which limits near-term downside but also means the bull case requires near-flawless execution to justify premium TPs. The JPA acquisition is strategically sound — central India is an attractive region — but cement companies have a long history of over-optimistic capacity ramp timelines, and central-region pricing dynamics differ from Dalmia's home turf in East/South. The 9% YoY volume growth in 1QFY27 is an early positive data point. I'd watch two things: (1) whether volume growth sustains above 7–8% through FY27 as the JPA assets ramp, and (2) whether EBITDA/t holds above ₹1,000 as new supply comes online. At current levels this is a more binary setup than the Neutral/Hold cluster implies.

BOB|260429.change: Upgraded Sell→Hold, TP raised ₹2,087→₹2,110. Prior note was Oct 2025 (Sell, TP ₹2,087); BOB had been Sell since at least Jul 2025 (TP ₹1,926).
BOB|260429.view: BOB's upgrade marks a meaningful shift after a stubborn Sell — they were the bearish outlier against a largely bullish peer group through 2025. The Hold at ₹2,110 reads as a valuation-driven call ("reasonable valuations" was the stated rationale) rather than a conviction turn: structural concerns remain, but the stock has derated enough to price them in. BOB's track record on Dalmia deserves respect — their Sell calls through 2025 captured a period of disappointing volume delivery that the Buy camp underweighted. The current Hold leaves open a two-way path: if JPA integration shows early execution upside, BOB has the analytical honesty to upgrade further; if volumes disappoint or cement pricing rolls, a return to Sell is plausible. Treat this as a cautious "no longer short the story" rather than a positive endorsement.

PL|260429.change: No prior PL report for Dalmia Bharat in the library; this appears to be their first captured note. Buy, TP ₹2,287.
PL|260429.view: PL's Buy with TP ₹2,287 (implying ~26% upside vs ~₹1,808 CMP as of late July 2026) is anchored on the Q4FY26 cost-led beat, flagging volume recovery as the critical upcoming catalyst. The framing is reasonable — cost improvement (WHR substitution, petcoke mix optimisation) is structural and provides an earnings floor even if volume recovery lags. However, the TP sits above the cluster of July 2026 1QFY27 notes from more cautious brokers, suggesting PL may be extrapolating a smoother volume and margin trajectory than the bears see. The key risk: JPA integration into central India, where competitive dynamics and pricing are less favourable than Dalmia's traditional East/South base. If volume recovery takes more than a quarter or two to materialise, the TP becomes hard to justify on a medium-term horizon.

MO|260428.change: Buy maintained. TP cut ₹2,570→₹2,230 (vs Feb 2026 note at TP ₹2,570, itself down from ₹2,660 in Jul 2025).
MO|260428.view: MO has been a persistent bull but has trimmed the TP three times in 12 months — ₹2,660 (Jul 2025) → ₹2,570 (Jan/Feb 2026) → ₹2,230 (Apr 2026) — a cumulative 16% reduction while maintaining the Buy. That trajectory is a soft warning: even the bull camp is recalibrating to a lower earnings path than originally modeled. The "muted volume growth" characterisation in the Q4FY26 note is honest, and cost control is clearly doing the heavy lifting for now. MO's Buy conviction is not unreasonable given the operating leverage potential (high fixed costs mean volume upside drops steeply to EBITDA), but the serial TP cuts suggest consensus earnings estimates have been falling and may not yet be bottomed. Treat MO's Buy as medium-conviction — the thesis is intact but the volume catalyst timeline keeps getting pushed. Watch 1H FY27 volume numbers closely.

Deepak Nitrite.summary:
Coverage is uniformly bearish to cautious — no house in the set has issued a Buy. **PL** issued the freshest note (Apr 2026, Reduce, TP ₹1,354) after downgrading from Hold (Feb 2026, TP ₹1,673), citing new polycarbonate capacity additions from domestic and Chinese competitors as a structural threat to **Deepak Phenolics** margins. **MO** downgraded to Sell in Aug 2025 (TP ₹1,630), moving early and directionally correctly. **ICICI** is the lone Hold (TP ₹1,950, Aug 2025) — but that note is now nearly a year stale. The ₹596 spread between ICICI's Hold target and PL's current Reduce TP largely reflects staleness: PL's sequential TP trajectory (₹1,883 Aug-25 → ₹1,673 Feb-26 → ₹1,354 Apr-26) maps a steady earnings deterioration that ICICI's dated note has not yet reflected. The one potential counterweight is ICICI's thesis that new capex commissioning would aid H2FY26 earnings — a call that PL's April 2026 capacity-threat analysis appears to have overtaken.

My own read: Deepak Nitrite is in the deepest phase of a sector downswing where the margin compression looks structural rather than cyclical. The polycarbonate/phenol business (Deepak Phenolics) is the dominant P&L driver, and the competitive dynamics have worsened — more Indian and Chinese PC capacity is coming into a market where demand growth is at best moderate. New capex diversification is the bull case for FY27+, but specialty chemical recovery timelines tend to be optimistic and depend on supply-side discipline that is hard to predict. PL's successive TP cuts suggest sell-side earnings models are still being revised down, not bottomed. The stock is a candidate for a value trap — cheap optically but fundamentally still deteriorating. I'd watch: (1) global phenol/acetone spreads as the leading indicator for Deepak Phenolics margins, and (2) any Indian PC tariff action that could provide domestic producers competitive breathing room.

PL|260413.change: Downgraded Hold→Reduce; TP cut ₹1,673→₹1,354 (from Feb 2026 Hold note at TP ₹1,673, itself down from ₹1,883 in Aug 2025).
PL|260413.view: PL's downgrade to Reduce is the most substantive recent call in the set — data-driven and triggered by identifiable new capacity additions rather than a diffuse bearish macro. The 19% TP cut signals a meaningful earnings revision, not a minor trim. PL has been consistently ahead of the curve in turning negative on Deepak Nitrite: they moved Hold→Sell/Reduce before the broader consensus updated, and their serial cuts suggest a clearer model of the phenol/PC supply chain than peers carry. The risk to the Reduce thesis: a faster-than-expected shakeout of new capacity (Chinese chemical project cancellations, or Indian PC demand accelerating via EV/electronics applications). Until there is concrete evidence of either, PL's Reduce is the most credible current call in the set, and the ₹1,354 TP may prove directionally right even if the exact level proves conservative or aggressive depending on cycle timing.

MO|250815.change: No prior MO report in the library to compare. Sole entry: Sell, TP ₹1,630, Aug 2025.
MO|250815.view: MO's Sell from August 2025 was directionally correct — they moved first among the major houses and PL's subsequent downgrade trajectory confirms the bearish read. However, the TP of ₹1,630 is now ~11 months old; PL's April 2026 Reduce target of ₹1,354 implies the stock has further to fall than MO's estimate captured. If MO has not published an update in nearly a year, the ₹1,630 TP is almost certainly stale relative to current fundamentals. Treat this as directional confirmation of the bearish consensus rather than an actionable current target. An updated MO note — especially after FY27 Q1 results — would be the most informative next read for this name.

ICICI|250815.change: Hold maintained; TP cut ₹2,000→₹1,950 (vs May 2025 note at TP ₹2,000).
ICICI|250815.view: ICICI's Hold at TP ₹1,950 from August 2025 is the lone outlier in an otherwise bearish coverage set, and the note is now nearly a year stale. The thesis — "new capex commissioning should aid earnings growth in H2" — was a reasonable call at the time, but PL's April 2026 downgrade post-Q3FY26 results suggests either the H2FY26 improvement was more muted than hoped, or the new competitor capacity additions have overwhelmed any internal capex benefit. ICICI's TP of ₹1,950 vs PL's current ₹1,354 is a ₹596 gap — the bulk of which likely reflects missing the post-August 2025 earnings deterioration rather than a genuine analytical disagreement. I'd significantly discount this as a current actionable view. If ICICI has been sitting quietly on a Hold for 11+ months without an update, that itself is a mildly bearish signal about their conviction.

Divi's Laboratories.summary:
Seven houses occupy the houseViews panel — 3 constructive (PL Accumulate, DC Accumulate, Sharekhan Buy) / 3 neutral (BOB Hold, Geojit Hold, MO Neutral) / 1 bear (ICICI Sell) — but the coverage is heavily time-lagged. As of August 2026, Divi's trades ~₹8,057 (CMP per the Aug-2026 Goldman Sachs note), which sits **above every price target on this panel** (range: ₹5,400–₹7,500). The two freshest entries — **PL** (Accumulate, ₹6,900) and **BOB** (Hold, ₹7,500), both May-2026 — predate Q1FY27 results, which delivered a blowout: revenue +28%, EBITDA +72% YoY, custom synthesis (CS) +45% YoY and now 60% of revenue. **DC** and **ICICI** are Nov-2025 vintage; **MO** (Neutral, ₹6,200) is Feb-2025 vintage — 18 months old; **Sharekhan** (Buy, ₹6,812) from Nov-2024 is the oldest. The live post-Q1FY27 debate is captured in recently ingested local PDFs not yet reflected here: **Goldman Sachs** (Buy, TP ₹9,070, Aug-2026) views the CS surge as structural, while **Kotak** (Sell, TP ₹6,925 — raised from ₹5,850 but still bearish, Aug-2026) flags validation-batch lumps and margin durability risk. The upshot: the constructive camp has been directionally vindicated, every bear is deeply offside on price, and the real question is whether Q1FY27’s margin step-up is durable or a lumpy one-quarter phenomenon.

My own read: Q1FY27 settled the CS-transition debate in Divi’s favour — this reads structural, not a single-shipment flush. The GS TP of ₹9,070 is probably the right upside reference now; this panel’s targets are a rearview mirror. The credible remaining bear thesis — best articulated by Kotak — rests on two things: validation-batch timing inflating the CS gross margin, and the Entresto EU lifecycle eventually capping the largest CS revenue stream. On the first: Kotak’s own note acknowledges the gross margin surge ‘may not be entirely sustainable due to lumpy sales’ — a fair caveat, and Q2FY27 margins will be the real test. On the second: the same Kotak note observes that client engagement across multiple projects (including peptides at various stages) ‘stays high’ — which partially undermines the staleness-of-pipeline story the bears keep telling. At ₹8,057 the stock prices a clean CS ramp and early peptide optionality with limited room for execution slips. Watch: (1) Q2FY27 CS EBITDA margins — whether they sustain the Q1 step-up or revert toward prior-quarter levels; (2) any management colour on Entresto EU contract volumes, which remain the single largest identifiable downside risk to consensus.

PL|260525.change: PT raised ₹6,550→₹6,900 vs prior Aug-2025 note (per trendlyne); Accumulate maintained.
PL|260525.view: PL’s Q4FY26 result update acknowledges the EBITDA miss candidly (‘miss; Peptide opportunities key for growth’) but holds Accumulate, correctly identifying peptide CS as the next growth leg. The ₹6,900 target was measured at the time and is now well below CMP — PL will need a fresh note post-Q1FY27. The modest ₹6,550→₹6,900 lift reflects genuine caution about near-term execution, not a conviction upgrade. Directionally right; numerically stale. Worth revisiting only when PL refreshes.

BOB|260524.change: PT raised ₹6,851→₹7,500 vs prior Aug-2025 note (per trendlyne); Hold maintained.
BOB|260524.view: BOB’s Hold with a ₹7,500 target was the most internally contradictory note on the May-2026 panel — the highest price target in the set attached to a cautious Hold rating. The ‘margin headwinds to persist near-term’ logic explained the rating, but ₹7,500 as a 12-month target implied BOB was more constructive on terminal value than the Hold label suggested. The ~9% PT lift from ₹6,851 was actually ahead of the constructive camp in absolute terms. Q1FY27 has since made the ‘margin headwinds’ premise look wrong; the note is below CMP and needs refreshing. BOB deserves credit for having the highest target on the May panel — it just chose the wrong rating tier to express it.

Geojit|260406.change: Upgraded to Hold from Sell; PT raised ₹5,400→₹6,336 vs prior Sep-2025 Sell note (per trendlyne).
Geojit|260406.view: Geojit upgraded from Sell to Hold in Apr-2026 — directionally right, but ₹6,336 is now well below CMP (~₹8,057). The upgrade likely chased the re-rating rather than leading it. Given the 4-month age and the target now implying substantial downside from current levels, this note carries no actionable weight. Geojit is not a high-conviction source on this name. Stale; no weight until refreshed post-Q1FY27.

DC|251120.change: PT raised ₹6,499→₹6,795 vs prior Aug-2025 note (per trendlyne); Accumulate maintained.
DC|251120.view: DC’s Nov-2025 note correctly identified CS traction and favourable mix as the structural positive — a thesis Q1FY27 has since validated. But ₹6,795 is ~15% below current CMP and the note is 9 months old, predating both Q4FY26 and Q1FY27. The directional thesis was right; the number is stale. Minimal live weight until DC publishes a post-Q1FY27 update.

ICICI|251109.change: PT raised ₹3,670→₹5,400 vs prior Aug-2024 note (per trendlyne); Sell maintained.
ICICI|251109.view: ICICI’s Sell at ₹5,400 is now approximately 48% below CMP — the most offside call in this coverage set. The ‘generics continue to drag; CS outlook unchanged’ thesis from Nov-2025 has been empirically falsified by Q1FY27: CS grew 45% YoY and now comprises 60% of revenue. ICICI will need a very substantial revision to re-enter the debate. Treat this as expired — it contains no actionable information about Divi’s current trajectory and should carry zero weight in any view formation.

MO|250203.change: No prior MO note in the library to compare; first captured entry. Neutral, TP ₹6,200 (Feb-2025).
MO|250203.view: MO’s Feb-2025 Neutral at ₹6,200 is 18 months old and now ~23% below CMP. MO is an active broker on this name and will have published multiple result updates since; none are captured in the library yet. The ‘CS drives earnings; generics stable’ framing was accurate but the valuation was quickly overtaken by events. Zero live weight — this entry is a placeholder until a current MO note is captured.

Sharekhan|241111.change: Upgraded to Buy with TP ₹6,812; no earlier Sharekhan entry in the library to compare prior TP.
Sharekhan|241111.view: Sharekhan’s Nov-2024 Buy upgrade at ₹6,812 has aged well directionally — the stock has comfortably cleared that target. But the note is 21 months old and carries zero current analytical weight. Purely historical context that the upgrade call was correct.

EPL.summary:
Coverage has narrowed to two houses — **ICICI** (Buy, TP ₹315, Mar-2026) and **MO** (Buy, TP ₹270, Mar-2026) — both bullish, both from late March 2026. The central shared thesis is the Indovida merger (CCI-approved, expected to close by 4QFY27), which would transform EPL from a laminated-tube specialist into a multi-platform emerging-markets packaging company. The 17% spread between targets (₹270–₹315) reflects how differently the two houses credit the Indovida synergy premium before the deal has closed. **ICICI** is the more optimistic house, framing EPL as ‘transitioning to multi-platform packaging with wider geographical reach’; **MO** is more grounded, with ₹270 representing a modest recovery from ₹260 (Nov-2025) after a sustained four-step cutting cycle from ₹315 (Nov-2024). Both notes predate any post-close merger data — Indovida is unlisted with limited public financial disclosure — so both targets embed assumptions that cannot yet be verified against reported numbers.

My own read: EPL is a solid but structurally narrow business — laminated tubes are a volume-and-relationship game with limited pricing power. Its durable edges are FMCG customer stickiness (Colgate, Unilever) and sustainability/barrier-tube capabilities that are winning market share globally. The Indovida deal is strategically sensible — broader geography, wider substrate range — but integration risk is real and the market is pricing something it cannot yet model. MO’s ₹270 is the more defensible near-term anchor: it gives limited synergy credit and reflects organic disappointments already embedded. ICICI’s ₹315 is achievable only if India segment margins recover and Indovida delivers simultaneously — a bull scenario, not a base. The India segment margin trajectory has been soft for several quarters and is the single most important organic variable to watch; the merger optionality is secondary until the core stabilises. Watch: (1) India segment EBITDA margins in Q1–Q2 FY27 — needs to demonstrate recovery before the merger premium is warranted; (2) any incremental Indovida financial disclosure at or before deal close.

ICICI|260331.change: PT raised ₹275→₹315 vs prior trendlyne entry (Aug-2024); Buy maintained. No pdfdata match; ~19-month gap between captured entries.
ICICI|260331.view:
ICICI is the more optimistic of the two active houses, and ₹315 is the bull-case ceiling in current coverage. The ‘multi-platform packaging’ framing maps cleanly onto the Indovida merger story — wider geography, more substrate types — and the ₹275→₹315 raise likely reflects credit for this strategic optionality. The 19-month gap between trendlyne entries makes the precise trigger unclear, but the framing is consistent with a merger-thesis upgrade rather than a reaction to organic results.

The risk with ICICI’s view is that ₹315 bakes in execution that has not yet occurred: Indovida has not closed, its financials are not public, and EPL’s India segment has underperformed for several quarters. Treat ₹315 as an aspirational upside scenario — correct if organic recovery and merger synergies land together — not as a base-case anchor. Useful as the top-of-range reference in a two-house panel.

MO|260330.change: PT raised ₹260→₹270 vs prior Nov-2025 note (per trendlyne); Buy maintained. Context: prior to this, MO cut TP repeatedly — ₹315 (Nov-2024) → ₹300 (Feb-2025) → ₹280 (Aug-2025) → ₹260 (Nov-2025) — before the modest ₹270 recovery.
MO|260330.view:
MO’s EPL history is the most instructive arc in the two-house panel: four consecutive PT cuts from ₹315 to ₹260 as organic results — particularly India margins — repeatedly disappointed, before ₹260→₹270 as the merger thesis gave a new directional leg. The ‘building a scaled consumer packaging leader for emerging markets’ framing is a structural pivot away from defending the quarterly run-rate.

The ₹270 is credible precisely because it is sober: it gives limited synergy credit and reflects the embedded organic disappointments. For MO to move meaningfully higher it would need visible India margin recovery and some quantification of Indovida at close. Among the two active houses this is the more grounded anchor, and I’d weight it more heavily than ICICI’s ₹315 until evidence arrives on either front.

Eicher Motors.summary:
The six active houseViews span a price-target range of ₹6,960 (MO, Neutral) to ₹8,122 (Geojit, Hold), with the lone outright Buy from **Axis Direct** (₹8,060, Feb-2026). Paradoxically the downgrade (Geojit from Buy to Hold, Jan-2026) carries the highest target, while the mildly constructive notes (**PL** Accumulate ₹7,580, **BOB** Hold ₹7,431) are the most recent in date. **MO** upgraded to Neutral at ₹6,960 in Mar-2026 -- the most cautious target. **ICICI Securities** (Hold, ₹7,200, Nov-2025) is the most stale, now nine months old. Critically, every note predates Q1FY27 results (July 29-30, 2026), where Eicher beat consensus cleanly: revenue and EBITDA both +32% YoY, EBITDA margin 24.0% despite ~290bps commodity inflation (offset by price hikes and lower other-expenses), lean channel inventory of 10-12 days, and strong booking momentum. The post-Q1 institutional consensus in the local library -- Goldman Sachs Buy ₹9,300, CLSA OP ₹8,568, JPMorgan OW ₹8,420, Nomura Neutral ₹8,437, Kotak ADD ₹8,200 -- has moved materially above the stale domestic targets, with the stock at ~₹7,781 already above BOB and PL's levels.

My own read: Royal Enfield occupies a structurally defensible niche -- the category creator in premium Indian motorcycles with genuine pricing power, community loyalty, and a premiumisation tailwind (GST cuts, rising aspirational demand) the competition has not seriously dented. Q1FY27 partially resolves the key bear concern: 24.0% EBITDA margins on +32% YoY revenue growth is not the profile of a business sacrificing profitability for market share. Morgan Stanley's EV-risk-caps-multiple-expansion thesis is the most intellectually substantive structural caution -- if RE misses the 250cc EV transition, the franchise premium compresses. I lean closer to the post-Q1 international consensus (₹8,200-₹8,600 range) than the stale domestic neutrals. Two things to watch most: (1) Q2FY27 margin trajectory as full-quarter commodity inflation lands without the favourable other-expenses offset; and (2) the new Cheyyar plant capacity ramp -- lean inventory plus fresh capacity before the festive season is the near-term volume catalyst.

The target is now below the current stock price (~₹7,781) following Q1FY27's beat, which PL has not yet reflected. The Accumulate framing was measured; a post-Q1 upward revision seems likely.

MO's Eicher coverage warrants a post-results refresh before assigning current weight.
