Emami.summary:
All five active houseViews are directionally bullish (Buy or Accumulate), but the consensus masks sharply different vintage and conviction. **KS** (Buy, ₹525, May-2026) is the only post-Q4FY26 note and has reflected the weak quarter with a target trim. **MO** (Buy, ₹650) and **PL** (Accumulate, ₹571) are from Feb-2026 based on Q3FY26 and pre-date Q4's miss. **Emkay** (Buy, ₹950) and **AR** (Buy, ₹900) are from Nov-2024 -- over 18 months stale -- and their targets are now detached from the stock's reality. The honest read on the panel is KS's own trajectory: ₹944 (Nov-2024) → ₹645 (Nov-2025) → ₹589 (Feb-2026) → ₹525 (May-2026) -- four consecutive target cuts that capture Emami's serial earnings disappointment far better than the still-bullish directional ratings do. There is no current structural bear in the active panel, which gives a misleadingly rosy picture: Q4FY26 results (revenues -4% YoY, summer portfolio -22% YoY on Middle East disruption, EBITDA miss ~16% vs consensus) would generate a Hold or Reduce from any house that refreshed post-results.

My own read: Emami's franchise -- Navratna, BoroPlus, Zandu, Smart & Handsome -- is genuinely niche and holds shelf-space loyalty, but the business has delivered flat-to-declining EBITDA for several years and the recovery keeps slipping one quarter forward. The structural issues are real: heavy summer/seasonal skew amplifies weather and geopolitical sensitivity; the Middle East export segment is a geopolitical hostage; and mass personal-care faces D2C and private-label pressure. KS's "recovery expected in 1H FY27" could be right -- the base is extremely weak and a normalised summer would mechanically restore the top line -- but this thesis has been stated in every prior cycle. I would stay on the sidelines until Q1FY27 (the critical summer quarter) prints. Two things to watch: (1) Navratna/summer-portfolio volume YoY in Q1FY27 -- a 10%+ bounce would validate the base-effect argument; (2) gross-margin sustainability above 68% (the one genuine bright spot in Q4FY26).

KS|260526.change: PT cut ₹589→₹525 (vs. prior KS trendlyne entry 260209/Buy/₹589); Buy maintained.
KS|260526.view:
KS is the only house with a post-Q4FY26 note and retains Buy, though the target trim to ₹525 reflects reduced near-term confidence. The geopolitical (Middle East) and seasonal framing is consistent with Q4 data, and the 1H FY27 recovery thesis is plausible on the base-effect argument.

However, KS's own target trajectory -- ₹944 (Nov-2024) → ₹645 (Nov-2025) → ₹589 (Feb-2026) → ₹525 (May-2026) -- is a consistent downgrade trend across every earnings season, suggesting the recovery keeps being pushed one quarter forward. Treat the Buy as a valuation-floor argument rather than growth conviction, and wait for Q1 FY27 data before acting.

MO|260204.change: PT cut ₹675→₹650 (vs. prior MO trendlyne entry 251110/Buy/₹675); Buy maintained.
MO|260204.view:
This is a pre-Q4FY26 note based on Q3FY26 results. MO was cautiously optimistic -- "steady show; positive commentary on growth recovery" -- but the subsequent Q4 miss makes this view stale. The ₹650 target sits above KS's post-miss ₹525, making MO more optimistic on an apples-to-apples basis than any house with Q4 in view.

MO's Emami view needs a post-Q4 refresh. The recovery story it was banking on did not materialise in Q4. Treat as an old data point until an updated note appears.

PL|260204.change: PT cut ₹697→₹571 (vs. prior PL trendlyne entry 250516/Accumulate/₹697); Accumulate maintained.
PL|260204.view:
PL's Accumulate from Feb-2026 is similarly pre-Q4 and based on Q3FY26 results. At ₹571 it is more conservative than MO, and the "cautiously optimistic" framing was an honest hedge at the time. PL has historically been the more measured voice on Emami relative to the bull pack.

Like MO, this view is now stale post-Q4. The Accumulate rather than Buy stance has been more defensible given the serial misses. The ₹571 target will likely be revised down when PL refreshes for Q4FY26.

Emkay|241110.change: Dated Nov-2024 (over 18 months old); no prior Emkay trendlyne entry for Emami to compare -- no recent prior.
Emkay|241110.view:
Emkay's Buy at ₹950 from November 2024 is deeply stale -- the stock has derated materially since and Emami has missed estimates in multiple quarters. "Better seasonality and focus on execution" was the thesis in Q2FY25; neither has delivered consistently in the 18 months since.

AR|241110.view:

Entero Healthcare.summary:
Only **Monarch** covers Entero Healthcare in the current library — a single bull view from August 2024 (PT ₹1,500, Buy, "Distribution excellence"), now nearly 24 months old. There is no inter-house debate: no bear, no neutral, no recent update. At IPO in Feb 2024 HDFC Securities published an IPO note (no target), but it is not a live research view. Coverage is sparse for a post-IPO pharma distributor that has been absorbing acquisitions and building out a medtech vertical.

My own read: Entero is India's most visible attempt at building a scaled, consolidated pharma distribution platform — a thesis that is structurally sound (the sector is deeply fragmented; the top few distributors hold less than 5% combined share) but carries real execution and financing risk. The IPO promise was to aggregate, use technology to improve working capital cycle, and layer in higher-margin medtech distribution over time. Two-plus years in, the key unresolved questions are: (a) whether EBITDA margins are actually expanding beyond the low-3% range typical for pharma distribution, or whether acquisition costs, integration drag, and minority interest are eating the scale benefits; (b) whether medtech is scaling fast enough to move the blended margin; and (c) whether the IPO premium has been earned in earnings. Without a fresh research note grounding a current target price, I would treat Entero as a speculative "show me" story — the structural thesis is compelling, but the conviction call requires updated earnings evidence on margin trajectory and organic vs. inorganic growth split.

Monarch|240816.view: Nearly 24 months old and essentially stale as a current input. The "Distribution excellence" framing was the right structural thesis for an IPO-era note, but the formative period since then — multiple acquisitions closed, medtech layered in, several full quarters of listed-company results — has made the specific numbers outdated. Monarch has either not updated coverage or the update has not reached the library. The Buy at ₹1,500 carries no actionable informational value without knowing whether Monarch still holds this view after the post-IPO earnings cycle. Treat as directional background only.

Eureka Forbes.summary:
Two houses cover Eureka Forbes in the current library: **ICICI** (Nov 2025, PT ₹685, Buy) and **East India** (Sep 2024, PT ₹536, Hold initiation). Both recognise the structural under-penetration story — particularly for water purifiers — but at very different risk/return assessments: ICICI is constructively bullish at ₹685, East India initiated cautiously at ₹536 nearly two years ago. The gap reflects initiation-vintage differences more than genuine disagreement on fundamentals today. Neither house has published a visible update post-4QFY26, leaving the RM cost pressure narrative that dominated the early-2026 earnings cycle unaddressed in the current library.

My own read: Eureka Forbes is a franchise-quality consumer company with genuinely durable competitive advantages — the AMC (annual maintenance contract) installed base creates a recurring-revenue engine and customer stickiness that most Indian consumer peers lack. Water purifier penetration in India remains low (sub-20% urban at meaningful price points; near-zero rural), which provides a long volume runway. Where I'd be watchful: RM cost pressure (steel, polymers for filter housings) can be structural during commodity cycle turns, and Eureka's premium positioning limits aggressive pass-through; competition has intensified meaningfully (Kent, Havells, AO Smith, Livpure all investing in distribution and brand); and new-category bets (air purifiers, water softeners) remain sub-scale. The two metrics I'd anchor to: (1) EBITDA margin trajectory over the next two quarters to confirm RM pressure is not worsening; (2) services revenue as a share of total — if it crosses 35%+, the recurring-cash AMC model becomes a meaningful valuation re-rating driver.

ICICI|251116.change: No pdfdata match in the library. Trendlyne history for ICICI: PT ₹660 (Oct 2024), raised to ₹735 (Dec 2024), then cut to ₹685 (Nov 2025); Buy maintained throughout. The current note implies a PT cut of ₹735→₹685 vs. the prior Dec 2024 report.
ICICI|251116.view:
ICICI's structural under-penetration thesis is the right anchor — WP penetration is genuinely low and the AMC model is sticky recurring revenue. The TP trajectory (₹660 → ₹735 → ₹685) shows ICICI has been recalibrating rather than holding a static bullish view, which is a good sign for intellectual honesty. The Dec 2024 raise and Nov 2025 pullback suggest they got more bullish on category acceleration in late 2024, then moderated on cost realities.

This note is now ~9 months old and pre-dates whatever RM pressure played out in early 2026. The ₹685 TP may be stale; the post-4QFY26 cost picture (RM/sales pressure flagged by other houses in May 2026) is not yet reflected here. There is no current informational value from this note; set it aside unless a fresh East India update emerges.

FSN E-commerce Ventures.summary:
Only one houseView is currently active for Nykaa — **Geojit** (Accumulate/₹277, Dec 2025) — which is now 8 months stale and predates both Q4FY26 results and the July 2026 Q1FY27 business update. The PDF library holds fresh post-Q1FY27 notes from **Morgan Stanley** (OW/₹321), **Nomura** (Buy/₹317), and **CLSA** (OP/₹358), all dated July 2026, but these do not appear in the current houseViews set. Across those three, the consensus is uniformly bullish: Nykaa's Q1FY27 preliminary update showed consolidated GMV/NSV growth in the early-30s (ahead of expectations), Fashion near-50% growth, and BPC sustaining strong momentum. Geojit's ₹277 target is far below every fresh note in the library. In practice, the houseViews board shows only a stale cautious print while the active coverage debate is between bull and outright-buy calls at ₹317–₹358.

My own read: Nykaa is one of the better-quality Indian internet franchises. The BPC moat is real — own-brands at ~54% YoY growth (CLSA) is not just margin accretion but brand equity compounding that is genuinely hard to replicate at speed. Fashion's near-50% growth is impressive but Fashion faces structurally tougher competition (Myntra/Flipkart, Ajio/Reliance) — both better capitalised and willing to subsidise growth whenever market share is at stake. The Q4FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.4% was a record, but the Q1FY27 update being preliminary means full margin delivery is still to be confirmed. Key watches: marketing cost line (was running 14% of NSV vs ~15% target in Q4FY26 — any reversal under competitive pressure would quickly reverse the margin story) and own-brand penetration in BPC sustaining above 20% of GMV. At ₹317–₹358, the market is pricing in continued execution; there is limited margin of safety if Fashion reverts or BPC growth decelerates.

Geojit|251211.view: Geojit's Dec 2025 Accumulate at ₹277 is now deeply stale — it predates Q4FY26 results (record 8.4% EBITDA margin, Fashion EBITDA breakeven), the Q1FY27 business update (GMV/NSV growth in early-30s, Fashion near-50%), and all the fresh July 2026 notes in the library. The downgrade from Buy (May 2024, ₹186) to Accumulate (Dec 2025, ₹277) likely reflected reasonable valuation caution at that time, but the ₹277 target now sits well below Nomura (₹317), Morgan Stanley (₹321), and CLSA (₹358). This note should be treated as archival only; it carries no current directional weight until Geojit publishes a post-Q1FY27 update.

Finolex Cables.summary:
Both active houseViews for Finolex Cables are cautious-to-stale: **Geojit** (Accumulate, TP ₹1,008, Mar-2026 — a downgrade from Buy) and **Anand Rathi** (Buy, TP ₹975, Nov-2025). Neither target sits above the level the stock had already reached by mid-2026, so both read as de facto Sell signals at current prices — yet no house carries a formal Sell; the bear case is expressed only through below-CMP or stale targets. The freshest marker is **Jefferies**, outside the houseViews set: Buy with TP raised ₹1,200→₹1,410 in Aug-2026 (from ₹1,200 in Jun-2026) on a strong Jun-Q beat — the Communication (OFC) segment's EBIT margin swung to ~30% from ~1% a year earlier (a segment that is ~23% of Q1 EBIT on ~9% of sales), and backward integration into OFC preform capacity can add more from Q3FY27. The real debate has moved past what the two domestic notes capture: the bull case now rests on OFC margins and copper pass-through in C&W, not the housing-demand story the older notes argued.

My own read: Finolex is a credible franchise — one of the stronger consumer-facing brands in Indian wires and cables, benefiting from housing and infra tailwinds, with a demonstrated ability to pass copper costs through pricing (~20% cumulative hikes in FY26 per Jefferies). The core electrical-cables business is sound. What the sell-side consistently underweights is competition: Polycab and KEI are better-capitalised and investing aggressively in distribution and product mix; any slip in Finolex's pricing power or volume share would compress margins quickly given the commodity input structure. FMEG (fans, switches) has been improving toward EBIT-positive but remains a modest drag. The OFC opportunity is real if government broadband rollout accelerates but is still early-stage and lumpy — the ~30% Communication margin Jefferies flagged is unlikely to be a clean run-rate. With only two stale domestic notes in scope, I would watch segment volume data (housing, power, auto cables), FMEG EBIT trajectory, and whether the OFC margin holds for another quarter before forming a conviction call.

Geojit|260318.change: Downgraded Buy→Accumulate; PT nudged ₹988 (Oct-2025 prior trendlyne entry, Buy)→₹1,008 (Mar-2026). No pdfdata entry — details from trendlyne.
Geojit|260318.view: Geojit's oscillation between Buy and Accumulate tracks valuation closely: upgraded to Buy at ₹988 in Oct-2025 (after a dip from the Dec-2024 Accumulate at ₹1,354), then downgraded back to Accumulate by Mar-2026 as the stock rallied. The token PT raise alongside the downgrade (₹988→₹1,008) is a fence-sitting move — capping upside near current price without committing to a Sell. With the Mar-2026 note now ~6 months stale and the stock higher, this functions as a cautious valuation cap rather than active directional guidance. Most conservative voice in the set, but discount the absolute PT as archival.

AR|251124.change: PT cut ₹1,031 (Aug-2025 prior trendlyne entry, Buy)→₹975 (Nov-2025); Buy maintained. No pdfdata entry — details from trendlyne.
AR|251124.view: Anand Rathi has held Buy through a steep, persistent PT compression: ₹1,577 (Nov-2024) → ₹1,031 (Aug-2025) → ₹975 (Nov-2025). The "mixed performance, steady H2 recovery" thesis from Nov-2025 has partly validated — Jefferies' later notes cite strong margin quarters. But at ₹975 (now ~10 months stale and below CMP), AR's PT is not a useful signal, and the repeated Buy-through-cuts suggests anchoring to an earnings model that has needed constant revision. Low weight until AR refreshes with post-Q1FY27 numbers; the rating matters less than whether their volume and margin estimates prove right.

Finolex Industries.summary:
The three recently-updated houses break 2:1 in favour of constructive views, with **IDBI Capital**'s year-old Hold as stale background. **Anand Rathi** (Buy, PT ₹240) is the most optimistic; **Prabhudas Lilladhar** downgraded to Accumulate (PT ₹207, cut from ₹228), citing subdued volumes and partly inventory-driven margin expansion; **BOB Capital** (Hold, PT ₹190) has stayed flat since February 2026, unmoved by the Q4FY26 margin beat. Target prices span ₹190–₹240 — a 26% spread for what is essentially one sub-sector play. The real debate is whether the Q4FY26 OPM spike reflects a durable cost reset or a temporary inventory-spread gain, and whether FY27 will see meaningful volume recovery after FY26's weakness.

My own read: Finolex is a commodity converter — it buys PVC resin (USD-priced, import-dependent) and processes it into pipes. Its economics are structurally mean-reverting: when resin spreads are favourable, OPM spikes; when they normalise, it collapses. The agri pipe segment (~65% of volumes) is highly weather and rural capex sensitive. The pivot toward plumbing/fittings is strategically correct but pits Finolex against better-capitalised incumbents — Astral Poly, Supreme Industries, Prince Pipes — with deeper distribution reach. I would sit closest to PL's Accumulate view: the Q4 beat is real but not compelling enough to add aggressively given that volume growth has not yet materialised. Watch Q1FY27 volumes and the plumbing segment's share gain trajectory — those are the two data points that would shift conviction.

BOB|260529.change: Hold maintained at PT ₹190; unchanged vs the February 2026 prior note (also Hold ₹190). BOB downgraded from Buy (PT ₹240, November 2025) to Hold (PT ₹190) in February 2026 and made no adjustment despite the Q4FY26 margin beat.
BOB|260529.view:
BOB's flat update through a strong Q4 print is a deliberate signal. They have been in 'show me volume recovery' mode since the November 2025 downgrade, and one strong margin quarter — even at ~25% OPM — has not changed that. The ₹190 target is the bear anchor in this coverage set.

I give this meaningful weight. BOB traced a full disappointment arc: Buy ₹265 (May 2025) → Buy ₹240 (Nov 2025) → Hold ₹190 (Feb 2026) → unchanged today. They have been consistently right to flag volume risk through FY26, and their reluctance to move post-Q4 is coherent with the data. The Hold/₹190 likely requires confirmed FY27 volume recovery before moving.

PL|260528.change: PT cut to ₹207 from ₹228 (prior captured entry: August 2025, Accumulate ₹228); headline states 'Downgrade to ACCUMULATE', implying PL held a Buy or higher rating between August 2025 and May 2026 not captured in the library.
PL|260528.view:
PL's downgrade and PT cut is the most analytically disciplined call post-Q4. Acknowledging the margin beat while flagging subdued volumes and inventory-driven expansion is honest — inventory spreads are transient and do not compound the way volume growth does. An Accumulate at ₹207 post a strong quarter essentially signals 'do not chase this.'

I find this the most credible current note. PL is not dismissing the franchise — the plumbing pivot and the Q4 OPM print are real — but they are not pretending the volume picture has turned. This is the view I would weight most when triangulating the investment case.

AR|260527.change: Buy maintained at PT ₹240 ('Maintain BUY' per headline). No prior Anand Rathi report in the library or trendlyne history; unable to assess TP movement.
AR|260527.view:
Anand Rathi's ₹240 is the most optimistic target — 26% above BOB's bear anchor and 16% above PL's cautious Accumulate. Without a prior note in the library it is hard to determine whether ₹240 has held constant or was raised post the Q4 beat, or what volume and margin assumptions underpin it.

Treat as the bull case. The 'sharp beat led by margin despite soft volume' framing is constructive but the missing model detail makes it harder to stress-test. If Q1FY27 volumes disappoint, the ₹240 target requires revisiting. Useful as an upside reference, but I would want to see the underlying assumptions before sizing to it.

IDBI|250806.change: Downgraded from Buy (PT ₹234, February 2025) to Hold (PT ₹207, August 2025). Note is approximately 12 months old and predates Q2–Q4 FY26 results entirely.
IDBI|250806.view:
This note is very stale — written post-Q1FY26 on the back of monsoon-driven demand weakness. The downgrade from Buy ₹234 to Hold ₹207 was rational at the time. Since then, Q2–Q4 FY26 have printed, a margin beat has occurred, and the stock has moved materially.

Place no weight on this as a current signal. It is only useful as historical context showing IDBI was early and correct to flag volume risk entering FY26. Whether IDBI has updated since August 2025 is unknown from the available data.

Fortis Healthcare.summary:
The three current houseViews split 2:1 bull vs hold. **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Buy, PT ₹1,050, February 2026) is the most recent constructive note — now over five months old, predating 4QFY26. **Geojit** (Buy, PT ₹1,030, December 2025) upgraded and has not refreshed since. **ICICI Securities** (Hold, PT ₹970, November 2025) is the lone dissenter on valuation grounds. The spread between the highest bull target (₹1,050) and the Hold (₹970) is modest — roughly 8% — making this a disagreement on valuation headroom rather than a fundamental divergence on the business. The broader coverage set that previously appeared here (JPMorgan, Jefferies, Nomura) is no longer in scope, so the current view set is thinner. The real debate: whether Fortis's guided 15%+ hospital revenue growth and 100bps EBITDA margin improvement (targeting 25% hospital margins by FY28) can be delivered consistently quarter after quarter, given that the most recent available data point — 4QFY26 — showed revenue outperformance but EBITDA margin pressure, with PAT flattered by a lower effective tax rate.

My own read: Fortis is a genuine compounding story. IHH's backing provides capital depth, clinical benchmarking, and M&A optionality that standalone chains cannot match, and the brownfield-led expansion model is the right template — lower capex, faster ramp, better ROCE trajectory than greenfield. But all three active notes are ageing, and the most important recent data point (4QFY26 EBITDA margin pressure) is not reflected in any of them. The diagnostic segment (SRL) is an under-discussed drag: structural margin compression against Lal Path Labs, Metropolis, and Thyrocare limits how fast consolidated margins can expand. I would be directionally bullish on the franchise but closer to ICICI's caution on current valuation. The two things to watch most: (1) quarterly hospital EBITDA margin — each print is a direct scorecard on the FY27 guide; and (2) whether new brownfield bed ramps dilute blended occupancy in the interim.

PL|260217.change: PT raised to ₹1,050 from ₹1,000 (prior: August 2025, Buy ₹1,000); Buy maintained.
PL|260217.view:
This Q3FY26 note from February 2026 is now over five months old and predates 4QFY26. PL was directionally correct — strong growth across hospital and diagnostic segments justified the PT step from ₹1,000 to ₹1,050. The consistent Buy progression (₹785 → ₹1,000 → ₹1,050) reflects the stock's re-rating arc and underlying business momentum.

That said, 4QFY26 prints — showing EBITDA margin pressure not visible in this note — make this a stale read for current sizing. Treat as supportive directional context. PL's track record on Fortis has been good, but a post-4Q refresh would materially strengthen or moderate the conviction.

Geojit|251222.change: Upgraded to Buy at PT ₹1,030 in December 2025; no prior Geojit coverage in the library or trendlyne history to compare.
Geojit|251222.view:
A 7-month-old upgrade with no subsequent refresh. The ₹1,030 target — lower of the two bull targets — suggests Geojit turned constructive on IHH-backed execution and the improving margin trajectory, but with measured conviction. Without a prior note it is hard to assess what specific catalysts drove the upgrade.

This is the oldest active note and should be treated as stale background colour. Geojit's lower target vs PL (₹1,030 vs ₹1,050) may simply reflect a later upgrade date with less earnings history in view, or a more conservative margin ramp assumption.

ICICI|251113.change: Dated November 2025; prior ICICI entry in trendlyne is from August 2023 (Buy ₹390) — too old for a meaningful delta. Current stance: Hold, PT ₹970.
ICICI|251113.view:
ICICI's November 2025 Hold at ₹970 is now 8 months old, but the core thesis — execution and network expansion support growth, valuation limits upside — has structural durability. The 4QFY26 EBITDA margin pressure (visible in broker notes outside this watchlist set) is exactly the kind of execution stumble ICICI's caution anticipated.

I would give this view meaningful structural weight even as the specific PT number ages. The Hold may be stale in price terms but the underlying caution — that Fortis trades at a premium requiring spotless margin delivery — remains relevant. Worth checking for a post-4Q refresh; if one exists, it may have either moved to Buy on earnings growth or reinforced the Hold with fresh evidence of margin pressure.

Fusion Finance.summary:
Three houses cover Fusion Finance, with vintage ranging from 21 months (Emkay) to 9 months (ICICI). **ICICI** (Nov 2025, Buy ₹225) executed the boldest call: a swing from Sell ₹160 in February 2025 to Buy ₹225 in nine months, citing improvement across businesses while acknowledging the path to profitability would be gradual. **Motilal Oswal** (May 2025, Neutral ₹170) has held Neutral through the entire recovery phase, trimming the PT marginally from ₹175, noting progressive collection improvement but declining to upgrade. **Emkay** (Sep 2024, Sell ₹260) is effectively dormant at 21+ months old, written at the trough when management change and elevated LLP guidance were dominant concerns; its Sell TP of ₹260 sits paradoxically above ICICI's current Buy TP of ₹225, reflecting how much the stock has re-rated down since. The real debate is whether ICICI's upgrade reflects a genuine credit-cost turning point or front-runs a recovery that has not yet materialised in NII or PPOP growth.

My own read: Fusion is one of the more distressed MFI franchise stories in the listed universe — a company whose analyst coverage went from ₹800 Buy targets in FY23 to going-concern audit language in late 2024, now attempting rehabilitation. That history demands scepticism of aggressive recovery calls. ICICI's Buy at ₹225 captures directional improvement but was written before recent quarterly data could confirm NII expansion alongside AUM. MO's Neutral at ₹170 is the more disciplined live stance: it acknowledges improving flows without pricing in a full recovery. The ₹55 gap between MO and ICICI essentially defines the bull/base spread. The two things I'd watch most: (1) NII trajectory — AUM growing while NII shrinks signals yield compression that would cap any RoA recovery; and (2) management stability — Fusion has had leadership disruption, and consistent execution under a stable team is the precondition for re-rating.

ICICI|251107.change: Upgraded from Sell (PT ₹160, Feb-2025) to Buy; PT raised to ₹225.
ICICI|251107.view:
ICICI's swing from ₹160 Sell to ₹225 Buy in nine months captures the violence of the MFI sentiment cycle. The November 2025 upgrade cited improvement across businesses and stabilising collections, while honestly flagging that profitability enhancement would be gradual. Directionally the call was early on a genuine inflection, and may be broadly right in signalling the cycle trough is past.

However, ICICI's track record on this stock — ₹800 Buy in FY23, ₹160 Sell in Feb-2025, ₹225 Buy in Nov-2025 — shows it has been reactive rather than anticipatory, making large moves late in the cycle. The Buy predates any post-upgrade quarterly confirmation of NII expansion. I'd treat it as a directional signal but would want at least one quarter of sequentially improving NII before giving the ₹225 TP real weight.

MO|250526.change: PT trimmed ₹175→₹170; Neutral maintained (vs Feb-2025 Neutral ₹175).
MO|250526.view:
Motilal Oswal has held Neutral through the entire recovery phase and remains the most conservative live view on price. The marginal trim to ₹170 in May 2025 reflects persistent scepticism — MO had flagged going-concern uncertainty as recently as November 2024, and the May note noted progressive improvement but saw insufficient upside to upgrade.

At 14+ months old, MO's note predates the most recent quarterly data. Their Neutral may underestimate fair value if the collections normalisation is genuine, but ₹170 serves as a useful downside anchor: it prices the recovery at fair value, not at a premium. The gap between MO's ₹170 and ICICI's ₹225 defines the scenario range — a ₹55 spread on a recovery stock makes position sizing the critical decision.

Emkay|240923.change: Dated Sep-2024; no prior Emkay note in the library to compare.
Emkay|240923.view:
Emkay's Sep-2024 Sell at ₹260 is 21+ months old and should be treated as historical context only. The concerns raised — elevated LLP guidance and management change — were valid at the trough and were subsequently confirmed by auditors' going-concern language noted in MO's November 2024 report.

The paradox is that Emkay's Sell TP of ₹260 now sits above ICICI's current Buy TP of ₹225, meaning the stock re-rated down significantly since Emkay was bearish. As a pricing input it is irrelevant. As a reminder of the severity of the cycle trough it is useful context. Emkay's absence from the post-trough discussion is itself a data point — they have not yet judged the recovery credible enough to re-engage.

GAIL India.summary:
Five houses are in the current library for GAIL India, spanning a wide range of conviction. **BOB Capital Markets** (May 2026, Sell ₹147) is the sole bear and freshest negative view: it downgraded from HOLD ₹153 in February 2026 back to Sell, flagging persistent LNG-price volatility and performance consistently below expectations across three consecutive quarters. **ICICI** (Jun 2025, Buy ₹245) carries the highest target in the peer set but is 14 months old, predating significant FY26 marketing-margin pressure. **Geojit** (Jun 2025, Buy ₹209, upgraded) and **Motilal Oswal** (Nov 2025, Buy ₹220, PT raised ₹205→220) are the other bulls; MO's is the freshest bull note but still 8+ months old and predates FY26 deterioration. **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Jul 2025, Hold ₹180, PT cut ₹191→180) is the most cautious non-bear. Note: pdfdata holds a cluster of very fresh post-Q1FY27 notes not yet in houseViews — **Nomura** (BUY ₹195, Aug 2026), **Kotak** (upgraded to BUY ₹215 from ₹175, Aug 2026), **JPMorgan** (OW ₹200, Aug 2026), **Jefferies** (HOLD ₹185 raised from ₹180, Jul 2026) — all flagging a sharp EBITDA beat driven by Middle East-linked gas trading gains. That fresh cluster, once in houseViews, will substantially reframe the picture.

My own read: GAIL is a regulated pipeline infrastructure business consistently misread as a commodity stock. The gas transmission moat — 12,000+ km of trunk infrastructure — is genuine and unreplicable. The problem is the gas marketing segment, where GAIL buys LNG at volatile international prices and sells at contractual rates, creating inherently volatile earnings that distort the P&L. The Q1FY27 EBITDA beat (reportedly 60–156% above estimates per the fresh broker notes) appears driven by the Middle East supply disruption making pipeline gas cheaper relative to LNG imports — a transient tailwind that reverses when conditions normalise. The **PNGRB tariff revision** is the genuine re-rating event: a long-delayed regulatory reset that could permanently lift transmission earnings. Until gazetted, transmission earnings are rangebound and the stock is effectively a binary event play. Two things to watch: the tariff revision timeline (PNGRB hearing calendar, court proceedings), and whether Q2FY27 gas marketing margins are recovering or still pressured post-Middle East normalisation.

BOB|260522.change: Downgraded from HOLD (PT ₹153, Feb-2026) to SELL (PT ₹147); per trendlyne.
BOB|260522.view:
BOB has moved in a round trip — Sell (Nov 2025, ₹166) → HOLD (Feb 2026, ₹153) → Sell (May 2026, ₹147) — a pattern suggesting they upgraded briefly and reverted as Q4FY26 disappointed again. Three consecutive weak-result notes have reinforced their view that LNG-price volatility is structural, not cyclical. At ₹147, BOB is the lowest target in the cohort by a wide margin.

BOB is implicitly pricing the marketing segment as a persistent drag and refusing to give full credit to the transmission moat. The transmission business alone likely justifies well above ₹147 on an infrastructure sum-of-parts basis, so the target is punitive. That said, BOB's caution on marketing volatility is structurally sound and worth monitoring — if Q1FY27's trading windfall prompts a BOB revision upward, that would be an important signal.

MO|251130.change: PT raised ₹205→₹220; Buy maintained (per trendlyne; Nov-2025 note, ~8 months old).
MO|251130.view:
Motilal Oswal raised its PT by ₹15 to ₹220 in November 2025, noting the tariff hike fell slightly short of expectations but calling valuations more compelling — a contrarian stance when market sentiment was cautious. The ₹220 target is the freshest bull view in the current library.

However, the November 2025 note predates Q3/Q4FY26 earnings weakness and the Q1FY27 one-off beat. Current data has moved substantially. The ₹220 target should be treated as a scenario ceiling — achievable if both the PNGRB tariff order materialises and marketing margins recover — not a near-term base case. A fresh MO note post-Q1FY27 would likely revise to around ₹195–210 reflecting the updated earnings base.

PL|250729.change: PT cut ₹191→₹180; Hold maintained (per trendlyne; Jul-2025 note, ~12 months old).
PL|250729.view:
Prabhudas Lilladhar's Hold at ₹180 was written after an in-line Q1FY26 with no particular beat or miss — the PT cut reflected declining confidence in near-term catalysts, not a business deterioration thesis. The Hold has been broadly validated by subsequent events.

At ~12 months old, PL's note is significantly stale. At ₹180, the target sits between BOB's Sell (₹147) and the bull cluster (₹195–245) and can be read as a cautious ceiling with no conviction either way. A fresh PL note would likely maintain Hold with a revised TP. Not a useful pricing reference at current vintage.

Geojit|250627.change: Upgraded to Buy; PT ₹209. No prior Geojit note for GAIL India in the library to compare.
Geojit|250627.view:
Geojit's June 2025 Buy upgrade to ₹209 was explicitly a tariff-hike play — the note describes an upgrade on that catalyst expectation. The upgrade predates the tariff order materialising, so the call was conditional on a catalyst that remains pending 14 months later.

At 14 months old, Geojit's Buy is now significantly stale. The ₹209 target sits in the middle of the stale bull range and adds limited incremental analytical value. Treat it as directional confirmation that a range of brokers turned bullish mid-2025 in anticipation of the tariff hike, not as a live pricing input.

ICICI|250627.change: No prior ICICI note for GAIL India in the library to compare.
ICICI|250627.view:
ICICI's June 2025 Buy at ₹245 is the highest target in the peer set — ₹25 above MO's ₹220 and roughly 30% above where the fresh post-Q1FY27 broker cluster (₹185–215) sits. At 14 months old, the note predates both the FY26 marketing-margin deterioration and the Q1FY27 trading windfall, making it analytically very stale. The ₹245 target requires both the PNGRB tariff hike to fully materialise and marketing margins to recover sustainably — neither has occurred.

I would discount ICICI's ₹245 as a live target entirely. A fresh ICICI note for GAIL post-Q1FY27 results would almost certainly set a materially lower PT. Use it only as an illustration of the optimistic scenario ceiling.

Grasim Industries.summary:
Only one broker appears in the active houseViews: **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, PT ₹3,700, Feb-2026) — a note now six months old that predates both the Q4FY26 results season and the landmark Sprng Energy acquisition. Broader context from the local PDF library (Jul-2026) is more instructive: **JPMorgan** (OW, PT ₹3,460) and **Morgan Stanley** (OW, PT not disclosed in the captured extract) both responded specifically to Aditya Birla Renewables' agreement to acquire Solenergi Power (holding company of Sprng Energy) from Shell at ₹172bn EV — adding ~5 GW of contracted renewable capacity to ABRen's existing ~4.4 GW, pending regulatory approval and expected to close by Dec-31, 2026. JPMorgan's post-acquisition ₹3,460 OW sits below MO's pre-acquisition ₹3,700, and represents the most current institutional calibration in the library. For historical context, the library also holds Jefferies (Buy, PT ₹3,600, May-2026), an earlier JPMorgan note (OW, PT ₹3,460, May-2026, raised ₹3,180→₹3,460), Kotak (ADD, PT ₹3,335, May-2026, upgraded) and Morgan Stanley (OW, PT ₹3,900, Jun-2026) — all constructive after Q4FY26 results. There is no active bear on record. The central near-term debate is the Sprng acquisition: whether ABRen paying ₹172bn EV for ~5 GW of contracted capacity is value-accretive at current renewable tariff levels, how GIP's co-funding alters Grasim's consolidated leverage, and whether the deal closes on schedule.

**My own read:** Grasim is a classic Indian conglomerate — diversified across cement (via UltraTech stake), VSF/chemicals, paints (Birla Opus), B2B ecommerce (Pivot), financial services (Aditya Birla Capital), and now renewables (ABRen + Sprng) — a structure that virtually guarantees a persistent holdco discount regardless of how individual parts perform. The Sprng acquisition is the most important development since the paints launch: at ₹172bn EV for ~5 GW, the implied per-MW price sits at a mid-premium to typical domestic clean energy deals; value accretion depends on tariff quality, PPA tenure, and whether ABRen can operate a Shell-assembled portfolio efficiently. The paints business (Birla Opus) was making genuine progress through Q4FY26 (19% QoQ growth, losses narrowing as reflected in the broader library coverage), but remains EBITDA-negative and competes against deeply entrenched incumbents with better distribution density. Two things I would watch most: (1) the Sprng deal closing timeline and the debt structure at the ABRen level — the ₹172bn EV is large relative to Grasim's standalone earnings base, and leverage trajectory matters for the holdco discount; (2) Birla Opus quarterly revenue and loss trajectory through 1QFY27 — the Street had pencilled in EBITDA breakeven in FY27, and whether that path holds is the key near-term sentiment driver for the stock.

MO|260211.change: PT raised ₹3,600→₹3,700; Buy maintained (prior MO Trendlyne entry: Buy, PT ₹3,600, Jan-2026, "Multiple growth engines at play; structurally positive").
MO|260211.view:
MO has been a persistent bull on Grasim — Buy on every captured note from mid-2024 through Feb-2026, with the PT steadily lifted from ₹2,840 (May-2024) through ₹3,410→₹3,500→₹3,550→₹3,600→₹3,700. The incremental ₹100 raise in February reflects steady-state conviction in the multi-business compounding thesis rather than a fresh catalyst. The title "Strong performance; high-growth businesses in traction" points to VSF/chemicals and early paints momentum.

The critical caveat: this note is six months old and does not incorporate two material events — Q4FY26 results (which prompted Kotak, JPMorgan, and Jefferies to raise PTs to ₹3,335–₹3,600 in May-Jun 2026, with Morgan Stanley at ₹3,900) and the July 2026 Sprng Energy acquisition announcement (₹172bn EV). JPMorgan's post-acquisition OW at ₹3,460 (Jul-2026) is the most current institutional valuation anchor in the library and implies a somewhat more conservative base than MO's pre-acquisition ₹3,700 — possibly reflecting acquisition capital risk pricing. Treat MO's note as the foundational thesis statement; the live valuation reference should be JPMorgan's post-acquisition figure until a fresh post-Sprng update appears from MO or another active house.

Gujarat Gas.summary:
Coverage has thinned to three houses, and the cross-house debate is minimal. **BOB Capital** (Hold ₹406, Jun 2026) is the only note reflecting the newly-amalgamated Gujarat Energy entity; **PL** (Hold ₹432, Aug 2025) and **ICICI Securities** (Buy ₹560, Feb 2025) both predate the merger and carry very different company contexts. There is no bear, no meaningful spread between the two Holds (BOB ₹406 vs PL ₹432 is a ₹26 gap), and the lone bull at ₹560 is over 18 months stale. The more recent and analytically richer post-merger notes — from Jefferies (upgrade to Hold ₹415), CLSA (Hold ₹375), JPMorgan (UW ₹270), and Nomura (Buy ₹511) — are no longer in the active houseViews, leaving a thin and largely consensus-Hold picture. Of what remains, BOB's Jun 2026 framing — "Transitioning from CGD Utility to Energy Conglomerate" — captures the identity problem for the stock precisely: this is no longer a pure-play CGD utility and existing valuation frameworks need revisiting.

My own read: The amalgamation of GSPC, GSPL, and Gujarat Gas into a single Gujarat Energy entity is a structural transformation that the thin current coverage does not adequately capture. The core CGD franchise — particularly Morbi ceramics industrial volumes and Gujarat's household penetration, among the best in the sector — is genuinely high quality, and the propane-to-gas switch in Morbi is a real near-term earnings lever. The concern is the conglomerate overlay: GSPC's gas trading is volatile, GSPL's transmission business introduces a different valuation multiple, and power sector additions are structurally challenged assets that create a holding-company discount. I'd anchor fair value in the ₹390–₹415 range — broadly consistent with BOB's ₹406 — rather than ICICI's stale ₹560. JPMorgan's earlier ₹270 UW (no longer in the active set) felt too punitive on a good CGD franchise, but consolidated earnings visibility is genuinely poor this early into the merger. The two things to watch: (1) how consolidated PAT trends in FY27 as gas trading and power contributions become clearer; (2) whether Morbi industrial volumes sustain after propane availability normalises.

BOB|260601.view:
BOB's Jun 2026 note is the only post-amalgamation view in the current set. The modest PT raise (₹379→₹406, +₹27) and maintained Hold reflect comfort with the CGD recovery but real uncertainty about the non-CGD businesses grafted on via the merger. The framing — "Transitioning from CGD Utility to Energy Conglomerate" — is analytically honest: BOB is not disputing the CGD quality, but is unwilling to extend a higher multiple on the blended entity until gas trading and power contributions clarify.

The ₹406 target is credible as a base case anchored on the CGD business with a conglomerate discount applied to the rest. This is the most current and grounded view available in the active coverage set.

PL|250806.change: Upgraded to Hold from Sell; PT raised ₹372→₹432.
PL|250806.view:
PL's Aug 2025 upgrade reversed a sustained Sell stance (Sell ₹395→₹372 since Feb 2025) after Q1FY26 results on the pre-merger Gujarat Gas — a structurally different entity from what exists today.

This note is now a year old and does not reflect the amalgamated entity at all. PL's ₹432 Hold target sits above BOB's current ₹406 but is built on entirely different entity assumptions. Treat as stale context: PL has not updated coverage since the merger and its current view is unknown.

ICICI|250208.change: Upgraded to Buy from Sell; PT raised ₹350→₹560.
ICICI|250208.view:
ICICI Securities' Feb 2025 Buy at ₹560 is the most stale note in the set — over 18 months old, issued on Q3FY25 results, and predating the amalgamation. The thesis ("prospects look better for next 12 months") was written on the legacy CGD entity. A ₹560 target implies ~40% upside to BOB's current ₹406 fair value — a spread that reflects staleness, not analytical disagreement.

This call is vestigial. ICICI has not updated since Feb 2025 and the post-merger entity is a fundamentally different investment. Disregard until ICICI issues a post-amalgamation update.

Gujarat Pipavav Port.summary:
Two houses covered GPPL within 24 hours of the same FY4Q26 results yet sit on opposite sides of the trade. **Kotak** upgraded to Buy (PT ₹186, raised from ₹172) citing a strong quarter, annual price hikes, and the upcoming Far East container service from July; **Jefferies** stayed at Underperform (PT ₹120, unchanged) flagging Middle East tensions as a near-term volume headwind and concession-renewal updates as 12–18 months away. The TP spread is 1.55× — ₹186 vs ₹120 — unusually wide for a single port asset. The real debate is not the quarterly beat but two structural questions: (1) whether the transshipment uplift from Middle East route disruption is durable or a temporary diversion that reverses on normalisation; and (2) whether GPPL's concession gets renewed on acceptable terms, which Jefferies treats as an unresolved overhang and Kotak largely glosses over.

My own read: GPPL has a genuine operational track record — cost discipline and blended-realisation improvement are real, and the 260bps margin expansion this quarter is not a fluke. But the competitive moat is thin relative to Mundra or JNPA, and the Maersk parentage is a double-edged sword: it provides anchor volumes but Maersk optimises its own network first. Jefferies is right to flag the concession risk as under-appreciated — a port where terminal tenure is uncertain within 12–18 months deserves a discount, not a premium re-rating. The new Far East service is a genuine catalyst but I would wait to see volume ramp before crediting it in the multiple. Kotak's ₹186 implies both the service launch and concession clarity materialising — two conditions, not one. I lean closer to Jefferies' structural caution, though the near-term earnings momentum makes an outright short uncomfortable. A ₹140–155 range looks more defensible than either extreme.

Kotak|260601.change: PT raised ₹172→₹186; report title states upgrade to BUY (prior call not captured in pdfdata — exact prior rating cannot be confirmed from that source alone).
Kotak|260601.view:
Kotak's upgrade is well-timed to a beat quarter and a constructive near-term setup. The 7–8% EBITDA estimate raise is grounded in realisation improvement and cost discipline, both of which are visible in the results. The thesis hinges on the July Far East service as the next re-rating catalyst — reasonable, but binary: if volumes diversify away from Middle East exposure ₹186 is achievable; if the service under-ramps or Middle East tensions ease (reducing transshipment), the upgrade unwinds quickly.

What I'd push back on: Kotak appears to treat part of the transshipment uplift as structural, but transshipment is notoriously fickle and follows the cheapest route. The concession overhang gets minimal attention in this note, which is the one risk Jefferies is explicitly pricing. Key watch-points are July–September container volume trends and any concession announcement — those two data points will confirm or challenge whether this upgrade was premature.

Jeff|260531.view:
Jefferies' bear case rests on two legs: near-term volume uncertainty from Middle East tensions and the 12–18 month horizon on concession updates. That the quarter came in 13% above JEFe yet Jefferies held its target and rating signals the valuation discount is deliberate — they are not ignoring the beat, they are discounting the terminal value.

This is probably the more rigorous structural view of the two. The concession point is one the market tends to dismiss until it suddenly cannot. At ₹120, Jefferies prices in minimal credit for concession extension beyond current terms — arguably harsh given Maersk's strategic interest in maintaining the port's viability, but it is the correct question to keep asking. I give this note high credibility on the structural risk, even if the near-term earnings momentum makes the outright Underperform a difficult hold in a rising market. The honest use of this note is as a checklist of what needs to be resolved before GPPL deserves a re-rating: concession terms and Far East service ramp.

Hindalco.summary:
Of 8 brokers in the current set, 4 are bullish (**Emkay** Buy ₹1,100 May-26, **MO** Buy ₹1,110 Mar-26, **BOB** Buy ₹1,050 Mar-26, **Geojit** Buy ₹1,034 Jan-26), 2 are Hold/neutral (**Axis** Hold ₹1,050 and **ICICI Direct** Hold ₹950, both downgraded Feb-26), and 2 are cautious (**ICICI Securities** Sell ₹765 Nov-25, **PL** Accumulate ₹762 Aug-25). The bull TPs cluster ₹1,034–₹1,110; the two caution calls sit at ₹762–₹765, and both are 9–12 months stale. The two Feb-26 downgraders (Axis and ICICI Direct) both predated the strong Q4FY26 results beat and have not refreshed — their views are likely too cautious and are probably being revised upward internally. The most current signal is Emkay's May 2026 note explicitly flagging early Oswego restart as a comfort signal, meaning the Novelis EBITDA drag that has suppressed earnings for two quarters is beginning to reverse. Most major institutional bulls (CLSA, JPMorgan, Kotak, Jefferies — visible in the broader PDF library but not in the current active houseViews) raised TPs materially post-4QFY26 to a ₹1,050–₹1,240 range, giving the active bull camp of ₹1,050–₹1,110 a credible factual anchor.

My own read: Hindalco's India business is structurally sound — captive coal, the sulfuric acid byproduct kicker from the copper smelter, and an aluminium expansion runway that differentiates it from pure commodity plays. The LME aluminium backdrop remains supportive, and tariff friction on Chinese metals could extend the upcycle. But **Novelis is the binary**. Bay Minett (the Canadian greenfield) has seen escalating capex and IRR compression with each revision; ICICI Securities' Nov-2025 thesis — "high capex intensity to push up debt" — remains structurally valid even as the stock has moved well above their ₹765 sell target. Oswego's fire-related disruption is theoretically recoverable, but multiple safety incidents in quick succession raise operational culture questions that a single restart does not fully answer. Net debt/EBITDA will climb through FY27-28 peak capex, compressing the return profile. I would be comfortable owning Hindalco on dips as an LME momentum trade or for the India upcycle, but Bay Minett execution risk and Novelis complexity keep me from full conviction at the top of the bull range. The two things to watch: (1) Oswego hot-mill restart sustainability over the next two quarters; (2) the next Bay Minett capex disclosure and any IRR guidance revision.

Emkay|260519.change: PT raised ₹900→₹1,100; Buy maintained. Prior trendlyne entry (Sep-2025) showed upgrade to Buy at ₹900; May-2026 note is a further PT raise with Buy maintained.
Emkay|260519.view:
Emkay's May 2026 note is the most current in the set and the most explicitly optimistic on Novelis near-term recovery. "Early Oswego restart adds comfort" is the key signal — if the hot-mill restart holds through H1 FY27, the Novelis EBITDA drag reverses materially. Emkay is making a focused tactical bet on operational normalisation.

The risk is that restart is a one-quarter event while Bay Minett keeps expanding the capex envelope. Emkay's ₹1,100 Buy is the most actionable current view — it will be validated or refuted quickly by the next Novelis quarterly result. This is the note worth tracking most closely as the near-term checkpoint is clearly defined.

BOB|260320.change: Initiation at Buy, TP ₹1,050 (Mar-2026); no prior BOB Capital Hindalco report in the library to compare.
BOB|260320.view:
A straightforward initiation at the lower end of the bull camp. BOB entered the stock after the market had already partially rerated from November 2025 lows. "Poised to gain from capex projects in India and Novelis" is not a differentiated thesis — it is the standard recovery play.

BOB's relative conservatism (₹1,050 vs Emkay/MO at ₹1,100–₹1,110) may reflect appropriate caution on Novelis recovery timing. Limited incremental insight relative to the more detailed institutional bulls, but adds coverage breadth.

MO|260316.change: TP ₹1,110; Buy maintained. MO raised PT ₹920→₹1,110 in the prior cycle (Nov-25 to Feb-26) and held flat through Mar-2026.
MO|260316.view:
MO's framing — "Structural tailwinds; Novelis sees near-term pressure" — is the most candid bull thesis in the set. They are explicitly accepting the near-term Novelis drag while arguing India's structural tailwinds more than offset it in the medium term. The flat TP across Feb and Mar 2026 despite elevated LME suggests their upside is already in the target.

The Mar-2026 note is 5 months stale and predates the 4QFY26 results beat. MO's ₹1,110 Buy could actually be conservative relative to a refreshed model. Still the most balanced bull framing: buy the structural story, acknowledge Novelis is a near-term drag.

Axis|260213.change: Downgraded to Hold from Buy; TP ₹1,050 (Feb-2026; trendlyne headline confirms "downgraded").
Axis|260213.view:
Axis downgraded in February 2026, predating the strong Q4FY26 results that prompted the bulls to raise TPs. The ₹1,050 Hold target now sits at or below the prevailing bull-camp targets, meaning Axis's view (if maintained) implies negligible upside.

This note is 6 months old and has not been refreshed in the library. The February downgrade was likely on valuation and near-term Novelis concern — both of which the Q4 beat partially addressed. Treat as a stale placeholder; Axis's true current view is unknown until they update post the recent results cycle.

ICICI|260213.change: Downgraded to Hold; TP ₹950 (Feb-2026; trendlyne headline confirms "downgraded" — implying prior rating was Buy). No prior ICICI Direct Hindalco entry in the library.
ICICI|260213.view:
ICICI Direct's February 2026 downgrade carries the most conservative target in the current set at ₹950 — meaningfully below the Hold camp's ₹1,050 and well below the bull camp. The ₹950 PT suggests ICICI Direct sees meaningful downside risk, likely on a more cautious Novelis/debt view.

This note is 6 months stale and predates Q4FY26 results. At ₹950, ICICI Direct's target is the most exposed to upward revision given the results beat. The concern about Novelis debt overhang is structurally legitimate, but the near-term thesis is moving against it. Discount heavily; watch for a refresh.

Geojit|260105.change: Upgraded to Buy; TP ₹1,034 (Jan-2026; trendlyne headline confirms "upgraded"; no prior Geojit Hindalco entry in the library).
Geojit|260105.view:
Geojit's January 2026 upgrade is 7 months old and predates both the Q3FY26 and Q4FY26 results cycles. The ₹1,034 PT is the lowest in the bull camp and likely reflects an earlier vintage of LME and Novelis assumptions. The upgrade was probably driven by the stock's pullback from late-2025 highs — a value entry call at the time.

Limited current relevance. Useful as a data point that broader broker sentiment turned positive in early 2026, but the TP and assumptions are not current. Treat as minor confirmatory context, not a primary analytical guide.

ICICI|251109.change: Downgraded to Sell from Hold; PT raised ₹720→₹765 (Nov-2025). Prior trendlyne entry (Aug-2025) was Hold at TP ₹720.
ICICI|251109.view:
ICICI Securities' Nov 2025 Sell — "Positives priced in; high capex intensity to push up debt" — was the most contrarian call in the set at the time. The unusual combination of PT raise (₹720→₹765) with a downgrade to Sell signals the stock had rerated ABOVE fair value during the Hold period; this is a valuation-driven call, not an operational deterioration call.

The note is 9 months old and the ₹765 target has likely been surpassed to the upside since the FY26 results cycle. ICICI Securities has not updated in the library since then. The underlying thesis — Bay Minett capex pushing up debt and compressing returns — remains structurally valid as a risk even as the stock moved well above ₹765. Either ICICI updates with a meaningful upward revision, or this becomes vestigial. Keep the capex concern in mind regardless of the stale rating.

PL|250813.change: PT ₹762; Accumulate (Aug-2025). No prior PL Hindalco entry in the library to compare.
PL|250813.view:
PL's Aug 2025 Accumulate at ₹762 is the most dated note in the set — over a year old, written on Q1FY26 results at a materially lower base price. The Accumulate rating reflected early-cycle recovery optimism before the stock rerated through subsequent results cycles.

This is vestigial. PL's Q1FY26 view does not capture Novelis disruptions, Bay Minett capex escalation, or the Q3-Q4FY26 beats that rerated the stock. Disregard for current positioning until PL refreshes coverage.

Hindustan Aeronautics.summary:
Only two houses sit in the covered set and both are bullish: **ICICI Securities** (Buy, TP ₹5,725, Nov 2025) and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Buy, TP ₹5,500, Aug 2025). Targets cluster in a tight ₹5,500–5,725 band, so there is no directional debate — but both notes are old (10 and 13 months as of Sep 2026) and predate HAL's strong Q1FY27 print. ICICI trimmed its target slightly (₹5,800→₹5,725) after a Q2FY26 provision hit but kept Buy; PL upgraded Accumulate→Buy in Aug 2025 on valuation with its target unchanged. Both framed the story the same way — order book excellent, near-term execution the open question. The staleness is the main caveat: neither has been refreshed through the FY26 zero-LCA-Mk1A-delivery year or the subsequent FY27 ramp evidence, and the broader street has since moved well ahead of them (Aug 2026 post-Q1FY27 notes from CLSA, Kotak, JPMorgan, Nomura and Goldman carry TPs of ₹5,265–6,314, all Buy/OP/OW/Add).

My own read: HAL's franchise is structurally unassailable — near-monopoly on Indian military platform manufacturing and MRO, a captive sovereign customer, and a multi-year indigenisation tailwind. Demand is not the question. What the sell-side keeps underweighting is HAL's serial execution risk: the LCA Mk1A slippage through FY26 was a pattern, not a one-off, and GE F404 engine supply is the binding constraint on the FY27 ramp. Current multiples (~28–30x FY27E) embed a clean delivery recovery, and the working-capital model is more MoD-advance-dependent than it looks. I'd land near the covered houses on valuation (~₹5,500–5,800) but wouldn't lean on notes this stale — the Aug 2026 cohort is the better guide. The two things I'd watch: (1) actual Q1/Q2FY27 LCA Mk1A and F404-fed deliveries as the primary derisking event, and (2) the FY27 MoD capex release pace, the biggest single lever on revenue recognition.

ICICI|251113.change: Buy maintained; PT trimmed ₹5,800→₹5,725 vs ICICI's prior note (13 Aug 2025). Sourced from trendlyne — no pdfdata match for this report.
ICICI|251113.view:
The Nov 2025 note ("provision dented performance; awaiting execution pickup") was a post-Q2FY26 reaction — a royalty/component-margin provision dented earnings quality and drove the marginal PT cut, with Buy held on the view that underlying demand is intact.

It is now ~10 months stale and the "awaiting execution pickup" framing aged poorly: execution did not materially recover through the rest of FY26 (zero LCA Mk1A deliveries). Read it as a conditional bull whose condition had not been met at the time of writing; the thesis only began to derisk with the Q1FY27 results, which this note predates. Directionally fine, analytically superseded.

PL|250812.change: Upgraded Accumulate→Buy; PT unchanged at ₹5,500 vs PL's prior note (18 May 2025). Sourced from trendlyne — no pdfdata match.
PL|250812.view:
PL's Aug 2025 upgrade with a flat ₹5,500 target was a valuation call, not a fundamental re-rating — the stock had de-rated after a weak FY25/Q1FY26 and the risk-reward crossed into Buy at the corrected price. The unchanged PT is the tell: they did not lift their view of intrinsic value, just concluded it had come to them cheaper.

At ~13 months old this is the stalest note in the covered set. Its ₹5,500 target still sits within the current upside range, but the thesis rests entirely on the FY27 delivery ramp that has only recently started to show. Weight lightly.

Cello World.summary:
All three covering brokers — **PL** (Buy, TP ₹621, Feb-2026), **ICICI** (Buy, TP ₹750, Nov-2025) and **MO** (Buy, TP ₹700, Oct-2025) — are constructive, so there is no bull–bear split; the variation is recency and conviction. **PL** (Feb-2026) is the most recent: Q3FY26 consumerware was soft, TP trimmed ₹678→₹621, Buy maintained — part of a consistent downward drift (₹770→₹746→₹678→₹621 since its Feb-2025 initiation). **ICICI** (Nov-2025, TP ₹750) carries the most differentiated thesis: the re-acquisition of the Cello brand in writing instruments (royalty elimination plus full brand control) as a potential re-rating catalyst. **MO** (Oct-2025, TP ₹700) leaned on new-plant ramp-up and a demand revival that PL's later note shows had not arrived by Q3FY26. Across all three, targets have roughly halved from IPO-era ₹960–₹1,100 to ₹621–₹750 while every rating stays Buy — the real debate is not direction but whether the consumerware and steel-products recovery lands in H1FY27, or whether the writing-instruments brand deal proves to be the first genuine fundamental inflection.

My own read: Cello is a genuinely strong consumer franchise — the Cello brand in writing instruments has deep household recall across India, and the consumerware and plastic-products business has real premiumisation tailwinds over time. But execution has disappointed badly since the IPO, and the multi-broker, multi-quarter PT-cut story is hard to dismiss. The steel-products segment remains the key near-term drag — captive capacity ramp-up should help on costs but will not fix demand alone. The writing-instruments brand re-acquisition (ICICI's Nov-2025 thesis) is the most strategically interesting angle: royalty elimination is a direct P&L benefit, and full brand control enables the premiumisation and distribution investment that partial-brand ownership constrained. At TP ₹621–₹750 the sell-side is pricing a recovery it has forecast for several quarters running; I would want an actual Q1FY27 volume inflection before taking conviction. Key watches: (1) consumerware volume and margin trajectory in Q1FY27; (2) writing-instruments revenue growth post brand acquisition — if meaningful, this is the first clean new positive in the story; (3) steel-products captive utilisation and volume recovery.

PL|260216.change: Prior PL entry Aug-2025 (trendlyne): Buy, TP ₹678. Now Buy, TP ₹621 — PT cut ~₹57; Buy maintained. No pdfdata match.
PL|260216.view:
PL's Feb-2026 Q3FY26 update is the most recent note in scope and consistent with the pattern: weak consumerware, TP trimmed, Buy held. The initiation-to-today drift (₹770→₹746→₹678→₹621) shows PL tracking quarterly deterioration without losing the long-run thesis.

Of the three, PL gives the most current near-term read. A Buy at ₹621 with consumerware volumes not yet inflected is more "don't sell your long" than active conviction. Watch PL's Q1FY27 update — if the TP holds or is cut again, that tells you whether the floor is in.

ICICI|251113.change: Prior ICICI entry Aug-2024 (trendlyne): Buy, TP ₹1,050. Now Buy, TP ₹750 — PT cut ~29%; Buy maintained. No pdfdata match.
ICICI|251113.view:
ICICI's Nov-2025 note is the most thematically differentiated of the three: the Cello brand re-acquisition in writing instruments is flagged as a potential re-rating catalyst. The structural logic is sound — royalty elimination directly improves economics, and full brand control enables premiumisation and distribution spend that partial-brand ownership constrained.

ICICI's own target series is the caution flag: a ₹300 cut from ₹1,050 to ₹750 over 15 months while holding Buy reflects repeated miss-and-adjust cycles. The "potential rerating catalyst" language is appropriately forward-looking but has to show up in revenue. If writing-instruments revenue grows 30-35% YoY in FY27, that would be the first clean new positive in some time. The note is ~10 months old — watch for an update after Q1FY27 results.

MO|251020.change: Prior MO entry Feb-2025 (trendlyne): Buy, TP ₹800. Now Buy, TP ₹700 — PT cut ~₹100; Buy maintained. No pdfdata match.
MO|251020.view:
MO's Oct-2025 note leaned on new-plant ramp-up and demand revival as recovery catalysts. The ₹100 cut from ₹800 reflected multi-quarter disappointment but MO stayed constructive. PL's Feb-2026 note confirms consumerware remained soft through Q3FY26, so the demand revival MO anticipated had not materialised.

The note is now ~10 months old and the recovery thesis has yet to show in numbers. Treat MO's view as background — directionally aligned with the other bulls but overtaken by PL's more recent, more data-grounded update. The ₹700 target is a rough consensus floor rather than a near-term anchor.

Dabur India.summary:
With **Jefferies** and **JPMorgan** no longer in the active houseViews, the remaining panel is a wall of caution broken only by the increasingly stale **Axis Direct** (Buy, ₹630, Sep-25). The freshest credible voices are **MO** (Neutral, ₹535, Jan-26, downgraded from a more constructive prior) and **PL** (Hold, ₹491, May-26, trimmed post-Q4FY26). **ICICI** (Hold, ₹500, Oct-25) and **BOB Capital** (Hold, ₹566, Aug-25) round out the cautious middle. **Emkay** (Sell, ₹450, May-25) is the lone bear but is 14+ months stale. The credible target cluster is ₹491–₹535. For richer context, Q1FY27 results (Jul-30 2026) prompted a cluster of fresh views outside the active panel: **Nomura** raised PT ₹600→₹625 (Buy), **JPMorgan** cut PT ₹525→₹485 (Neutral), **Kotak** trimmed PT ₹475→₹465 (Reduce), and **Morgan Stanley** held at UW/₹425 — a ₹425–₹625 spread that confirms Q1FY27 (consolidated revenue +10.6%, domestic volumes +5% off a weak base) was broadly in-line but the debate on durability of volume-led growth remains open.

My own read: Dabur is a deep but serially disappointing franchise in the near term. The Q1FY27 headline numbers are encouraging, but 5% domestic volume growth off a base that declined 1.8% in Q1FY26 is not a clean trend signal. Management's double-digit FY27 revenue guidance leans on pricing growth ahead of volumes (commodity pass-through) plus INR-aided international contribution (Q1 international +15.5%) — both fragile if input cost inflation persists or urban demand softens. The rural-urban gap (company rural outpacing urban by ~550bp in Q1) suggests recovery is concentrated in lower-priced rural SKUs, which mixes down margins. At ~40–44x P/E for a mid-single-digit volume grower with structural category pressure from Patanjali and HUL's Ayush range, I lean toward the Kotak/Morgan Stanley cautious camp. The two things I'd watch most: (1) whether H2FY27 volume growth sustains above 6–7% without a pricing crutch; (2) A&P/sales ratio — Dabur has a history of cutting brand investment to defend margins in tough periods, protecting near-term EPS at the cost of long-term positioning.

PL|260508.change: Hold maintained; PT trimmed ₹501→₹491 (May-26). Prior Trendlyne entry: Hold/₹501, May-2025.
PL|260508.view:
PL's marginal TP trim is a modest acknowledgement that Q4FY26 landed soft without triggering a directional shift. "Moderate outlook, valuations limit major downside" is honest sit-on-the-fence language: not cheap enough for Sell, not compelling enough for Buy.

PL covers FMCG with reasonable depth; the trim signals Q4 came in below their model. A ₹491 target implies very limited upside from ~₹433. Watch whether Q1FY27's broadly in-line print (domestic vol +5%) prompts PL to refresh this call or simply confirms the Hold band.

MO|260129.change: Downgraded to Neutral (PT ₹535, Jan-2026); no prior MO entry in the library to compare the exact prior call.
MO|260129.view:
MO's downgrade is arguably the most significant rating action in this coverage set — it signals that the bull case (volume recovery justifying a more constructive stance) had not materialised on schedule by Jan-26. MO's FMCG research is well-regarded; this carries more credibility than a routine TP trim.

Interestingly, at ₹535 with the stock at ~₹433 today, MO's Neutral implies ~23% upside — more constructive than the label suggests. This is a 6-month-old Neutral: worth watching whether Q1FY27's in-line delivery prompts MO to revisit the rating upward, or whether they trim the TP closer to the ₹491–₹485 caution cluster.

ICICI|251031.change: Hold, PT ₹500 (Oct-2025); no prior ICICI entry in the library to compare.
ICICI|251031.view:
"Cyclical upturn feasible but structural some time away" is a pithy and still-accurate summary of the Dabur dilemma. The cyclical upturn appears to be unfolding (Q1FY27 +10.6% consolidated revenue), but "structural some time away" remains apt — category-share pressure from Patanjali and regional Ayurveda brands, limited pricing power in competitive herbal segments, and rural concentration of the volume recovery all point to a slow structural fix.

ICICI at ₹500 is a conservative fair-value anchor, now ~15% above current price. The structural caution is the right lens even though the note is 9 months old. Worth refreshing now that Q1FY27 results have landed.

Axis|250905.change: Upgraded Hold→Buy; PT raised ₹510→₹630 (Sep-25). Prior Trendlyne entry: Hold/₹510, May-2025.
Axis|250905.view:
Axis upgraded in September 2025 — now 11 months old, and before MO's downgrade, PL's Q4FY26 TP trim, and three quarterly results cycles. At ₹630 the target is the most bullish in coverage and looks increasingly stretched relative to the ₹491–₹535 caution cluster.

The upgrade thesis (rural recovery, margin improvement on a normalised base) has not played out. I'd treat this as an outlier whose catalyst timeline has slipped; it deserves the least weight in the active set until Axis refreshes the call post-Q1FY27.

BOB|250801.change: Hold, PT ₹566 (Aug-2025); no prior BOB entry in the library to compare.
BOB|250801.view:
"Improving underlying trends but A&P needs to hold" is the structurally most important flag in this set. Dabur has historically cut advertising spend to defend margins in tough periods, but that erodes brand equity in FMCG categories where recall and shelf presence matter.

This is the right tension to monitor every quarter: A&P sustained = near-term margin pressure; A&P cut = long-term category-share risk. The note is nearly 12 months old and the ₹566 target is well above current price (~₹433), but the A&P concern remains live. Check Q1FY27 investor presentation for A&P/sales disclosure.

Emkay|250508.change: Sell, PT ₹450 (May-2025); no prior Emkay entry in the library to compare.
Emkay|250508.view:
Emkay's "weak Q4 delivery; growth guidance remains aspirational" has aged better directionally than on price — the stock is near ₹433, close to their ₹450 PT, even without a price collapse. The underlying concerns about guidance credibility and structural execution are more accurate than the more charitable notes imply.

At 14+ months old this is too stale for active weight, but the observation that management guidance has been aspirational rather than grounded is a useful calibration. Even the Q1FY27 double-digit growth came on a very weak base — exactly the pattern Emkay was flagging. The Sell label may be stale; the structural scepticism is not.

Hitachi Energy India.summary:
The covered set is uniformly cautious — no bull among the four. **IDBI Capital** (Hold, ₹35,001) and **Motilal Oswal** (Neutral, ₹32,000, upgraded from Sell) sit mid-road; **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (Reduce, ₹30,768, downgraded from Hold) is the bear; **Geojit** (Hold, ₹22,859, Aug 2025) is ~13 months stale and far below market — disregard it. The three live targets cluster in a tight ₹30,800–35,000 band around the mid-2026 market price (~₹32,000–33,000), so the covered houses are effectively saying "good business, roughly fairly valued, don't chase." Both PL and IDBI moved to a more cautious rating in late May 2026 while raising (PL) or setting a high (IDBI) target — a valuation call, not a thesis reversal; all four accept the structural transmission-capex and data-centre demand story. These notes are ~3 months old (post-Q4FY26) and have since been overtaken by a second strong quarter (Q1FY27, Aug 2026) that prompted PT hikes from the more bullish uncovered houses (Jefferies ₹45,790, JPMorgan ₹40,500, Nomura ₹40,030; Goldman stayed Neutral at ₹30,100).

My own read: Hitachi Energy India is a genuinely differentiated franchise — near-monopoly in large power transformers, parent technology and balance-sheet backing, and an HVDC early-mover position as India builds out long-distance transmission corridors. The grid investment super-cycle is real and multi-year, with data-centre power demand a still-early second engine. But this is a "right business, hard valuation" case: Q4FY26 EBITDA margin (~16%) was roughly flat sequentially despite strong revenue growth, opex ran ahead, and operating leverage has not yet shown up cleanly; the capex ramp will pressure free cash flow for 2–3 years. I'm more constructive than PL's Reduce but agree with the covered houses that ₹40k+ needs evidence HVDC margins are landing. The two things I'd watch most: (1) FY27 EBITDA-margin trajectory — does operating leverage finally appear? and (2) order-inflow mix — HVDC/exports versus commoditised domestic T&D, which carries lower margins and more competition.

IDBI|260527.change: Downgraded to Hold, PT ₹35,001 (27 May 2026). No prior IDBI Capital report in the library to compare.
IDBI|260527.view:
IDBI's Hold at ₹35,001 is the highest target in the covered set yet carries a neutral rating — a higher PT with a cautious call usually means "the model supports upside but risk-reward has deteriorated at the current price." The oddly precise figure looks like a direct DCF output rather than a conviction round number.

Without the prior note it is unclear whether this is a cut from Buy or continuity of caution. Net read: good business, fair value roughly here, don't chase — a pause flag, not a sell. Revisit if the stock pushes materially above ₹35,000.

PL|260527.change: Downgraded Hold→Reduce; PT raised ₹26,108→₹30,768 vs PL's initiation note (10 Mar 2026, Hold). Sourced from trendlyne — no pdfdata match.
PL|260527.view:
PL's Reduce-with-a-raised-target is the most intellectually honest call in the group: they concede the structural growth story is intact and numbers are going up, but argue the re-rating has run so far that risk-reward has flipped negative. Valuation calls like this — thesis intact, price wrong — tend to be more durable than thesis reversals.

If CMP is materially above ₹30,768 this is the cleanest downside flag available. Take it seriously as a counterweight to the bullish uncovered houses. The signal to watch: successive upward PT revisions while the rating stays Reduce would confirm the structural bull is outrunning fundamentals.

MO|260526.change: Upgraded Sell→Neutral; PT raised ₹12,500→₹32,000 vs MO's prior note (15 May 2025, Sell). Sourced from trendlyne — no pdfdata match; the ~1-year gap makes this a re-rating, not a single-quarter move.
MO|260526.view:
Motilal Oswal's journey from Sell at ₹12,500 to Neutral at ₹32,000 over a year tracks the broad re-rating of T&D / capital-goods names. Stopping at Neutral says MO accepts the demand tailwind but still finds the valuation uncomfortable.

Most useful as a valuation anchor: an MO Neutral at ₹32,000 puts sell-side "fair value" in roughly the ₹30,000–35,000 zone, which makes Jefferies' ₹45,790 a genuine outlier. A further MO upgrade on proven FY27 margin delivery would be the inflection signal.

Geojit|250812.change: Upgraded Sell→Hold; PT raised ₹16,853→₹22,859 vs Geojit's prior note (30 May 2025). Dated Aug 2025 — ~13 months old, treat as stale.
Geojit|250812.view: Easily the oldest note in the set and no guide to current positioning. At ₹22,859 the target is far below the current market price, and the 2025 rating history (Buy→Sell→Sell→Hold) reflects a stock that has since re-rated dramatically. Disregard for positioning; it survives only as a marker of how far the stock has run since mid-2025.

Honasa Consumer.summary:
Only one house sits in the covered house-view set for Honasa — **ICICI Securities** (Buy, ₹400) — and it is a year-old August-2025 note whose target has since been overtaken by the stock (~₹479). Local data shows how sharply the wider street has split after a run of quarterly beats through FY26 and 1QFY27: **Jefferies** (Buy, ₹650) and **Kotak** (Buy, ₹580, upgraded from Add) are the bulls; **Goldman Sachs** (Neutral, ₹450) and **CLSA** (Hold, ₹505) acknowledge the beats but stay on the fence; **JPMorgan** (Underweight, ₹410) is the lone structural bear. Targets span ₹410–650 around a ~₹479 price. The debate is no longer whether the FY26 turnaround is real (it is) but whether the multi-year compounding-plus-margin-expansion story justifies the multiple, and whether Mamaearth's core can sustain double-digit growth without channel help.

My own read: Honasa's replatforming genuinely worked — A&P concentration on focus categories, a distribution overhaul and brand rationalisation drove real LFL organic growth and 400–500bps of EBITDA-margin expansion, and The Derma Co crossing ₹10bn ARR gives a credible second engine. But the bear case has teeth: Mamaearth (still roughly half the business) is only growing high-teens on a weak base, gross margin slipped YoY (JPMorgan flagged 69.7%, -150bps), and BPC is brutally competitive with Minimalist now inside HUL, plus Pilgrim and Plum. I'd land constructive but well below Jefferies' ₹650 — closer to the ₹500–520 zone — until Mamaearth reaccelerates on its own. The two things I'd watch most: (1) Mamaearth value/volume growth stripped of base effects, and whether secondary sales keep tracking primary; (2) whether the margin gains hold as A&P normalises and the lower-margin younger brands scale in the mix.

ICICI|250813.change: Trendlyne shows TP ₹400, Buy (Aug-2025); the prior ICICI note (Jun-2025 'Honasa Day') also carried ₹400, Buy — no change between them. No pdfdata match. The note is ~12 months old and its ₹400 target now sits below the market price (~₹479).
ICICI|250813.view: Written before the run of FY26/1QFY27 beats, this 'we stay believers' Buy has been vindicated in direction but overtaken in level — ₹400 is now a floor rather than a target, and the analysis predates the offline scale-up, TDC's ₹10bn ARR milestone and the margin inflection. Treat it as stale: it tells you ICICI was early and right on the turnaround, not where the stock should trade today. It needs a refreshed post-1QFY27 note before this house carries weight in the current debate.

Hyundai Motor India.summary:
Of the three covered house-views, two are bulls and one is a stale bear. **BOB Capital** (Buy, ₹2,261, May-2026) and **ICICI** (Buy, ₹2,150, Mar-2026) both back the capacity-ramp plus whitespace-launch recovery thesis; BOB has since nudged its target down slightly (₹2,287→₹2,261) and flags a "short-term snag". **Emkay** (Reduce, ₹1,750) is the lone bear, but its call is an Oct-2024 IPO-era initiation, ~22 months stale. Local data shows the wider street is now sharply divided after a weak 1QFY27 (EBITDA -31% YoY, margin ~9.3%): **Goldman Sachs** (Buy, ₹2,530), **Nomura** (Buy, ₹2,498), **JPMorgan** (OW, ₹2,240) and **CLSA** (Outperform, ₹2,300) on one side; **Jefferies** (Underperform, ₹1,725 — "franchise slipping, a distant #4 in SUVs") and **Kotak** (Reduce, ₹2,000) on the other.
