The real debate: does the 2HFY27 recovery — two new launches, export normalisation, a third Pune shift — restore share and margins, or is HMIL structurally losing the SUV space it created?

My own read: Hyundai is a genuinely strong franchise — India's #2 PV maker, a deep dealer network, profitable localisation, and a credible EV roadmap through the parent. But the bears are pointing at something real: HMIL has slid to a distant #4 in SUVs as Mahindra and Tata launched faster with domestically developed products, and 1QFY27's -31% EBITDA and sub-10% margin show how hard the operating deleverage bites when volume stalls (1Q domestic volume -1.3% YoY). Management's FY27 8–10% volume guidance leans entirely on a second-half hockey stick that isn't yet in the run-rate. I'd sit cautious — nearer Kotak/Morgan Stanley (~₹2,000–2,130) than the ₹2,500 bulls — because at bull-target levels the stock already discounts a clean recovery and the risk is asymmetric on a launch miss. Emkay's stale note still names the right tension: quality franchise, rich multiple, muted growth. The three things I'd watch most: (1) festive-season reception and pricing of the new mid-size SUV; (2) monthly domestic PV market share through 2HFY27; (3) whether the GST-cut demand lift is broad-based or accrues mostly to the challengers.

BOB|260509.change: PT trimmed ₹2,287→₹2,261; Buy maintained (vs BOB's 24-Mar-2026 initiation). No pdfdata match; figures from trendlyne.
BOB|260509.view: BOB initiated in March 2026 on a capacity-ramp thesis and has nudged the target down ~1% while keeping the Buy — a marginal trim, and the 'snag in the short term' language concedes exactly the near-term execution and demand lumpiness that the weak 1QFY27 then confirmed. BOB is a smaller domestic house adding breadth rather than a differentiated modelling edge; at four months old and pre-1QFY27, the ₹2,261 target predates both the soft print and the wider street's split. Directionally in the bull camp, but I'd weight the fuller post-results work from JPMorgan, Nomura and Jefferies more heavily.

ICICI|260331.change: PT ₹2,150; Buy. No earlier ICICI report in the library to compare — dated Mar-2026, ~5 months old.
ICICI|260331.view: The 'Beyond Creta-Venue' report frames the pivotal bull argument: that HMIL can arrest share loss by launching into segments it doesn't currently contest. That is the right question to ask, but the note is now pre-1QFY27 and pre the export weakness, and its ₹2,150 target sits mid-pack. The thesis lives or dies on launch execution — cadence, pricing, consumer pull — where HMIL has clearly lagged Tata and Mahindra. Treat it as a credible medium-term case that needs a post-results refresh; new-model booking data is the acid test.

Emkay|241022.change: Initiation in Oct-2024; Reduce, PT ₹1,750. ~22 months old — no subsequent Emkay update in the library.
Emkay|241022.view: Emkay was the lone bear at IPO — strong brand, but a rich multiple against muted volume growth. That tension has largely played out: HMIL has lost domestic share since listing and 1QFY27 margin fell to ~9%. Tellingly, Jefferies' mid-2026 Underperform (₹1,725) has since converged almost exactly on Emkay's old target. The note itself is far too stale to trade on — the auto cycle, the GST cuts and the launch pipeline have all moved — but the valuation-versus-growth framework it set out remains the cleanest statement of the bear case. It needs an update to count as a live call.

Delhivery.summary:
Five houses cover Delhivery, all with Buy-equivalent ratings. The two freshest are **Motilal Oswal** (May-26, Buy, PT ₹580, raised from ₹570) and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** (May-26, upgraded from Accumulate to Buy, PT raised ₹466→₹534) — both reacting to Q4FY26 results that showed FCF turning positive for the first time since IPO. **Emkay** (Mar-26, Buy, PT ₹500) predates Q4 results; **Geojit** (Dec-25, Buy, PT ₹469) and **ICICI** (Nov-25, Buy, PT ₹600) are 5–8 months stale. Fresh May-26 consensus clusters ₹534–₹580; the ICICI ₹600 was set anticipating an FCF inflection that has now delivered, so it should be read as a baseline, not a ceiling. No house is cautious or bearish — the debate is on pace of FCF compounding and whether Express Parcel EBITDA margins can hold above 18% at scale, not on direction.

My own read: the FCF inflection from –₹2.5bn in FY25 to +₹890mn in FY26 is genuine and marks a real regime shift — four years of post-IPO cash burn rightfully depressed sentiment, and this changes the capital-allocation calculus. What the sell-side underweights: Q4FY26's 73% volume surge partly reflects a one-time consolidation windfall as smaller players ceded share. Sustaining that trajectory requires winning fresh outsourcing mandates from large e-commerce players whose own captive arms are getting more sophisticated, and pricing power in that context is the variable that matters most. Yield-per-shipment in Q1FY27 is the clearest early signal. I find ICICI's ₹600 (set pre-FCF, essentially pre-pricing the inflection) a useful reference: if they refresh post-Q4 and still hold ₹600+, it signals more upside remains; if they trim, it suggests the market has already captured the re-rating. I would be constructive but value-conscious above ₹560 — upside from here requires the FY28 FCF scale-up to land on schedule.

PL|260518.change: Rating upgraded from Accumulate to Buy; PT raised ₹466→₹534 (vs Aug-2025 prior: Accumulate, PT ₹466).
PL|260518.view: PL's upgrade is the clearest rating action from Q4FY26 results — their prior Accumulate at ₹466 had explicitly flagged B2C volume uncertainty, and the FCF-positive print crossed their stated gating condition (the report title "Turns FCFF positive" says exactly what moved them). The PT step-up (₹466→₹534, +15%) is meaningful but still lags the MO/ICICI range, suggesting PL is running a conservative FCF model or a lower exit multiple. Treat the ₹534 as a post-results floor that will likely drift higher in a follow-up note; the upgrade itself is the more important signal than the absolute number.

MO|260517.change: PT raised ₹570→₹580; Buy maintained (vs Apr-2026 prior: Buy, PT ₹570).
MO|260517.view: MO has been consistently bullish across at least six reports since early 2025 — Buy through the Q2FY26 margin miss, through consolidation uncertainty, and now through Q4FY26's beat. The incremental PT raise (₹570→₹580, +₹10) post-Q4 is conspicuously modest for a strong result, suggesting MO is already running near the upper bound of their DCF range rather than opening new upside. Their outsourcing-to-3PL and consolidation-beneficiary thesis was correct and early. The risk is that persistent conviction without a step-change revision makes it hard to distinguish genuine model updates from anchoring. Watch whether they revise materially after Q1FY27 — that would signal fresh conviction rather than maintenance of an existing call.

Emkay|260307.change: PT trimmed ₹510→₹500; Buy maintained (vs Nov-2025 prior: Buy, PT ₹510).
Emkay|260307.view: Emkay's March note is five months old and predates Q4FY26 results. Their consolidation thesis — industry rationalisation supporting B2C volume recovery — proved correct; Q4 delivered 73% volume growth. The slight PT trim to ₹500 at the time reflected near-term uncertainty around consolidation timing. With Q4 results now public and peer PTs revised to ₹534–₹600, Emkay's ₹500 is the most outdated active target in this set. Use this as a directional bull signal; the absolute TP needs a post-Q4 refresh to be useful.

Geojit|251226.change: Upgraded to Buy, PT ₹469; Dec-2025. No prior Geojit entry in the library to compare on TP or prior rating.
Geojit|251226.view: Stale (Dec-2025) and materially below the current consensus range. Geojit's upgrade was a catch-up move after several other brokers had been at Buy for longer. The ₹469 PT was set before Q4FY26 results and is now the lowest active target in the set. Useful only as a record that Geojit turned bullish by end-2025; not a live price reference.

ICICI|251106.change: PT ₹600; Buy maintained. Unchanged vs Aug-2025 prior (also Buy, PT ₹600).
ICICI|251106.view: ICICI's Nov-2025 note is 8 months old and predates Q4FY26. Their "structural tailwinds + strong execution = rerating" framing was directionally prescient. The ₹600 PT was set before FCF turned positive — ICICI was pre-pricing the FCF inflection that Q4FY26 subsequently delivered, which means their thesis has been validated. Whether ₹600 still represents net upside depends on the current price. The most useful data point to watch: a post-Q1FY27 update from ICICI. If they reiterate Buy at ₹600+ having seen the FCF confirmation, that is genuine conviction; if they trim, it signals the re-rating is largely complete.

IPCA Laboratories.summary:
All four covering houses in scope are bullish — no bear or neutral. **Prabhudas Lilladhar** is by far the most current and most actively tracked: Buy, TP ₹1,800 (Jun-2026 Q4FY26 result update), the end-point of a steady upgrade path — Accumulate ₹1,525 (mid-2025) → Buy ₹1,710 (Feb-2026 Q3 beat) → Buy ₹1,800 (Mar-2026 management meet) → held at ₹1,800 (Jun-2026). **ICICI Direct** upgraded to Buy at ₹1,660 in Nov-2025 — directionally aligned but its target has since been overtaken by PL and by the stock. **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, ₹1,980, Dec-2024) and **Sharekhan** (Buy, ₹1,765, Nov-2024) are ~20-month-old notes written before the FY26 margin recovery; MO's ₹1,980 is the highest number in the set purely because it is the least updated. The debate has essentially collapsed — the Q4FY26 print validated the turnaround thesis every house was building toward, and PL's explicit 'strong FY27 guidance' flag is the forward pivot: the question is no longer whether the recovery happened but whether guidance converts.

My own read: IPCA is a solid mid-cap pharma franchise that spent FY24–25 digesting the Unichem merger and delivering disappointingly flat margins — PL's upgrade cycle (Accumulate ₹1,525 to Buy ₹1,800 over three quarters) tracks the operational recovery closely and feels earned, not premature. The chronic-therapy domestic position is sticky and the shift in export mix toward branded formulations is the right structural direction for margins. What the sell-side is glossing over: US generic revenue remains lumpy and molecule-concentrated — IPCA's US history is one of niche wins followed by pricing attrition, and any ANDA setback or US customer-concentration issue would unwind the export-led part of the thesis quickly. The Unichem working-capital drag also lingers. I'd be broadly aligned with the bulls — the margin trajectory is real — but I'd want two quarters of H1FY27 delivery against management's guidance before attaching much weight to PL's ₹1,800, let alone MO's now-vintage ₹1,980. The two things I'd watch: (1) the quarterly US revenue trend and gross-margin direction; (2) H1FY27 earnings versus the 'strong FY27 guidance' bar PL cited.

PL|260602.change: No pdfdata match; from trendlyne coverage history: PT ₹1,800 and Buy both maintained vs the PL management-meet note dated 06-Mar-2026 (PL had upgraded from Accumulate ₹1,525 to Buy ₹1,710 in Feb-2026, then to ₹1,800 in Mar-2026).
PL|260602.view:
PL has been the most consistently tracked house across the FY26 cycle, and its upgrade trajectory — Accumulate ₹1,525 (mid-2025) → Buy ₹1,710 (Feb-2026 Q3 beat) → Buy ₹1,800 (Mar-2026 management meet) → held ₹1,800 (Jun-2026 Q4) — reads as a disciplined step-by-step re-rating rather than a one-shot call. The Q4 note flagging 'strong FY27 guidance' is the key line: PL is committing to the forward trajectory, not just endorsing the Q4 beat.

The tell is that ₹1,800 is a 0% move from the Mar-2026 target — PL chose not to raise even after a strong Q4. That likely means the target is being held pending H1FY27 confirmation, or the stock has caught up with fair value. Treat this note as confirmation the recovery is on track, and watch whether PL moves the number materially after Q1FY27.

ICICI|251117.change: Upgraded to Buy with PT ₹1,660 on 17-Nov-2025; no earlier ICICI Direct entry in the library to compare a prior call or target.
ICICI|251117.view:
The ICICI Direct upgrade at ₹1,660 is now ~9 months old and its target has been overtaken by PL's ₹1,800 and by the stock itself. The upgrade was most likely a catch-up call after IPCA had already shown early margin-recovery signs; the entry thesis — that IPCA looked cheap versus pharma peers at that level — has played out.

Without a fresh ICICI Direct note post-Q4FY26 this is a directional signal, not a live price target. Treat as stale.

MO|241227.change: No pdfdata match; from trendlyne coverage history: PT raised ₹1,950→₹1,980 vs the MO upgrade-to-Buy note dated 14-Oct-2024; Buy maintained.
MO|241227.view:
Motilal Oswal's Dec-2024 note carries the highest target in the set (₹1,980) but is now ~20 months old — written before the FY26 margin recovery and well before the Q4FY26 data. The thesis pillars it cited — US scaling and outperformance of the Indian pharma market — have since been directionally validated, which is a mark in its favour, but the ₹1,980 target was set in a very different earnings and valuation context.

The token PT move (₹1,950→₹1,980) suggests MO was already near its then-fair-value estimate right after the October upgrade. Absent a post-FY26-results refresh, this note is mainly useful as historical context on how early MO backed the US ramp.

Sharekhan|241114.change: PT ₹1,765, Buy; dated Nov-2024, ~21 months old, with no earlier Sharekhan entry in the library to compare.
Sharekhan|241114.view: Sharekhan's Nov-2024 note predates the FY26 recovery and is badly stale. The two pillars it cited — US recovery and Unichem integration benefits — have since validated, and ₹1,765 was a reasonable target at the time. But there has been no Sharekhan refresh in the library since; treat this as an early-cycle conviction call that has largely run its course and adds little to the current risk/reward picture.

IRB Infrastructure.summary:
In scope there is now only **one** live house on IRB Infrastructure: **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, TP ₹52, Feb-2026), a note carried forward unchanged from MO's 14-Nov-2025 upgrade (Neutral→Buy). It is roughly seven months stale. The fresher PDF library shows two other constructive-but-more-sober views: **Kotak** (ADD, fair value ₹24, trimmed from ₹25, Jul-2026 after a strong 1QFY27) and **CLSA** (Outperform, TP ₹34.5, Aug-2026). Against a share price of roughly ₹20–₹23 (CLSA's 12-month range is ₹19.4–₹22.7), the targets fan out widely — ₹24 to ₹52 — but the direction is unanimous: all three are positive. The disagreement is about magnitude and what to capitalise. CLSA's bull case is that IRB's toll InvITs have matured into large dividend payers (₹1.33bn distribution in 1QFY27, up 72% YoY, driving PAT +51%) with 12–13% group toll growth and WPI-linked rate resets ahead. Kotak is constructive on the assets but keeps repeating that "sustained order wins remain key" and trimmed FY27–29 estimates, reflecting caution on TOT acquisition economics and interest cost. MO's ₹52 is the outlier and the least current.

My own read: IRB is the only private operator in India with real scale across both BOT and TOT road assets, which gives it genuine advantages in tender eligibility and O&M operating leverage, and the InvIT structure is now doing what it was designed to do — recycle capital and pay cash back. But the market pricing the stock below even Kotak's conservative ₹24 tells you where the doubt sits: project-level debt spread across SPVs, the risk that TOT-17/18 were won in a competitive window at prices that leave a thin margin of safety, and the government's uneven record on toll-rate revisions. The 1QFY27 PAT jump was flattered by InvIT distribution timing and a lower tax rate — not a clean margin re-rate. I'd anchor near Kotak/CLSA (₹24–₹35) and treat MO's ₹52 as an upside scenario conditional on TOT traffic ramping in line with underwriting and no dilutive equity raise. The single most important thing to watch is realised traffic on the newly acquired TOT bundles versus the assumptions baked into the acquisition price.

MO|260216.change: Dated Feb-2026; Buy and TP ₹52 maintained — unchanged from MO's 14-Nov-2025 upgrade note (Neutral→Buy, TP ₹50→₹52). No pdfdata entry for this report and no fresher MO note in the library to compare; now ~7 months stale.
MO|260216.view:
MO's ₹52 is now the high outlier — more than double Kotak's ₹24 fair value and roughly 2.3x the share price at publication — and the note pre-dates two quarters of results plus the recent TOT-17/18 wins. A gap that large over the market price usually means a NAV/sum-of-parts model that assigns generous option value to the pipeline and discounts long-duration toll cash flows at an aggressive rate. The structural logic is fine (inflation-linked toll resets, traffic compounding, scale efficiencies), but staleness is the problem here, not method.

Until MO refreshes, I'd treat ₹52 as a bull-case ceiling rather than a base case, and lean on the more current Kotak (₹24) and CLSA (₹34.5) marks. What would make MO's number credible: evidence that project-level SPV debt is on a clear downward path and that acquired TOT traffic is tracking at or above acquisition-time assumptions.

ITC.summary:
All five houses in scope pre-date the event that now defines ITC: the FY27 shift from GST compensation cess to a much higher excise regime on cigarettes (an effective step-up of roughly 50%). As a result the in-scope notes read as a bloc of caution rather than a genuine spread of opinion. **Prabhudas Lilladhar** is the outright bear (REDUCE/Sell, TP ₹302, May-2026), warning the "cigarette excise impact yet to play out." **Motilal Oswal** (Neutral, ₹400), **ICICI Direct** (Hold, ₹385) and **Axis Direct** (Hold, ₹380) all downgraded ITC in the first five days of Jan-2026 on the taxation overhang, clustering tightly at ₹380–₹400. **Deven Choksey** is the lone bull (Buy, TP ₹486, Nov-2025) but that note is ~10 months old and predates everything that matters. The ₹302–₹486 range is mostly vintage, not conviction. The fresher library (Aug-2026, post-Q1FY27) shows the debate has already moved on: after cigarette volumes fell only ~5% YoY versus the ~10%+ feared, **Nomura** upgraded to Buy (TP ₹300→₹340) and **Jefferies** upgraded to Buy (TP ₹350), while **Goldman Sachs** (₹320→₹290) and **JPMorgan** (₹325→₹310) cut targets and stayed Neutral, and **Kotak** held Buy (₹360, "valuations at trough," ~5% dividend yield). The real current question is the pace of cigarette EBIT recovery — Kotak models the YoY decline easing from ~35% in Q1FY27 to ~10% by Q4FY27 — and whether the 25–27% price hikes pass through without breaking volume.

My own read: ITC is a high-quality cash machine — the cigarette franchise still generates enormous free cash flow, funds a ~4–5% dividend yield, and the non-cigarette FMCG business has finally reached profitability scale. The sell-side's recurring blind spot is treating each tax shock as a one-off when cigarette taxation in India is a structural, ratcheting headwind: step-change in tax, volume dip, gradual price-led recovery, margin normalisation, repeat. The 2026 excise shift also inflates the reported cost base optically because excise is booked as a cost rather than netted from revenue. Where I'd land: closer to the constructive-but-not-euphoric camp (Kotak/Nomura) than to PL's Sell — at ~18x forward earnings the stock is priced for the bad news, and the ITC Hotels demerger has removed one leg of the conglomerate-discount argument. Two things I'd watch most: (1) cigarette volume elasticity to the cumulative price hikes over the next two to three quarters — resilience validates the recovery and keeps the illicit-trade risk contained; (2) the non-cigarette FMCG margin trajectory, which has to keep expanding to justify any re-rating. I'd discount the Jan-2026 Hold/Neutral cluster and DC's ₹486 as stale anchors.

PL|260521.change: Dated May-2026 (Q4FY26 result update); REDUCE / Sell, TP ₹302. No pdfdata entry for this note; trendlyne shows the Sell call and ₹302 target. No earlier PL note on ITC in the library to compare.
PL|260521.view:
PL's Sell was the most bearish call in scope and, in hindsight, the right near-term instinct — it explicitly warned the excise impact was "yet to play out," which it then did in Q1FY27 (cigarette EBIT down ~35% YoY). But the ₹302 target and Sell rating are now stale: the stock corrected sharply, volumes held better than feared, and peers began upgrading in August. The houseView paragraph is essentially just the headline, so there is little underlying analysis to weigh.

Unless PL refreshes with a similarly negative structural view post-results, treat this as a well-timed warning that has largely played out rather than a live call. If they publish a fuller post-Q1FY27 note it would be worth reading to see whether the bear case rests on lasting volume damage or just the transition optics.

Axis|260105.change: Downgraded to Hold from Buy (per trendlyne), TP ₹380, on 5-Jan-2026, on the cigarette-taxation overhang. Prior target not captured in the library; no post-Q1FY27 update.
Axis|260105.view: Axis's Jan-2026 cut to Hold was one of three near-simultaneous downgrades (with ICICI and MO in the same week) pre-positioning for the tax change. Directionally the caution was correct. But ₹380 is a pre-shock price anchor, roughly eight months old and pre-results, and now sits above where most post-Q1FY27 houses have landed (₹290–₹360). Its signal value today is limited to "cautious enough to drop Buy in January" — not an actionable level.

ICICI|260102.change: Downgraded to Hold from Buy (per trendlyne), TP ₹385, on 2-Jan-2026. Prior target not captured in the library; no post-Q1FY27 update.
ICICI|260102.view: Same read as the Axis note — part of the January-2026 downgrade cluster on the taxation risk, with the highest target of that group (₹385). Pre-shock, pre-results and now stale. The clustering of ICICI/Axis/MO tells you the sell-side broadly saw the tax hit coming; beyond that it adds no independent signal. A post-Q1FY27 refresh, if one appears, is the note worth reading.

MO|260101.change: Downgraded to Neutral, TP ₹400, on 1-Jan-2026, on the taxation overhang. No pdfdata entry and no earlier MO note on ITC in the library to compare; no post-Q1FY27 update.
MO|260101.view: MO's ₹400 was the top of the January-2026 downgrade cluster and the most optimistic of the cautious bloc. After Q1FY27, other houses' targets landed ₹290–₹360, so ₹400 now looks high and the note is stale. MO's Neutral framing — good franchise, upside capped by tax uncertainty — was reasonable then and arguably still describes the stock, but the number needs a full post-results update before it is usable.

DC|251106.change: Dated Nov-2025 (Q2FY26 update); Buy, TP ₹486. No pdfdata entry and no earlier Deven Choksey note on ITC in the library to compare; now ~10 months stale and pre-tax-shock.
DC|251106.view: Deven Choksey's ₹486 Buy is the lone bull in scope but predates the excise shift, the price correction and the FY27 reset entirely — it is not a usable current reference. The observation in the note (steady FMCG growth offsetting agri and margin drag) is a fair description of the non-cigarette story, but the target belongs to a different tax regime and should be treated as a stale anchor.

ITC Hotels.summary:
**Jefferies** is the only broker covering ITC Hotels in our library, maintaining a Buy at ₹205 PT after a marginal cut from ₹210 following weak Q4FY26 results. The weakness was driven by Foreign Tourist Arrival (FTA) disruptions affecting South India assets in March; 1QFY27 is expected to recover. There is no cross-house debate in our data — coverage is thin, reflecting ITC Hotels' recent demerger status.

**My own read:** ITC Hotels owns some of India's most irreplaceable hospitality assets — the Maurya (Delhi), Rajputana (Jaipur), Grand Chola (Chennai), Sonar (Kolkata). The FTA disruption is transitory; the structural thesis is owned-RevPAR recovery as international travel normalises. The FY26 demerger from ITC Ltd means institutional coverage is still building — the relatively thin sell-side base is itself an opportunity. The Sri Lanka hotel improving occupancy and the new 72-key Kerala acquisition are early signs of post-demerger capital deployment. Key watches: (1) owned RevPAR trajectory as FTA normalises in 2QFY27, (2) capex discipline — the company must demonstrate it can grow without destroying returns, and (3) whether an asset-light layer develops over time. At ₹205, Jefferies calls valuations reasonable; I'd agree the franchise quality justifies a premium, but the light coverage means price discovery is incomplete.

Jeff|260517.change: PT lowered ₹210→₹205; Buy maintained. Weak Q4FY26 (3% owned RevPAR growth, negative operating leverage) due to FTA disruption in South India; FY27 capex estimate raised for Kerala acquisition.
Jeff|260517.view:
Jefferies is constructive on the quality of the franchise and sees the FTA impact as transitory — 1QFY27 should improve and the Sri Lanka hotel is gaining occupancy. The marginal PT cut is pragmatic rather than a change in thesis; the Buy is maintained on what the note describes as reasonable valuations.

The call is credible. Jefferies is the most active institutional voice in Indian hospitality, and this is an initiating-style note on a freshly demerged company. I'd stress-test the 'reasonable valuations' claim — ITC Hotels' owned-asset model carries higher depreciation/capex than asset-light peers, which compresses FCF. Watch whether Jefferies revisits the PT upward once FTA data normalises, and monitor the Kerala acquisition's economics on disclosure.

Indian Hotels.summary:
Only two houses sit in our **Indian Hotels** houseViews and both are bullish but dated: **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, TP ₹900, Feb-2026) on 'diversification and scale', and **ICICI Securities** (Buy, TP ₹941, Jul-2025) on resilient demand. Neither has an earlier report in our library to compare against, and neither has been refreshed through the strong 1QFY27 results season. There is no bear in our set. For context, the broader street re-rated IHCL through Jul–Aug 2026: post-1QFY27, Jefferies moved to ₹875 (Buy), Goldman Sachs ₹850 (Buy), JPMorgan ₹858 (OW) and Nomura ₹830 (Buy), while the cautious end is now **Kotak** (Add, ₹780) and **Morgan Stanley** (Equal-weight, ~₹783–793). So the live debate is multiple, not direction: our two (dated) houseView targets of ₹900–₹941 actually sit *above* the current post-results street cluster of ₹830–₹875, so the question is whether that early-2026 optimism or the more measured current consensus is right, and how the Oriental Hotels / associate-company merger (announced Aug-2026) should be valued.

**My own read:** the Taj franchise is the best luxury hospitality brand in India, with genuine pricing power in gateway cities, and the asset-light management-contract pipeline plus Ginger give it growth runways most Indian peers lack — 1QFY27's mid-teens RevPAR growth and margin expansion validated the model. The risk the sell-side underweights is valuation: IHCL trades well above global hospitality comps, so the stock is priced for sustained double-digit RevPAR and clean execution against a wave of new luxury supply. I'd treat our two houseView targets (₹900/₹941) as un-refreshed rather than directionally wrong — they pre-date both the March FY26 FTA-disruption scare and the FY27 recovery, and now sit above a street that has settled at ₹830–₹875. I'd anchor to that ₹830–₹875 cluster and keep Morgan Stanley's EW (~₹783–793) as the valuation-discipline counterweight. Watch: (1) whether metro RevPAR growth holds above high-single-digits as new Marriott/Hilton luxury rooms land; (2) Ginger unit economics and group ROCE; (3) the terms and dilution of the Oriental/associate mergers; (4) capex intensity versus the asset-light narrative.

MO|260212.change: Trendlyne: Buy, TP ₹900 (Feb-2026). No earlier Motilal Oswal report in the library, so no prior rating/PT delta to state. Not refreshed through 1QFY27 results.
MO|260212.view:
The 'diversification and scale' thesis is sound and still intact — multi-brand (Taj, Vivanta, SeleQtions, Ginger) plus a growing management-fee book is exactly what insulates IHCL from any single-segment air pocket.

The ₹900 target hasn't been re-underwritten against the actual June-quarter numbers; it now sits above where the freshest bulls have landed (Jefferies ₹875, JPMorgan ₹858, Goldman ₹850), which suggests the early-2026 model was a touch rich or the target multiple has since compressed. Directionally still fine; treat the specific number as needing a refresh.

ICICI|250718.change: Trendlyne: Buy, TP ₹941 (Jul-2025); the only ICICI entry in the library, so no prior to compare. ~14 months stale — pre-dates the FY26 disruption and the FY27 recovery.
ICICI|250718.view: 'Resilience amid turbulence' was written in July 2025, before the FY26 demand air pocket and the FY27 rebound — it is the stalest view in our coverage by a wide margin. TP ₹941 is the highest number in the set but is over a year old and not actionable as a current estimate. The bullish direction has aged well; the magnitude is unreliable.

Indian Oil Corporation.summary:
Within our houseViews IOCL is split and mostly stale. The three current voices are all post-4QFY26 (May-2026): **Geojit** downgraded to **Hold** (₹153, from Buy/₹179 in Jan-2026); **BOB Capital** went the other way, **upgrading to Buy** (₹173, trimmed from ₹181) on a 'de-rated enough to own' basis; and **Prabhudas Lilladhar** kept **Accumulate** (₹145, cut from ₹152), explicitly flagging a strong Q4 but a 'challenging' Q1FY27. The other three are old and no longer actionable: **ICICI Securities** Buy ₹170 (a Sep-2025 management-meet note), **Motilal Oswal** Neutral ₹150 (its Aug-2025 downgrade) and **Emkay** Buy ₹160 (Jan-2025). So the only live disagreement in the set is Geojit's Hold versus BOB's Buy — barely ₹20 apart around a ~₹135–150 stock, with PL sitting between them. The 4QFY26 beat (PAT roughly +57% YoY) was universally read as inventory / adventitious-gain driven; the real question is how deep 1HFY27 losses run given negative petrol/diesel marketing margins.

**My own read:** the wider street is far more polarised than our set — 1QFY27 (reported Aug-2026) came in with a narrower-than-feared net loss and even marginally positive EBITDA on a ~$36/bbl GRM, which pushed Jefferies and Nomura to Buy/₹180 and JPMorgan to OW/₹170, while Kotak stayed Reduce/₹150 and Goldman Sachs sits at Sell/₹105. That ₹105–₹180 spread tells you the fundamentals are genuinely hard to underwrite. The swing variable is government fuel-pricing policy, not the refining cycle or capacity timelines, and it is politically constrained. IOCL's decision to stop disclosing the GRM / inventory-gain split is a real governance mark against the bull case. The refining/petchem expansion is a genuine medium-term lever, but the earnings benefit is largely a 2028 story already embedded in the bull models. At ~₹140 with a likely loss-making first half and thin disclosure, I lean to the Hold/Neutral camp over the buyers. Watchpoints: any fuel-price-hike announcement, 2QFY27 results, the crude import-premium trajectory, and the rupee.

Geojit|260525.change: Downgraded Buy→Hold; PT ₹179→₹153 (vs Geojit's Jan-2026 upgrade note in trendlyne). No pdfdata match for this report.
Geojit|260525.view: Geojit's IOCL calls have trailed the tape: an upgrade to Buy at ₹179 in Jan-2026 near the highs, then down to Hold at ₹153 in May once 4QFY26 conditions had already turned. Hold at ₹153 against a ~₹135–150 stock is at least honest about the lack of near-term catalysts, but I would read it as a following indicator, not a leading one.

PL|260520.change: Accumulate maintained; PT ₹152→₹145 (vs PL's Aug-2025 note in trendlyne, Accumulate/₹152). No pdfdata match for this report.
PL|260520.view: PL's own headline says it: 'strong Q4 beat; Q1FY27 to remain challenging.' The rating hasn't followed that logic — Accumulate at ₹145 implies only mid-single-digit upside on a stock facing a likely loss-making first half, so it reads more as a value-watch than genuine conviction. Useful mainly as confirmation that even the moderates have trimmed.

BOB|260519.change: Upgraded Hold→Buy; PT ₹181→₹173 (vs BOB's Feb-2026 note in trendlyne, Hold/₹181). No pdfdata match for this report.
BOB|260519.view: The simultaneous upgrade and target cut is a 'de-rated enough to own' call driven by price action rather than any fundamental upgrade — BOB itself carried a Sell on IOCL as recently as Aug-2024. Mechanically defensible after a ~25% drawdown, but there is no differentiated thesis here; it adds to the bull headcount without adding to the bull case's quality.

ICICI|250928.change: Trendlyne: Buy, TP ₹170 (Sep-2025 management-meet note); the only ICICI entry in the library, no prior to compare. Pre-dates both 4QFY26 and 1QFY27 — ~11 months stale.
ICICI|250928.view: A management-access note relaying the new Chairman's growth vision — refining and petchem expansion, city gas, green hydrogen. Useful medium-term colour on the capex story, but as a live call the ₹170 Buy is stale: it was set before two quarters of results and before marketing margins turned sharply negative. The structural growth narrative is real but distant (benefits ~2028); discount the target.

MO|250818.change: This entry is itself Motilal Oswal's downgrade to Neutral (PT ₹150), Aug-2025; no earlier MO report in the library to compare the prior rating/PT. ~13 months stale.
MO|250818.view: MO's move to Neutral at ₹150 over a year ago now looks prescient — it flagged the marketing-margin squeeze early. But the note is old enough that the specific ₹150 target carries no information today; several fresher houses have since converged near that level anyway. Keep the directional caution, ignore the number.

Emkay|250128.change: Trendlyne: Buy, TP ₹160 (Jan-2025); the only Emkay entry in the library, no prior to compare. ~19 months stale — the oldest view in our coverage.
Emkay|250128.view: A Q3FY25 results note whose own title ('inventory loss and marketing weakness drag earnings') describes the exact problem that has dogged the stock ever since. The Buy/₹160 is far too old to act on. Interesting only as a marker of how long the marketing-margin issue has been visible and still unresolved.

Indigo Paints.summary:
The **Indigo Paints** coverage set has a severe staleness problem. The only fresh view is **Kotak**'s Reduce (PT ₹900, May-2026) following 4QFY26 results — a Reduce but with PT raised from ₹850, as decorative growth of 8.5% YoY was marginally better than feared. The bulls — **ICICI** (Buy, PT ₹1200, Feb-2026) and **Motilal Oswal** (Buy, PT ₹1400, Nov-2025) — are 4–7 months old and built on a recovery thesis that Kotak's fresher data does not confirm. **Asit** (Hold, PT ₹1710, Nov-2024) and **Keynote** (Neutral/downgrade, PT ₹1457, Aug-2024) are 19–22 months old and can be disregarded for current analysis. The central debate — between Kotak's Reduce at ₹900 and ICICI/MO's stale Buys at ₹1200–₹1400 — hinges on whether Indigo can re-accelerate to its stated 1.5–2× industry growth, something it has not delivered in recent quarters. Kotak's core critique: 8.5% decorative growth is "a tad better than peers" but well below Indigo's own target; EBITDA margin flat at 22.5% despite 180bp of gross margin expansion, fully offset by sales-force and A&P investment.

My own read: Indigo is a quality franchise that has lost its growth-premium narrative. The differentiated product moat — Dirtproof, Bright Ceiling, Floor-Guard, Apple Chemie — is real but not wide enough to consistently outgrow Asian Paints, Berger, and Kansai in a price-competitive decorative market. The EBITDA margin story tells it plainly: the company is reinvesting the entire input-cost tailwind into distribution and branding — necessary, but not yet converting to sustained volume acceleration. Apple Chemie (industrial/construction chemicals), which ICICI highlights as a bull driver, is genuinely interesting — less commoditised, better pricing power — but currently too small to move consolidated results. Kotak's ₹900 Reduce implies the market is right to reprice away from a "premium-growth" multiple toward an "in-line growth at a discount" multiple, and I agree with that framework. Until Indigo demonstrates two consecutive quarters of 1.5×+ industry growth, the re-rating story is on hold. Key watchpoints: (1) quarterly decorative volume growth vs peers; (2) Apple Chemie revenue disclosed separately and growing meaningfully.

Kotak|260526.view: Kotak's Reduce with a raised PT is a grudging acknowledgment that 4QFY26 was marginally less bad than feared — 8.5% decorative growth was "a tad better than peers." But the core critique is intact: Indigo has positioned itself as a 1.5–2× industry grower, and barely matching industry pace means the premium multiple is unjustified. The structural concern is the EBITDA margin: 180bp of GM expansion fully offset by opex investment shows the growth machine is still burning fuel to maintain speed rather than accelerating. The Reduce at a PT only modestly above (or at) CMP signals Kotak sees better value elsewhere in the consumer space. This is the most credible and current view in the set, and I weight it accordingly.

ICICI|260215.change: Buy (upgraded at some point vs Hold in May-2024 prior); PT ₹1380→₹1200. No pdfdata match; no intermediate ICICI entry in library between May-2024 and Feb-2026.
ICICI|260215.view: ICICI's Feb-2026 Buy at ₹1200 is primarily anchored to Apple Chemie's strong performance and broader market-share gains. The PT cut from ₹1380 to ₹1200 reflects lower estimates after the stock's significant decline — a "fallen enough to own" call. ICICI's track record on this name has been inconsistent (Sell in 2023, Hold in 2024, Buy in 2026), which tempers conviction. At ~4 months old, this note predates Kotak's May-2026 data showing growth in line with — not ahead of — peers. I would want an updated ICICI note post-4QFY26 results before treating the ₹1200 Buy as actionable.

MO|251108.change: Buy maintained; PT ₹1400 unchanged (vs Aug-2025 prior in trendlyne).
MO|251108.view: MO's Nov-2025 Buy at ₹1400 is ~7 months old and the "recovery momentum building, positive 2H outlook" thesis has not been vindicated by Kotak's May-2026 data. The ₹1400 target looks very stretched against Kotak's current Reduce at ₹900. An unchanged PT from Aug-2025 suggests the model has not been refreshed since then. Treat this as a historical data point only; the investment case needs MO's post-4QFY26 update, which is not available in the library.

Asit|241113.change: Dated Nov-2024; no prior Asit entry in library to compare.
Asit|241113.view: Asit's Hold at ₹1710 from November 2024 is nearly 20 months old and has no actionable bearing on current analysis. The ₹1710 target vs Kotak's current Reduce at ₹900 shows how dramatically estimates have been revised since then. The "muted industry dynamics, relative outperformance continued" framing has been overtaken by subsequent data showing that relative outperformance has largely evaporated. Discard for current purposes.

Keynote|240812.change: Dated Aug-2024; no prior Keynote entry in library to compare.
Keynote|240812.view: Keynote's Aug-2024 downgrade to Neutral at ₹1457 was timely relative to the subsequent stock decline. At 22 months old, this view is entirely stale — ₹1457 Neutral bears no relation to the current debate between Kotak's ₹900 Reduce and ICICI's ₹1200 Buy. Useful only as a historical footnote showing the cautious turn began well before the current level.

Indraprastha Gas.summary:
**JPMorgan** is the lone bear at UW (PT ₹120, cut from ₹125), citing sequential gross-margin compression to ₹10.9/SCM, a weak gas-purchase mix shift, and a 21% YoY PAT decline in 4QFY26. All other houses are constructive: **CLSA** (O-PF, PT ₹210 cut from ₹240) and **Nomura** (BUY, PT ₹200, first captured report) anchor the bull camp; **Jefferies** is BUY at ₹180 (cut from ₹205); **BOB Capital** BUY at ₹184 (cut from ₹197); **Prabhudas Lilladhar** Accumulate at ₹191 (upgraded from Sell in Feb 2026). **Kotak** is the dissenting local at REDUCE/₹160 — a fresh initiation, the lowest non-JP PT — while **Geojit** sits at Hold/₹173 (upgraded from Sell in Mar 2026). Target spread is wide: ₹120–₹210. CLSA explicitly models margins “much lower than guided,” and Jefferies uses a conservative 5% volume CAGR, so even the bulls embed a discount to management’s double-digit volume + ₹7–8/scm EBITDA guidance. The real debate is whether the CNG-bus retirement drag in Delhi is truly behind and whether APM gas input costs have bottomed.

My own read: IGL has genuine toll-road quality — near-monopoly CGA in Delhi NCR, decades of PNG conversion runway, sticky industrial and commercial volumes. The franchise is not in dispute; the margin structure is. The core risk is that IGL sits downstream of an opaque APM gas allocation policy: if the government trims allocations or prices market gas higher, ₹7–8/scm EBITDA/scm is aspirational, not structural. JPMorgan’s ₹120 looks too punitive — it doesn’t credit the franchise or any recovery — but Kotak’s REDUCE at ₹160 is the right discipline check. I’d be closest to Jefferies (BUY, ₹180) with the caveat that the PT is conditional on FY27 volume recovering as the Delhi bus fleet transitions. The two things I’d watch: (1) APM gas allocation volumes and whether IGL’s share shrinks further in FY27; (2) CNG retail volume momentum in 1QFY27 — the first clean quarter post-bus retirement.

CLSA|260520.change: PT lowered ₹240→₹210; O-PF (Outperform) maintained. FY27/28 EPS cut 14%/9%.
CLSA|260520.view: CLSA is the highest-PT bull but is trimming estimates aggressively, acknowledging that 4QFY26’s 34% PAT beat was real but driven partly by better-than-modelled margins — not a run-rate base. Their most important signal is the explicit statement that they model “much lower than guided” on both margins and volume growth. That is a credible research stance: management’s ₹7–8/scm target is medium-term, not near-term deliverable. The ₹210 PT (even after the cut) implies CLSA is buying the franchise at a discount, expecting eventual margin normalisation. Reasonable, but the downside scenario — a sustained APM gas cost headwind — is not fully reflected even at ₹210. The O-PF is a comfortable hold, not a high-conviction buy.

JP|260520.view: JP is the structural bear, and their thesis — sequential margin compression, gas-mix headwinds, INR pressure — is factually grounded in 4Q data. But ₹120 as fair value goes well beyond a near-term margin dip: it implies permanent impairment of the franchise. For a CGD monopoly with mandated geographic exclusivity, that seems too aggressive. JP is right to flag the ₹11.1→₹10.9/SCM gross-margin compression and the HH gas mix shift, but their PT appears to embed both sustained cost escalation and zero pricing power recovery. Use JP’s note to stress-test margin assumptions, not to set a price target.

Nomura|260520.change: First captured Nomura report on IGL (prevTP null, no prior to compare); PT ₹200, BUY.
Nomura|260520.view: Nomura enters with BUY/₹200 — close to CLSA — acknowledging a 3% EBITDA miss vs their forecast but a 5% consensus beat. Their cost concerns (staff 11% above estimate, raw material 5% above) are consistent with the broader picture. The report title “volume may surprise” signals they see upside optionality in volume recovery. At ₹200, Nomura is broadly aligned with the bull camp on franchise value. As a first-captured report there is no track record to judge how responsive their estimates are to misses; the ₹200 target may be more of an initiation anchor than a conviction level.

Jeff|260519.view: Jefferies shows measured discipline: they cut the PT ~12% while holding BUY, and their 5% volume CAGR assumption (FY26–28E) is deliberately below management’s double-digit guidance. The key call is that the CNG-bus retirement drag in Delhi is now behind — which, if correct, turns FY27 into a cleaner volume recovery year. The ₹180 target is the most conservative among the BUY camp, making it the most credible entry point. The PT trim is a proper acknowledgment that prior estimates had been too optimistic. This is one of the more trustworthy notes in the set.

Kotak|260519.change: First captured Kotak report on IGL (prevCall null, no prior to compare); PT ₹160, REDUCE initiated.
Kotak|260519.view: Kotak’s REDUCE at ₹160 is the most bearish domestic call. Despite acknowledging the 4Q EBITDA beat (10.5% above their estimate), the 15.4% QoQ EBITDA decline and EBITDA/scm compression to ₹4.9 dominate their assessment. The report title “CNG price increases getting easier” hints that Kotak’s upgrade scenario requires retail tariff hikes that are not yet certain. A REDUCE with the stock likely 10–20% above ₹160 is a contrarian call that will be validated or disproven quickly in 1QFY27. Worth watching whether Kotak revises upward after any CNG price hike.

BOB|260519.change: PT cut ₹197→₹184 (based on trendlyne history; Feb 2026 BOB entry had PT ₹197); BUY maintained.
BOB|260519.view: BOB Capital’s BUY at ₹184 is a middle-ground call — acknowledging the operational miss on higher costs while keeping faith in the recovery thesis. The ₹184 PT clusters with the cautious-but-constructive camp (PL Accumulate ₹191, Geojit Hold ₹173). This is a trendlyne-sourced external call; without the full report it is harder to assess the rigour of the estimate revision. Take the PT cut as a directional signal rather than a precise valuation update.

Geojit|260306.change: Upgraded to Hold from Sell (prior May 2025 Geojit entry: Sell, PT ₹191); PT lowered to ₹173. Dated Mar 2026 — predates 4QFY26 results.
Geojit|260306.view: Geojit’s upgrade from Sell to Hold at ₹173 in March 2026 reflects acknowledgment that the worst of the sell-off had passed, but not conviction in a recovery. The PT cut to ₹173 (from prior ₹191) is a further downgrade of the absolute valuation even as the rating improved — a cautious stance. This is a 3-month old note, pre-dating 4QFY26 results; Geojit has not yet updated in the library. Treat as a “monitoring/neutral” signal until a post-earnings update appears.

PL|260214.change: Upgraded to Accumulate from Sell (prior Apr 2025 PL entry: Sell, PT ₹150); PT ₹191 at time of upgrade. Dated Feb 2026 — predates 4QFY26 results.
PL|260214.view: PL’s upgrade from Sell to Accumulate in Feb 2026 (Q3FY26 result note) was a significant shift from a very bearish prior stance. The upgrade to Accumulate at ₹191 signals PL saw Q3FY26 volume trajectory as the inflection point. But this is a 4-month old note predating the May 2026 quarterly results; no updated PL entry is in the library. The Accumulate stance may be stale — treat with caution until a post-Q4 update appears.
